**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  Global bulk change [permission](https://support.atlassian.com/jira-cloud-administration/docs/manage-global-permissions/).
 *  Browse [project permission](https://support.atlassian.com/jira-cloud-administration/docs/manage-project-permissions/) in all projects that contain the selected issues.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "selectedIssueIdsOrKeys": [
    "10001",
    "10002"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-watch-issues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IssueBulkWatchOrUnwatchPayload](#schemaissuebulkwatchorunwatchpayload)|true|The request body containing the issues to be watched.|
|» selectedIssueIdsOrKeys|body|[string]|true|List of issue IDs or keys which are to be bulk watched or unwatched. These IDs or keys can be from different projects and issue types.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
"{\"taskId\":\"10641\"}"
```

> 400 Response

```json
"{\"errors\":[{\"message\":\"Some of the issues in the issueIdsOrKeys are not valid\"}]}"
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-watch-issues-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returned if the request is successful.|[SubmittedBulkOperation](#schemasubmittedbulkoperation)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|[BulkOperationErrorResponse](#schemabulkoperationerrorresponse)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|[BulkOperationErrorResponse](#schemabulkoperationerrorresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|[BulkOperationErrorResponse](#schemabulkoperationerrorresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: write:jira-work )
</aside>

## Get bulk issue operation progress

<a id="opIdgetBulkOperationProgress"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/bulk/queue/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/bulk/queue/{taskId}`

Use this to get the progress state for the specified bulk operation `taskId`.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  Global bulk change [permission](https://support.atlassian.com/jira-cloud-administration/docs/manage-global-permissions/).

If the task is running, this resource will return:

    {"taskId":"10779","status":"RUNNING","progressPercent":65,"submittedBy":{"accountId":"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g"},"created":1690180055963,"started":1690180056206,"updated":169018005829}

If the task has completed, then this resource will return:

    {"processedAccessibleIssues":[10001,10002],"created":1709189449954,"progressPercent":100,"started":1709189450154,"status":"COMPLETE","submittedBy":{"accountId":"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g"},"invalidOrInaccessibleIssueCount":0,"taskId":"10000","totalIssueCount":2,"updated":1709189450354}

**Note:** You can view task progress for up to 14 days from creation.

<h3 id="get-bulk-issue-operation-progress-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|taskId|path|string|true|The ID of the task.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"created\":1704110400000,\"invalidOrInaccessibleIssueCount\":0,\"processedAccessibleIssues\":[10001,10002],\"progressPercent\":100,\"started\":1704110460000,\"status\":\"COMPLETE\",\"submittedBy\":{\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\"},\"taskId\":\"10000\",\"totalIssueCount\":2,\"updated\":1704110520000}"
```

> 400 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"The task associated with this taskId is not a bulk operation task\"],\"errors\":{},\"httpStatusCode\":{\"empty\":false,\"present\":true}}"
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-bulk-issue-operation-progress-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[BulkOperationProgress](#schemabulkoperationprogress)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|[BulkOperationErrorResponse](#schemabulkoperationerrorresponse)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|[BulkOperationErrorResponse](#schemabulkoperationerrorresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-comment-properties">Issue comment properties</h1>

This resource represents [issue comment](#api-group-Issue-comments) properties, which provides for storing custom data against an issue comment. Use is to get, set, and delete issue comment properties as well as obtain the keys of all properties on a comment. Comment properties are a type of [entity property](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/jira-entity-properties/).

## Get comment property keys

<a id="opIdgetCommentPropertyKeys"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/comment/string/properties \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/comment/{commentId}/properties`

Returns the keys of all the properties of a comment.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  If the comment has visibility restrictions, belongs to the group or has the role visibility is restricted to.

<h3 id="get-comment-property-keys-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|commentId|path|string|true|The ID of the comment.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"keys\":[{\"key\":\"issue.support\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/EX-2/properties/issue.support\"}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-comment-property-keys-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PropertyKeys](#schemapropertykeys)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the comment ID is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the comment is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Get comment property

<a id="opIdgetCommentProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/comment/string/properties/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/comment/{commentId}/properties/{propertyKey}`

Returns the value of a comment property.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  If the comment has visibility restrictions, belongs to the group or has the role visibility is restricted to.

<h3 id="get-comment-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|commentId|path|string|true|The ID of the comment.|
|propertyKey|path|string|true|The key of the property.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"key\":\"issue.support\",\"value\":{\"system.conversation.id\":\"b1bf38be-5e94-4b40-a3b8-9278735ee1e6\",\"system.support.time\":\"1m\"}}"
```

<h3 id="get-comment-property-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[EntityProperty](#schemaentityproperty)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the comment or the property is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Set comment property

<a id="opIdsetCommentProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/comment/string/properties/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'null'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/comment/{commentId}/properties/{propertyKey}`

Creates or updates the value of a property for a comment. Use this resource to store custom data against a comment.

The value of the request body must be a [valid](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4627), non-empty JSON blob. The maximum length is 32768 characters.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** either of:

 *  *Edit All Comments* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) to create or update the value of a property on any comment.
 *  *Edit Own Comments* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) to create or update the value of a property on a comment created by the user.

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="set-comment-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|commentId|path|string|true|The ID of the comment.|
|propertyKey|path|string|true|The key of the property. The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|body|body|object|true|The value of the property. The value has to be a valid, non-empty [JSON](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4627) value. The maximum length of the property value is 32768 bytes.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
null
```

> 201 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="set-comment-property-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the comment property is updated.|Inline|
|201|Created|Returned if the comment property is created.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the comment is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: write:jira-work )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-comments">Issue comments</h1>

This resource represents issue comments. Use it to:

 *  get, create, update, and delete a comment from an issue.
 *  get all comments from issue.
 *  get a list of comments by comment ID.

## Get comments by IDs

<a id="opIdgetCommentsByIds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/comment/list \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "ids": [
      1,
      2,
      5,
      10
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/comment/list`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of comments specified by a list of comment IDs.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Comments are returned where the user:

 *  has *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project containing the comment.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  If the comment has visibility restrictions, belongs to the group or has the role visibility is restricted to.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ids": [
    1,
    2,
    5,
    10
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-comments-by-ids-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information about comments in the response. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `renderedBody` Returns the comment body rendered in HTML.<br> *  `properties` Returns the comment's properties.|
|body|body|[IssueCommentListRequestBean](#schemaissuecommentlistrequestbean)|true|The list of comment IDs.|
|» ids|body|[integer(int64)]|true|The list of comment IDs. A maximum of 1000 IDs can be specified.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"isLast\":true,\"maxResults\":1048576,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":1,\"values\":[{\"author\":{\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"active\":false,\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/user?accountId=5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\"},\"body\":{\"type\":\"doc\",\"version\":1,\"content\":[{\"type\":\"paragraph\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Pellentesque eget venenatis elit. Duis eu justo eget augue iaculis fermentum. Sed semper quam laoreet nisi egestas at posuere augue semper.\"}]}]},\"created\":\"2021-01-17T12:34:00.000+0000\",\"id\":\"10000\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/10010/comment/10000\",\"updateAuthor\":{\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"active\":false,\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/user?accountId=5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\"},\"updated\":\"2021-01-18T23:45:00.000+0000\",\"visibility\":{\"identifier\":\"Administrators\",\"type\":\"role\",\"value\":\"Administrators\"}}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-comments-by-ids-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PageBeanComment](#schemapagebeancomment)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request contains more than 1000 IDs or is empty.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Get comments

<a id="opIdgetComments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/string/comment \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/comment`

Returns all comments for an issue.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Comments are included in the response where the user has:

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project containing the comment.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  If the comment has visibility restrictions, belongs to the group or has the role visibility is role visibility is restricted to.

<h3 id="get-comments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|orderBy|query|string|false|[Order](#ordering) the results by a field. Accepts *created* to sort comments by their created date.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information about comments in the response. This parameter accepts `renderedBody`, which returns the comment body rendered in HTML.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|orderBy|created|
|orderBy|-created|
|orderBy|+created|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"comments\":[{\"author\":{\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"active\":false,\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/user?accountId=5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\"},\"body\":{\"type\":\"doc\",\"version\":1,\"content\":[{\"type\":\"paragraph\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Pellentesque eget venenatis elit. Duis eu justo eget augue iaculis fermentum. Sed semper quam laoreet nisi egestas at posuere augue semper.\"}]}]},\"created\":\"2021-01-17T12:34:00.000+0000\",\"id\":\"10000\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/10010/comment/10000\",\"updateAuthor\":{\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"active\":false,\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/user?accountId=5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\"},\"updated\":\"2021-01-18T23:45:00.000+0000\",\"visibility\":{\"identifier\":\"Administrators\",\"type\":\"role\",\"value\":\"Administrators\"}}],\"maxResults\":1,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":1}"
```

<h3 id="get-comments-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PageOfComments](#schemapageofcomments)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if `orderBy` is set to a value other than *created*.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the issue is not found or the user does not have permission to view it.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Add comment

<a id="opIdaddComment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/string/comment \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "body": {
      "content": [
        {
          "content": [
            {
              "text": "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Pellentesque eget venenatis elit. Duis eu justo eget augue iaculis fermentum. Sed semper quam laoreet nisi egestas at posuere augue semper.",
              "type": "text"
            }
          ],
          "type": "paragraph"
        }
      ],
      "type": "doc",
      "version": 1
    },
    "visibility": {
      "identifier": "Administrators",
      "type": "role",
      "value": "Administrators"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/comment`

Adds a comment to an issue.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* and *Add comments* [ project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue containing the comment is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "body": {
    "content": [
      {
        "content": [
          {
            "text": "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Pellentesque eget venenatis elit. Duis eu justo eget augue iaculis fermentum. Sed semper quam laoreet nisi egestas at posuere augue semper.",
            "type": "text"
          }
        ],
        "type": "paragraph"
      }
    ],
    "type": "doc",
    "version": 1
  },
  "visibility": {
    "identifier": "Administrators",
    "type": "role",
    "value": "Administrators"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="add-comment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information about comments in the response. This parameter accepts `renderedBody`, which returns the comment body rendered in HTML.|
|body|body|[Comment](#schemacomment)|true|none|
|» body|body|object|false|The comment text in [Atlassian Document Format](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/apis/document/structure/).|
|» properties|body|[[EntityProperty](#schemaentityproperty)]|false|A list of comment properties. Optional on create and update.|
|» visibility|body|object|false|The group or role to which this comment is visible. Optional on create and update.|
|» » identifier|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the group or the name of the role that visibility of this item is restricted to.|
|» » type|body|string|false|Whether visibility of this item is restricted to a group or role.|
|» » value|body|string|false|The name of the group or role that visibility of this item is restricted to. Please note that the name of a group is mutable, to reliably identify a group use `identifier`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|group|
|» » type|role|

> 201 Response

```json
"{\"author\":{\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"active\":false,\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/user?accountId=5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\"},\"body\":{\"type\":\"doc\",\"version\":1,\"content\":[{\"type\":\"paragraph\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Pellentesque eget venenatis elit. Duis eu justo eget augue iaculis fermentum. Sed semper quam laoreet nisi egestas at posuere augue semper.\"}]}]},\"created\":\"2021-01-17T12:34:00.000+0000\",\"id\":\"10000\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/10010/comment/10000\",\"updateAuthor\":{\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"active\":false,\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/user?accountId=5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\"},\"updated\":\"2021-01-18T23:45:00.000+0000\",\"visibility\":{\"identifier\":\"Administrators\",\"type\":\"role\",\"value\":\"Administrators\"}}"
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returned if the request is successful.|[Comment](#schemacomment)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|

## Get comment

<a id="opIdgetComment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/string/comment/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/comment/{id}`

Returns a comment.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project containing the comment.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  If the comment has visibility restrictions, the user belongs to the group or has the role visibility is restricted to.

|id|path|string|true|The ID of the comment.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information about comments in the response. This parameter accepts `renderedBody`, which returns the comment body rendered in HTML.|

`PUT /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/comment/{id}`

Updates a comment.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue containing the comment is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  *Edit all comments*[ project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) to update any comment or *Edit own comments* to update comment created by the user.
 *  If the comment has visibility restrictions, the user belongs to the group or has the role visibility is restricted to.

**WARNING:** Child comments inherit visibility from their parent comment. Attempting to update a child comment's visibility will result in a 400 (Bad Request) error.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "body": {
    "content": [
      {
        "content": [
          {
            "text": "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Pellentesque eget venenatis elit. Duis eu justo eget augue iaculis fermentum. Sed semper quam laoreet nisi egestas at posuere augue semper.",
            "type": "text"
          }
        ],
        "type": "paragraph"
      }
    ],
    "type": "doc",
    "version": 1
  },
  "visibility": {
    "identifier": "Administrators",
    "type": "role",
    "value": "Administrators"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-comment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|notifyUsers|query|boolean|false|Whether users are notified when a comment is updated.|
|overrideEditableFlag|query|boolean|false|Whether screen security is overridden to enable uneditable fields to be edited. Available to Connect app users with the *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg) and Forge apps acting on behalf of users with *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information about comments in the response. This parameter accepts `renderedBody`, which returns the comment body rendered in HTML.|
|body|body|[Comment](#schemacomment)|true|none|
|» body|body|object|false|The comment text in [Atlassian Document Format](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/apis/document/structure/).|
|» properties|body|[[EntityProperty](#schemaentityproperty)]|false|A list of comment properties. Optional on create and update.|
|» visibility|body|object|false|The group or role to which this comment is visible. Optional on create and update.|
|» » identifier|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the group or the name of the role that visibility of this item is restricted to.|
|» » type|body|string|false|Whether visibility of this item is restricted to a group or role.|
|» » value|body|string|false|The name of the group or role that visibility of this item is restricted to. Please note that the name of a group is mutable, to reliably identify a group use `identifier`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|» » type|role|

Sed semper quam laoreet nisi egestas at posuere augue semper.\"}]}]},\"created\":\"2021-01-17T12:34:00.000+0000\",\"id\":\"10000\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/10010/comment/10000\",\"updateAuthor\":{\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"active\":false,\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/user?accountId=5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\"},\"updated\":\"2021-01-18T23:45:00.000+0000\",\"visibility\":{\"identifier\":\"Administrators\",\"type\":\"role\",\"value\":\"Administrators\"}}"

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-custom-field-associations">Issue custom field associations</h1>

This resource represents the fields associated to project and issue type contexts. Use it to:

 *  assign custom field to projects and issue types.

## Create associations

<a id="opIdcreateAssociations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/field/association \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "associationContexts": [
      {
        "identifier": 10000,
        "type": "PROJECT_ID"
      },
      {
        "identifier": 10001,
        "type": "PROJECT_ID"
      }
    ],
    "fields": [
      {
        "identifier": "customfield_10000",
        "type": "FIELD_ID"
      },
      {
        "identifier": "customfield_10001",
        "type": "FIELD_ID"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/field/association`

Associates fields with projects.

Fields will be associated with each issue type on the requested projects.

Fields will be associated with all projects that share the same field configuration which the provided projects are using. This means that while the field will be associated with the requested projects, it will also be associated with any other projects that share the same field configuration.

If a success response is returned it means that the field association has been created in any applicable contexts where it wasn't already present.

Up to 50 fields and up to 100 projects can be associated in a single request. If more fields or projects are provided a 400 response will be returned.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "associationContexts": [
    {
      "identifier": 10000,
      "type": "PROJECT_ID"
    },
    {
      "identifier": 10001,
      "type": "PROJECT_ID"
    }
  ],
  "fields": [
    {
      "identifier": "customfield_10000",
      "type": "FIELD_ID"
    },
    {
      "identifier": "customfield_10001",
      "type": "FIELD_ID"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-associations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[FieldAssociationsRequest](#schemafieldassociationsrequest)|true|Payload containing the fields to associate and the projects to associate them to.|
|» associationContexts|body|[[AssociationContextObject](#schemaassociationcontextobject)]|true|Contexts to associate/unassociate the fields with.|
|» fields|body|[[FieldIdentifierObject](#schemafieldidentifierobject)]|true|Fields to associate/unassociate with projects.|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="create-associations-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the field association validation passes.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the field, project, or issue type is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

## Remove associations

<a id="opIdremoveAssociations"></a>

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/field/association \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "associationContexts": [
      {
        "identifier": 10000,
        "type": "PROJECT_ID"
      },
      {
        "identifier": 10001,
        "type": "PROJECT_ID"
      }
    ],
    "fields": [
      {
        "identifier": "customfield_10000",
        "type": "FIELD_ID"
      },
      {
        "identifier": "customfield_10001",
        "type": "FIELD_ID"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /rest/api/3/field/association`

Unassociates a set of fields with a project and issue type context.

Fields will be unassociated with all projects/issue types that share the same field configuration which the provided project and issue types are using. This means that while the field will be unassociated with the provided project and issue types, it will also be unassociated with any other projects and issue types that share the same field configuration.

If a success response is returned it means that the field association has been removed in any applicable contexts where it was present.

Up to 50 fields and up to 100 projects and issue types can be unassociated in a single request. If more fields or projects are provided a 400 response will be returned.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "associationContexts": [
    {
      "identifier": 10000,
      "type": "PROJECT_ID"
    },
    {
      "identifier": 10001,
      "type": "PROJECT_ID"
    }
  ],
  "fields": [
    {
      "identifier": "customfield_10000",
      "type": "FIELD_ID"
    },
    {
      "identifier": "customfield_10001",
      "type": "FIELD_ID"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="remove-associations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[FieldAssociationsRequest](#schemafieldassociationsrequest)|true|Payload containing the fields to uassociate and the projects and issue types to unassociate them to.|
|» associationContexts|body|[[AssociationContextObject](#schemaassociationcontextobject)]|true|Contexts to associate/unassociate the fields with.|
|» fields|body|[[FieldIdentifierObject](#schemafieldidentifierobject)]|true|Fields to associate/unassociate with projects.|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
null
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the field association validation passes.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the field, project, or issue type is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-custom-field-configuration-apps">Issue custom field configuration (apps)</h1>

This resource represents configurations stored against a custom field context by a [Forge app](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/). Configurations are information used by the Forge app at runtime to determine how to handle or process the data in a custom field in a given context. Use this resource to set and read configurations.

## Bulk get custom field configurations

<a id="opIdgetCustomFieldsConfigurations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/app/field/context/configuration/list \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "fieldIdsOrKeys": [
      "customfield_10035",
      "customfield_10036"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/app/field/context/configuration/list`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of configurations for list of custom fields of a [type](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/modules/jira-custom-field-type/) created by a [Forge app](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/).

The result can be filtered by one of these criteria:

 *  `id`.
 *  `fieldContextId`.
 *  `issueId`.
 *  `projectKeyOrId` and `issueTypeId`.

Otherwise, all configurations for the provided list of custom fields are returned.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg). Jira permissions are not required for the Forge app that provided the custom field type.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "fieldIdsOrKeys": [
    "customfield_10035",
    "customfield_10036"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-get-custom-field-configurations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|query|[integer(int64)]|false|The list of configuration IDs. To include multiple configurations, separate IDs with an ampersand: `id=10000&id=10001`. Can't be provided with `fieldContextId`, `issueId`, `projectKeyOrId`, or `issueTypeId`.|
|fieldContextId|query|[integer(int64)]|false|The list of field context IDs. To include multiple field contexts, separate IDs with an ampersand: `fieldContextId=10000&fieldContextId=10001`. Can't be provided with `id`, `issueId`, `projectKeyOrId`, or `issueTypeId`.|
|issueId|query|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the issue to filter results by. If the issue doesn't exist, an empty list is returned. Can't be provided with `projectKeyOrId`, or `issueTypeId`.|
|projectKeyOrId|query|string|false|The ID or key of the project to filter results by. Must be provided with `issueTypeId`. Can't be provided with `issueId`.|
|issueTypeId|query|string|false|The ID of the issue type to filter results by. Must be provided with `projectKeyOrId`. Can't be provided with `issueId`.|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|body|body|[ConfigurationsListParameters](#schemaconfigurationslistparameters)|true|none|
|» fieldIdsOrKeys|body|[string]|true|List of IDs or keys of the custom fields. It can be a mix of IDs and keys in the same query.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"isLast\":true,\"maxResults\":1000,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":2,\"values\":[{\"customFieldId\":\"customfield_10035\",\"fieldContextId\":\"10010\",\"id\":\"10000\"},{\"configuration\":{\"maxValue\":10000,\"minValue\":0},\"customFieldId\":\"customfield_10036\",\"fieldContextId\":\"10011\",\"id\":\"10001\",\"schema\":{\"properties\":{\"amount\":{\"type\":\"number\"},\"currency\":{\"type\":\"string\"}},\"required\":[\"amount\",\"currency\"]}}]}"
```

<h3 id="bulk-get-custom-field-configurations-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PageBeanBulkContextualConfiguration](#schemapagebeanbulkcontextualconfiguration)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user is not a Jira admin or the request is not authenticated as from the app that provided the field.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the custom field is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

|issueId|query|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the issue to filter results by. If the issue doesn't exist, an empty list is returned. Can't be provided with `projectKeyOrId`, or `issueTypeId`.|
|projectKeyOrId|query|string|false|The ID or key of the project to filter results by. Must be provided with `issueTypeId`. Can't be provided with `issueId`.|
|issueTypeId|query|string|false|The ID of the issue type to filter results by. Must be provided with `projectKeyOrId`. Can't be provided with `issueId`.|

|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user is not a Jira admin or the request is not authenticated as from the app that provided the field.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the custom field is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )

## Update custom field configurations

<a id="opIdupdateCustomFieldConfiguration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/app/field/string/context/configuration \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "configurations": [
      {
        "id": "10000"
      },
      {
        "configuration": {
          "maxValue": 10000,
          "minValue": 0
        },
        "id": "10001",
        "schema": {
          "properties": {
            "amount": {
              "type": "number"
            },
            "currency": {
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "amount",
            "currency"
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/app/field/{fieldIdOrKey}/context/configuration`

Update the configuration for contexts of a custom field of a [type](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/modules/jira-custom-field-type/) created by a [Forge app](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/).

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg). Jira permissions are not required for the Forge app that created the custom field type.

```json
        "minValue": 0
      },
      "id": "10001",
      "schema": {
        "properties": {
          "amount": {
            "type": "number"
          },
          "currency": {
            "type": "string"
          }
        },
        "required": [

          "currency"
        ]
      }

}
```

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-custom-field-contexts">Issue custom field contexts</h1>

This resource represents issue custom field contexts. Use it to:

 *  get, create, update, and delete custom field contexts.
 *  get context to issue types and projects mappings.
 *  get custom field contexts for projects and issue types.
 *  assign custom field contexts to projects.
 *  remove custom field contexts from projects.
 *  add issue types to custom field contexts.

## Get custom field contexts

<a id="opIdgetContextsForField"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/field/string/context \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/field/{fieldId}/context`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of [ contexts](https://confluence.atlassian.com/adminjiracloud/what-are-custom-field-contexts-991923859.html) for a custom field. Contexts can be returned as follows:

 *  With no other parameters set, all contexts.
 *  By defining `id` only, all contexts from the list of IDs.
 *  By defining `isAnyIssueType`, limit the list of contexts returned to either those that apply to all issue types (true) or those that apply to only a subset of issue types (false)
 *  By defining `isGlobalContext`, limit the list of contexts return to either those that apply to all projects (global contexts) (true) or those that apply to only a subset of projects (false).

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg). *Edit Workflow* [edit workflow permission](https://support.atlassian.com/jira-cloud-administration/docs/permissions-for-company-managed-projects/#Edit-Workflows)

<h3 id="get-custom-field-contexts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fieldId|path|string|true|The ID of the custom field.|
|isAnyIssueType|query|boolean|false|Whether to return contexts that apply to all issue types.|
|isGlobalContext|query|boolean|false|Whether to return contexts that apply to all projects.|
|contextId|query|[integer(int64)]|false|The list of context IDs. To include multiple contexts, separate IDs with ampersand: `contextId=10000&contextId=10001`.|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"isLast\":true,\"maxResults\":100,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":2,\"values\":[{\"id\":\"10025\",\"name\":\"Bug fields context\",\"description\":\"A context used to define the custom field options for bugs.\",\"isGlobalContext\":true,\"isAnyIssueType\":false},{\"id\":\"10026\",\"name\":\"Task fields context\",\"description\":\"A context used to define the custom field options for tasks.\",\"isGlobalContext\":false,\"isAnyIssueType\":false}]}"
```

> 403 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"Only Jira administrators can access custom field contexts.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 404 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"The custom field was not found.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

<h3 id="get-custom-field-contexts-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PageBeanCustomFieldContext](#schemapagebeancustomfieldcontext)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the required permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the custom field was not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

## Create custom field context

<a id="opIdcreateCustomFieldContext"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/field/string/context \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "A context used to define the custom field options for bugs.",
    "issueTypeIds": [
      "10010"
    ],
    "name": "Bug fields context",
    "projectIds": []
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/field/{fieldId}/context`

Creates a custom field context.

If `projectIds` is empty, a global context is created. A global context is one that applies to all project. If `issueTypeIds` is empty, the context applies to all issue types.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "A context used to define the custom field options for bugs.",
  "issueTypeIds": [
    "10010"
  ],
  "name": "Bug fields context",
  "projectIds": []
}
```

<h3 id="create-custom-field-context-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fieldId|path|string|true|The ID of the custom field.|
|body|body|[CreateCustomFieldContext](#schemacreatecustomfieldcontext)|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the context.|
|» issueTypeIds|body|[string]|false|The list of issue types IDs for the context. If the list is empty, the context refers to all issue types.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the context.|
|» projectIds|body|[string]|false|The list of project IDs associated with the context. If the list is empty, the context is global.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
"{\"id\":\"10025\",\"name\":\"Bug fields context\",\"description\":\"A context used to define the custom field options for bugs.\",\"projectIds\":[],\"issueTypeIds\":[\"10010\"]}"
```

> 409 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"Sub-tasks are disabled in Jira. At least one of the issue types is a sub-task.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

<h3 id="create-custom-field-context-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returned if the custom field context is created.|[CreateCustomFieldContext](#schemacreatecustomfieldcontext)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the field, project, or issue type is not found.|None|
|409|Conflict|Returned if the issue type is a sub-task, but sub-tasks are disabled in Jira settings.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

## Get custom field contexts default values

<a id="opIdgetDefaultValues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/field/string/context/defaultValue \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/field/{fieldId}/context/defaultValue`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of defaults for a custom field. The results can be filtered by `contextId`, otherwise all values are returned. If no defaults are set for a context, nothing is returned.  
The returned object depends on type of the custom field:

 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueDate` (type `datepicker`) for date fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueDateTime` (type `datetimepicker`) for date-time fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueSingleOption` (type `option.single`) for single choice select lists and radio buttons.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueMultipleOption` (type `option.multiple`) for multiple choice select lists and checkboxes.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueCascadingOption` (type `option.cascading`) for cascading select lists.
 *  `CustomFieldContextSingleUserPickerDefaults` (type `single.user.select`) for single users.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueMultiUserPicker` (type `multi.user.select`) for user lists.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueSingleGroupPicker` (type `grouppicker.single`) for single choice group pickers.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueMultipleGroupPicker` (type `grouppicker.multiple`) for multiple choice group pickers.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueURL` (type `url`) for URLs.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueProject` (type `project`) for project pickers.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueFloat` (type `float`) for floats (floating-point numbers).
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueLabels` (type `labels`) for labels.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueTextField` (type `textfield`) for text fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueTextArea` (type `textarea`) for text area fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueLongText` (type `longtext`) for plain text paragraph fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueReadOnly` (type `readonly`) for read only (text) fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueMultipleVersion` (type `version.multiple`) for single choice version pickers.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueSingleVersion` (type `version.single`) for multiple choice version pickers.

Forge custom fields [types](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/modules/jira-custom-field-type/#data-types) are also supported, returning:

 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueForgeStringFieldBean` (type `forge.string`) for Forge string fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueForgeMultiStringFieldBean` (type `forge.string.list`) for Forge string collection fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueForgeObjectFieldBean` (type `forge.object`) for Forge object fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueForgeDateTimeFieldBean` (type `forge.datetime`) for Forge date-time fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueForgeGroupFieldBean` (type `forge.group`) for Forge group fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueForgeMultiGroupFieldBean` (type `forge.group.list`) for Forge group collection fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueForgeNumberFieldBean` (type `forge.number`) for Forge number fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueForgeUserFieldBean` (type `forge.user`) for Forge user fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueForgeMultiUserFieldBean` (type `forge.user.list`) for Forge user collection fields.

**Deprecated:** This API is deprecated and will be removed in October 2026. A replacement API that supports multiple default values per issue type within a context is coming soon. See the deprecation notice [CHANGE-3082](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/changelog/#CHANGE-3082) for more details.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-custom-field-contexts-default-values-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fieldId|path|string|true|The ID of the custom field, for example `customfield\_10000`.|
|contextId|query|[integer(int64)]|false|The IDs of the contexts.|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"isLast\":true,\"maxResults\":50,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":3,\"values\":[{\"contextId\":\"10100\",\"optionId\":\"10001\"},{\"contextId\":\"10101\",\"optionId\":\"10003\"},{\"contextId\":\"10103\"}]}"
```

> 403 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"Only Jira administrators can access custom field contexts.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 404 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"The custom field was not found.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

<h3 id="get-custom-field-contexts-default-values-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PageBeanCustomFieldContextDefaultValue](#schemapagebeancustomfieldcontextdefaultvalue)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if one or more of the field's contexts have different default values per issue type, which this endpoint cannot represent. Use `GET /rest/api/3/field/{fieldId}/context/defaultvalues` instead.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the required permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the custom field is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueSingleGroupPicker` (type `grouppicker.single`) for single choice group pickers.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueMultipleGroupPicker` (type `grouppicker.multiple`) for multiple choice group pickers.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueURL` (type `url`) for URLs.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueProject` (type `project`) for project pickers.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueFloat` (type `float`) for floats (floating-point numbers).
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueLabels` (type `labels`) for labels.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueTextField` (type `textfield`) for text fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueTextArea` (type `textarea`) for text area fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueLongText` (type `longtext`) for plain text paragraph fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueReadOnly` (type `readonly`) for read only (text) fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueMultipleVersion` (type `version.multiple`) for single choice version pickers.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueSingleVersion` (type `version.single`) for multiple choice version pickers.

Forge custom fields [types](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/modules/jira-custom-field-type/#data-types) are also supported, returning:

 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueForgeStringFieldBean` (type `forge.string`) for Forge string fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueForgeMultiStringFieldBean` (type `forge.string.list`) for Forge string collection fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueForgeObjectFieldBean` (type `forge.object`) for Forge object fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueForgeDateTimeFieldBean` (type `forge.datetime`) for Forge date-time fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueForgeGroupFieldBean` (type `forge.group`) for Forge group fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueForgeMultiGroupFieldBean` (type `forge.group.list`) for Forge group collection fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueForgeNumberFieldBean` (type `forge.number`) for Forge number fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueForgeUserFieldBean` (type `forge.user`) for Forge user fields.
 *  `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueForgeMultiUserFieldBean` (type `forge.user.list`) for Forge user collection fields.

Only one type of default object can be included in a request. To remove a default for a context, set the default parameter to `null`.

## Get default values for a custom field grouped by context and issue type

<a id="opIdgetContextDefaultValues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/field/string/context/defaultValues \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/field/{fieldId}/context/defaultValues`

Returns a paginated list of default values grouped by custom field context.

Each returned `ContextDefaultValuesBean` has a `contextId` and a `defaultValues` list of `IssueTypeDefaultValueBean` entries - one per issue-type-scoped default value configured for the context. An entry with `"isAnyIssueType": true` represents the catch-all default that applies to every issue type covered by the context that is not covered by a more specific entry; a non-null `issueTypeId` represents a default that only applies to that issue type.

For contexts that have not been converted to the multiple-contexts data model, exactly one entry is returned per context with `isAnyIssueType=true`. For converted contexts, one entry is returned per configured per-issue-type default.

The value object on each entry is the same polymorphic `CustomFieldContextDefaultValueBean` exposed by the deprecated `GET /defaultValue` endpoint - its concrete subtype depends on the custom field's type (see the list of supported types on that endpoint).

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-default-values-for-a-custom-field-grouped-by-context-and-issue-type-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fieldId|path|string|true|The ID of the custom field, for example `customfield\_10000`.|
|contextId|query|[integer(int64)]|false|The IDs of the contexts to return default values for. If omitted, default values for every context the custom field has are returned.|
|issueTypeId|query|[string]|false|The IDs of the issue types to restrict the returned per-issue-type default values to. If omitted, default values for every issue type are returned. This filter never removes the catch-all `isAnyIssueType` entry of a context.|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "isLast": true,
  "maxResults": 0,
  "nextPage": "http://example.com",
  "self": "http://example.com",
  "startAt": 0,
  "total": 0,
  "values": [
    {
      "contextId": 0,
      "defaultValues": [
        {
          "isAnyIssueType": true,
          "issueTypeId": "string",
          "value": {
            "cascadingOptionId": "string",
            "contextId": "string",
            "optionId": "string",
            "type": "string"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"Only Jira administrators can access custom field contexts.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 404 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"The custom field was not found.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

<h3 id="get-default-values-for-a-custom-field-grouped-by-context-and-issue-type-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PageBeanContextDefaultValues](#schemapagebeancontextdefaultvalues)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the required permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the custom field is not found.|None|

## Set default values for a custom field by context and issue type

<a id="opIdsetContextDefaultValues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/field/string/context/defaultValues \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "defaultValues": [
      {
        "contextId": 0,
        "isAnyIssueType": true,
        "issueTypeId": "string",
        "value": {
          "cascadingOptionId": "string",
          "contextId": "string",
          "optionId": "string",
          "type": "string"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/field/{fieldId}/context/defaultValues`

Updates default values for individual issue types in custom field contexts.

Only tenants enrolled in the early access program (EAP) can access this resource. See the [EAP announcement](https://ecosystem.atlassian.net/browse/CHANGE-3082) for details.

Each entry targets either one issue type through \{@code issueTypeId\}, or the catch-all configuration through \{@code isAnyIssueType=true\}. A null value removes the default for that target. Entries not included in the request are left unchanged.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "defaultValues": [
    {
      "contextId": 0,
      "isAnyIssueType": true,
      "issueTypeId": "string",
      "value": {
        "cascadingOptionId": "string",
        "contextId": "string",
        "optionId": "string",
        "type": "string"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="set-default-values-for-a-custom-field-by-context-and-issue-type-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

## Get custom field contexts for projects and issue types

<a id="opIdgetCustomFieldContextsForProjectsAndIssueTypes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/field/string/context/mapping \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "mappings": [
      {
        "issueTypeId": "10000",
        "projectId": "10000"
      },
      {
        "issueTypeId": "10001",
        "projectId": "10000"
      },
      {
        "issueTypeId": "10002",
        "projectId": "10001"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/field/{fieldId}/context/mapping`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of project and issue type mappings and, for each mapping, the ID of a [custom field context](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/k44fOw) that applies to the project and issue type.

If there is no custom field context assigned to the project then, if present, the custom field context that applies to all projects is returned if it also applies to the issue type or all issue types. If a custom field context is not found, the returned custom field context ID is `null`.

Duplicate project and issue type mappings cannot be provided in the request.

The order of the returned values is the same as provided in the request.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "mappings": [
    {
      "issueTypeId": "10000",
      "projectId": "10000"
    },
    {
      "issueTypeId": "10001",
      "projectId": "10000"
    },
    {
      "issueTypeId": "10002",
      "projectId": "10001"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-custom-field-contexts-for-projects-and-issue-types-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fieldId|path|string|true|The ID of the custom field.|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|body|body|[ProjectIssueTypeMappings](#schemaprojectissuetypemappings)|true|The list of project and issue type mappings.|
|» mappings|body|[[ProjectIssueTypeMapping](#schemaprojectissuetypemapping)]|true|The project and issue type mappings.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"isLast\":true,\"maxResults\":50,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":3,\"values\":[{\"projectId\":\"10000\",\"issueTypeId\":\"10000\",\"contextId\":\"10000\"},{\"projectId\":\"10000\",\"issueTypeId\":\"10001\",\"contextId\":null},{\"projectId\":\"10001\",\"issueTypeId\":\"10002\",\"contextId\":\"10003\"}]}"
```

> 400 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"Duplicate project and issue type mappings cannot be provided.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 403 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"Only Jira administrators can access custom field contexts.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 404 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"These projects were not found: 10005.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

<h3 id="get-custom-field-contexts-for-projects-and-issue-types-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PageBeanContextForProjectAndIssueType](#schemapagebeancontextforprojectandissuetype)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the required permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the custom field, project, or issue type is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

## Get project mappings for custom field context

<a id="opIdgetProjectContextMapping"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/field/string/context/projectmapping \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/field/{fieldId}/context/projectmapping`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of context to project mappings for a custom field. The result can be filtered by `contextId`. Otherwise, all mappings are returned. Invalid IDs are ignored.

**Note:** Jira is adding support for multiple field contexts per project. On sites where this is enabled, a custom field can have more than one context associated with the same project, so this operation can return several mappings that share the same `projectId`, each with a different `contextId`. Do not assume that a project appears at most once in the response. See [CHANGE-3082](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/changelog/#CHANGE-3082) for more details.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-project-mappings-for-custom-field-context-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fieldId|path|string|true|The ID of the custom field, for example `customfield\_10000`.|
|contextId|query|[integer(int64)]|false|The list of context IDs. To include multiple context, separate IDs with ampersand: `contextId=10000&contextId=10001`.|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"isLast\":true,\"maxResults\":100,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":2,\"values\":[{\"contextId\":\"10025\",\"projectId\":\"10001\"},{\"contextId\":\"10026\",\"isGlobalContext\":true}]}"
```

> 403 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"Only Jira administrators can access custom field contexts.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 404 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"The custom field was not found.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

<h3 id="get-project-mappings-for-custom-field-context-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PageBeanCustomFieldContextProjectMapping](#schemapagebeancustomfieldcontextprojectmapping)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the required permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the custom field is not found.|None|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

## Add issue types to context

<a id="opIdaddIssueTypesToContext"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/field/string/context/0/issuetype \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "issueTypeIds": [
      "10001",
      "10005",
      "10006"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/field/{fieldId}/context/{contextId}/issuetype`

Adds issue types to a custom field context, appending the issue types to the issue types list.

A custom field context without any issue types applies to all issue types. Adding issue types replaces the any-issue-type mapping unless \{@code isAnyIssueType\} is true. A supplied \{@code defaultValue\} applies to newly added mappings. If omitted, the default value of the first existing issue type mapping is copied. Existing mappings retain their defaults.

If any of the issue types exists in the custom field context, the operation fails and no issue types are added.

This API will not allow adding issue types to the global context from April 2026. Instead, an HTTP 400 response will be returned. See [CHANGE-3019](https://developer.atlassian.com/changelog/#CHANGE-3019)

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "issueTypeIds": [
    "10001",
    "10005",
    "10006"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-issue-types-to-context-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fieldId|path|string|true|The ID of the custom field.|
|contextId|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the context.|
|body|body|[AddIssueTypesToContext](#schemaaddissuetypestocontext)|true|none|
|» defaultValue|body|[CustomFieldContextDefaultValue](#schemacustomfieldcontextdefaultvalue)|false|none|
|» isAnyIssueType|body|boolean|false|Whether to add or retain the any-issue-type mapping. At least one of this property or issueTypeIds is required. Defaults to false.|
|» issueTypeIds|body|[string \| null]|false|The issue type IDs to add. Optional when isAnyIssueType is true.|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
null
```

> 400 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"These issue types are already associated with the context: 10001.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 403 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"Only Jira administrators can access custom field contexts.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 404 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"The context was not found.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 409 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"Sub-tasks are disabled in Jira. At least one of the issue types is a sub-task.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

<h3 id="add-issue-types-to-context-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if operation is successful.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the required permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the custom field, context, or one or more issue types are not found.|None|
|409|Conflict|Returned if the issue type is a sub-task, but sub-tasks are disabled in Jira settings.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the required permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the custom field, context, or one or more projects are not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-custom-field-options">Issue custom field options</h1>

This resource represents custom issue field select list options created in Jira or using the REST API. This resource supports the following field types:

 *  Checkboxes.
 *  Radio Buttons.
 *  Select List (single choice).
 *  Select List (multiple choices).
 *  Select List (cascading).

See [Issue custom field options (apps)](#api-group-Issue-custom-field-options--apps-) to manipulate custom issue field select list options created by a Connect app.

Use it to retrieve, create, update, order, and delete custom field options.

## Get custom field option

<a id="opIdgetCustomFieldOption"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/customFieldOption/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/customFieldOption/{id}`

Returns a custom field option. For example, an option in a select list.

Note that this operation **only works for issue field select list options created in Jira or using operations from the [Issue custom field options](#api-group-Issue-custom-field-options) resource**, it cannot be used with issue field select list options created by Connect apps.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** The custom field option is returned as follows:

 *  if the user has the *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).
 *  if the user has the *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for at least one project the custom field is used in, and the field is visible in at least one layout the user has permission to view.

<h3 id="get-custom-field-option-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the custom field option.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/customFieldOption/10000\",\"value\":\"To Do\"}"
```

<h3 id="get-custom-field-option-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[CustomFieldOption](#schemacustomfieldoption)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  the custom field option is not found.<br> *  the user does not have permission to view the custom field.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

This operation works for custom field options created in Jira or the operations from this resource. **To work with issue field select list options created for Connect apps use the [Issue custom field options (apps)](#api-group-issue-custom-field-options--apps-) operations.**

```bash
        "value": "The Electric City"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/field/{fieldId}/context/{contextId}/option`

Updates the options of a custom field.

If any of the options are not found, no options are updated. Options where the values in the request match the current values aren't updated and aren't reported in the response.

Note that this operation **only works for issue field select list options created in Jira or using operations from the [Issue custom field options](#api-group-Issue-custom-field-options) resource**, it cannot be used with issue field select list options created by Connect apps.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

```json
    },

    }
  ]
}
```

## Create custom field options (context)

<a id="opIdcreateCustomFieldOption"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/field/string/context/0/option \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "options": [
      {
        "disabled": false,
        "value": "Scranton"
      },
      {
        "disabled": true,
        "optionId": "10000",
        "value": "Manhattan"
      },
      {
        "disabled": false,
        "value": "The Electric City"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/field/{fieldId}/context/{contextId}/option`

Creates options and, where the custom select field is of the type Select List (cascading), cascading options for a custom select field. The options are added to a context of the field.

The maximum number of options that can be created per request is 1000 and each field can have a maximum of 10000 options.

This operation works for custom field options created in Jira or the operations from this resource. **To work with issue field select list options created for Connect apps use the [Issue custom field options (apps)](#api-group-issue-custom-field-options--apps-) operations.**

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "options": [
    {
      "disabled": false,
      "value": "Scranton"
    },
    {
      "disabled": true,
      "optionId": "10000",
      "value": "Manhattan"
    },
    {
      "disabled": false,
      "value": "The Electric City"
    }
  ]
}
```
