## Bulk set issue property

<a id="opIdbulkSetIssueProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/properties/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "filter": {
      "currentValue": {
        "owner": "admin",
        "weight": 50
      },
      "entityIds": [
        10100,
        100010
      ],
      "hasProperty": true
    },
    "value": {
      "owner": "admin",
      "weight": 100
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/issue/properties/{propertyKey}`

Sets a property value on multiple issues.

The value set can be a constant or determined by a [Jira expression](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/jira-expressions/). Expressions must be computable with constant complexity when applied to a set of issues. Expressions must also comply with the [restrictions](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/jira-expressions/#restrictions) that apply to all Jira expressions.

The issues to be updated can be specified by a filter.

The filter identifies issues eligible for update using these criteria:

 *  `entityIds` Only issues from this list are eligible.
 *  `currentValue` Only issues with the property set to this value are eligible.
 *  `hasProperty`:
    
     *  If *true*, only issues with the property are eligible.
     *  If *false*, only issues without the property are eligible.

If more than one criteria is specified, they are joined with the logical *AND*: only issues that satisfy all criteria are eligible.

If an invalid combination of criteria is provided, an error is returned. For example, specifying a `currentValue` and `hasProperty` as *false* would not match any issues (because without the property the property cannot have a value).

The filter is optional. Without the filter all the issues visible to the user and where the user has the EDIT\_ISSUES permission for the issue are considered eligible.

This operation is:

 *  transactional, either all eligible issues are updated or, when errors occur, none are updated.
 *  [asynchronous](#async). Follow the `location` link in the response to determine the status of the task and use [Get task](#api-rest-api-3-task-taskId-get) to obtain subsequent updates.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for each project containing issues.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  *Edit issues* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for each issue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filter": {
    "currentValue": {
      "owner": "admin",
      "weight": 50
    },
    "entityIds": [
      10100,
      100010
    ],
    "hasProperty": true
  },
  "value": {
    "owner": "admin",
    "weight": 100
  }
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-set-issue-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|propertyKey|path|string|true|The key of the property. The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|body|body|[BulkIssuePropertyUpdateRequest](#schemabulkissuepropertyupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» expression|body|string|false|EXPERIMENTAL. The Jira expression to calculate the value of the property. The value of the expression must be an object that can be converted to JSON, such as a number, boolean, string, list, or map. The context variables available to the expression are `issue` and `user`. Issues for which the expression returns a value whose JSON representation is longer than 32768 characters are ignored.|
|» filter|body|object|false|The bulk operation filter.|
|» » currentValue|body|object|false|The value of properties to perform the bulk operation on.|
|» » entityIds|body|[integer(int64)]|false|List of issues to perform the bulk operation on.|
|» » hasProperty|body|boolean|false|Whether the bulk operation occurs only when the property is present on or absent from an issue.|
|» value|body|object|false|The value of the property. The value must be a [valid](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4627), non-empty JSON blob. The maximum length is 32768 characters.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errorMessages": [
    "string"
  ],
  "errors": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "status": 0
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errorMessages": [
    "string"
  ],
  "errors": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "status": 0
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-set-issue-property-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|303|See Other|Returned if the request is successful.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|[ErrorCollection](#schemaerrorcollection)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|[ErrorCollection](#schemaerrorcollection)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: write:jira-work )
</aside>

## Bulk delete issue property

<a id="opIdbulkDeleteIssueProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/properties/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "currentValue": "deprecated value",
    "entityIds": [
      10100,
      100010
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /rest/api/3/issue/properties/{propertyKey}`

Deletes a property value from multiple issues. The issues to be updated can be specified by filter criteria.

The criteria the filter used to identify eligible issues are:

 *  `entityIds` Only issues from this list are eligible.
 *  `currentValue` Only issues with the property set to this value are eligible.

If both criteria is specified, they are joined with the logical *AND*: only issues that satisfy both criteria are considered eligible.

If no filter criteria are specified, all the issues visible to the user and where the user has the EDIT\_ISSUES permission for the issue are considered eligible.

This operation is:

 *  transactional, either the property is deleted from all eligible issues or, when errors occur, no properties are deleted.
 *  [asynchronous](#async). Follow the `location` link in the response to determine the status of the task and use [Get task](#api-rest-api-3-task-taskId-get) to obtain subsequent updates.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [ project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for each project containing issues.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  *Edit issues* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for each issue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "currentValue": "deprecated value",
  "entityIds": [
    10100,
    100010
  ]
}
```

```json
  ],

  },
  "status": 0
}
```

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-redaction">Issue redaction</h1>

This resource represents Issue Redaction. Provides APIs to redact issue data.

## Redact

<a id="opIdredact"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/redact \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "redactions": [
      {
        "contentItem": {
          "entityId": "summary",
          "entityType": "issuefieldvalue",
          "id": "10000"
        },
        "externalId": "51101de6-d001-429d-a095-b2b96dd57fcb",
        "reason": "PII data",
        "redactionPosition": {
          "adfPointer": "/content/0/content/0/text",
          "expectedText": "ODFiNjM3ZDhmY2QyYzZkYTYzNTllNjk2MzExM2ExMTcwZGU3OTVlNGI3MjViODRkMWUwYjRjZmQ5ZWM1OGNlOQ==",
          "from": 14,
          "to": 20
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/redact`

Submit a job to redact issue field data. This will trigger the redaction of the data in the specified fields asynchronously.

The redaction status can be polled using the job id.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "redactions": [
    {
      "contentItem": {
        "entityId": "summary",
        "entityType": "issuefieldvalue",
        "id": "10000"
      },
      "externalId": "51101de6-d001-429d-a095-b2b96dd57fcb",
      "reason": "PII data",
      "redactionPosition": {
        "adfPointer": "/content/0/content/0/text",
        "expectedText": "ODFiNjM3ZDhmY2QyYzZkYTYzNTllNjk2MzExM2ExMTcwZGU3OTVlNGI3MjViODRkMWUwYjRjZmQ5ZWM1OGNlOQ==",
        "from": 14,
        "to": 20
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="redact-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BulkRedactionRequest](#schemabulkredactionrequest)|true|List of redaction requests|
|» redactions|body|[[SingleRedactionRequest](#schemasingleredactionrequest)]|false|none|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
"497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errorMessages": [
    "string"
  ],
  "errors": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "status": 0
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errorMessages": [
    "string"
  ],
  "errors": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "status": 0
}
```

<h3 id="redact-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Returned if the job submission is successful. The response contains the job id.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the redaction request is invalid.|[ErrorCollection](#schemaerrorcollection)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the user / app is not authorised to redact data|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the AGP subscription is not present.|[ErrorCollection](#schemaerrorcollection)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

## Get redaction status

<a id="opIdgetRedactionStatus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/redact/status/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/redact/status/{jobId}`

Retrieves the current status of a redaction job ID.

The jobStatus will be one of the following:

 *  IN\_PROGRESS - The redaction job is currently in progress
 *  COMPLETED - The redaction job has completed successfully.
 *  PENDING - The redaction job has not started yet

<h3 id="get-redaction-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|jobId|path|string|true|Redaction job id|

```json
  "bulkRedactionResponse": {
    "results": [
      {
        "externalId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
        "successful": true
      }
    ]
  },
  "jobStatus": "PENDING"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errorMessages": [
    "string"
  ],
  "errors": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },

}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errorMessages": [
    "string"
  ],

    "property1": "string",

  },
  "status": 0
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|200|OK|Returned if the job status is successfully retrieved.|[RedactionJobStatusResponse](#schemaredactionjobstatusresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the AGP subscription is not present.|[ErrorCollection](#schemaerrorcollection)|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the job id is not found.|[ErrorCollection](#schemaerrorcollection)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-remote-links">Issue remote links</h1>

This resource represents remote issue links, a way of linking Jira to information in other systems. Use it to get, create, update, and delete remote issue links either by ID or global ID. The global ID provides a way of accessing remote issue links using information about the item's remote system host and remote system identifier.

## Get remote issue links

<a id="opIdgetRemoteIssueLinks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/10000/remotelink \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/remotelink`

Returns the remote issue links for an issue. When a remote issue link global ID is provided the record with that global ID is returned, otherwise all remote issue links are returned. Where a global ID includes reserved URL characters these must be escaped in the request. For example, pass `system=http://www.mycompany.com/support&id=1` as `system%3Dhttp%3A%2F%2Fwww.mycompany.com%2Fsupport%26id%3D1`.

This operation requires [issue linking to be active](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yoXKM).

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

<h3 id="get-remote-issue-links-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|
|globalId|query|string|false|The global ID of the remote issue link.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"[{\"application\":{\"name\":\"My Acme Tracker\",\"type\":\"com.acme.tracker\"},\"globalId\":\"system=http://www.mycompany.com/support&id=1\",\"id\":10000,\"object\":{\"icon\":{\"title\":\"Support Ticket\",\"url16x16\":\"http://www.mycompany.com/support/ticket.png\"},\"status\":{\"icon\":{\"link\":\"http://www.mycompany.com/support?id=1&details=closed\",\"title\":\"Case Closed\",\"url16x16\":\"http://www.mycompany.com/support/resolved.png\"},\"resolved\":true},\"summary\":\"Customer support issue\",\"title\":\"TSTSUP-111\",\"url\":\"http://www.mycompany.com/support?id=1\"},\"relationship\":\"causes\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/issue/MKY-1/remotelink/10000\"},{\"application\":{\"name\":\"My Acme Tester\",\"type\":\"com.acme.tester\"},\"globalId\":\"system=http://www.anothercompany.com/tester&id=1234\",\"id\":10001,\"object\":{\"icon\":{\"title\":\"Test Case\",\"url16x16\":\"http://www.anothercompany.com/tester/images/testcase.gif\"},\"status\":{\"icon\":{\"link\":\"http://www.anothercompany.com/tester/person?accountId=5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"title\":\"Tested by Mia Krystof\",\"url16x16\":\"http://www.anothercompany.com/tester/images/person/mia.gif\"},\"resolved\":false},\"summary\":\"Test that the submit button saves the item\",\"title\":\"Test Case #1234\",\"url\":\"http://www.anothercompany.com/tester/testcase/1234\"},\"relationship\":\"is tested by\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/issue/MKY-1/remotelink/10001\"}]"
```

<h3 id="get-remote-issue-links-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful. A single RemoteIssueLink will be returned when specifying `globalId`, otherwise an array of RemoteIssueLink is returned.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if issue linking is disabled.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the issue or remote issue link is not found or the user does not have permission to view the issue.|None|
|413|Payload Too Large|Returned if the per-issue limit for remote links has been breached.|None|

<h3 id="get-remote-issue-links-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[[RemoteIssueLink](#schemaremoteissuelink)]|false|none|none|
|*anonymous*|[[RemoteIssueLink](#schemaremoteissuelink)]|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[RemoteIssueLink](#schemaremoteissuelink)|false|none|Details of an issue remote link.|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Create or update remote issue link

<a id="opIdcreateOrUpdateRemoteIssueLink"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/string/remotelink \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "application": {
      "name": "My Acme Tracker",
      "type": "com.acme.tracker"
    },
    "globalId": "system=http://www.mycompany.com/support&id=1",
    "object": {
      "icon": {
        "title": "Support Ticket",
        "url16x16": "http://www.mycompany.com/support/ticket.png"
      },
      "status": {
        "icon": {
          "link": "http://www.mycompany.com/support?id=1&details=closed",
          "title": "Case Closed",
          "url16x16": "http://www.mycompany.com/support/resolved.png"
        },
        "resolved": true
      },
      "summary": "Customer support issue",
      "title": "TSTSUP-111",
      "url": "http://www.mycompany.com/support?id=1"
    },
    "relationship": "causes"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/remotelink`

Creates or updates a remote issue link for an issue.

If a `globalId` is provided and a remote issue link with that global ID is found it is updated. Any fields without values in the request are set to null. Otherwise, the remote issue link is created.

This operation requires [issue linking to be active](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yoXKM).

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* and *Link issues* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "application": {
    "name": "My Acme Tracker",
    "type": "com.acme.tracker"
  },
  "globalId": "system=http://www.mycompany.com/support&id=1",
  "object": {
    "icon": {
      "title": "Support Ticket",
      "url16x16": "http://www.mycompany.com/support/ticket.png"
    },
    "status": {
      "icon": {
        "link": "http://www.mycompany.com/support?id=1&details=closed",
        "title": "Case Closed",
        "url16x16": "http://www.mycompany.com/support/resolved.png"
      },
      "resolved": true
    },
    "summary": "Customer support issue",
    "title": "TSTSUP-111",
    "url": "http://www.mycompany.com/support?id=1"
  },
  "relationship": "causes"
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-remote-issue-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|
|body|body|[RemoteIssueLinkRequest](#schemaremoteissuelinkrequest)|true|none|
|» application|body|object|false|Details of the remote application the linked item is in. For example, trello.|
|» » name|body|string|false|The name of the application. Used in conjunction with the (remote) object icon title to display a tooltip for the link's icon. The tooltip takes the format "\[application name\] icon title". Blank items are excluded from the tooltip title. If both items are blank, the icon tooltop displays as "Web Link". Grouping and sorting of links may place links without an application name last.|
|» » type|body|string|false|The name-spaced type of the application, used by registered rendering apps.|
|» globalId|body|string|false|An identifier for the remote item in the remote system. For example, the global ID for a remote item in Confluence would consist of the app ID and page ID, like this: `appId=456&pageId=123`.<br><br>Setting this field enables the remote issue link details to be updated or deleted using remote system and item details as the record identifier, rather than using the record's Jira ID.<br><br>The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|» object|body|object|true|Details of the item linked to.|
|» » icon|body|object|false|Details of the icon for the item. If no icon is defined, the default link icon is used in Jira.|
|» » » link|body|string|false|The URL of the tooltip, used only for a status icon. If not set, the status icon in Jira is not clickable.|
|» » » title|body|string|false|The title of the icon. This is used as follows:<br><br> *  For a status icon it is used as a tooltip on the icon. If not set, the status icon doesn't display a tooltip in Jira.<br> *  For the remote object icon it is used in conjunction with the application name to display a tooltip for the link's icon. The tooltip takes the format "\[application name\] icon title". Blank itemsare excluded from the tooltip title. If both items are blank, the icon tooltop displays as "Web Link".|
|» » » url16x16|body|string|false|The URL of an icon that displays at 16x16 pixel in Jira.|
|» » status|body|object|false|The status of the item.|
|» » » icon|body|object|false|Details of the icon representing the status. If not provided, no status icon displays in Jira.|
|» » » » link|body|string|false|The URL of the tooltip, used only for a status icon. If not set, the status icon in Jira is not clickable.|
|» » » » title|body|string|false|The title of the icon. This is used as follows:<br><br> *  For a status icon it is used as a tooltip on the icon. If not set, the status icon doesn't display a tooltip in Jira.<br> *  For the remote object icon it is used in conjunction with the application name to display a tooltip for the link's icon. The tooltip takes the format "\[application name\] icon title". Blank itemsare excluded from the tooltip title. If both items are blank, the icon tooltop displays as "Web Link".|
|» » » » url16x16|body|string|false|The URL of an icon that displays at 16x16 pixel in Jira.|
|» » » resolved|body|boolean|false|Whether the item is resolved. If set to "true", the link to the issue is displayed in a strikethrough font, otherwise the link displays in normal font.|
|» » summary|body|string|false|The summary details of the item.|
|» » title|body|string|true|The title of the item.|
|» » url|body|string|true|The URL of the item.|
|» relationship|body|string|false|Description of the relationship between the issue and the linked item. If not set, the relationship description "links to" is used in Jira.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"id\":10000,\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/issue/MKY-1/remotelink/10000\"}"
```

> 201 Response

```json
"{\"id\":10000,\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/issue/MKY-1/remotelink/10000\"}"
```

> 400 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[],\"errors\":{\"title\":\"'title' is required.\"}}"
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-remote-issue-link-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the remote issue link is updated.|[RemoteIssueLinkIdentifies](#schemaremoteissuelinkidentifies)|
|201|Created|Returned if the remote issue link is created.|[RemoteIssueLinkIdentifies](#schemaremoteissuelinkidentifies)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to link issues.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the issue is not found or the user does not have permission to view the issue.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: write:jira-work )
</aside>

## Delete remote issue link by global ID

<a id="opIddeleteRemoteIssueLinkByGlobalId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/10000/remotelink?globalId=system%3Dhttp%3A%2F%2Fwww.mycompany.com%2Fsupport%26id%3D1' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/remotelink`

Deletes the remote issue link from the issue using the link's global ID. Where the global ID includes reserved URL characters these must be escaped in the request. For example, pass `system=http://www.mycompany.com/support&id=1` as `system%3Dhttp%3A%2F%2Fwww.mycompany.com%2Fsupport%26id%3D1`.

This operation requires [issue linking to be active](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yoXKM).

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* and *Link issues* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is implemented, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

<h3 id="delete-remote-issue-link-by-global-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|
|globalId|query|string|true|The global ID of a remote issue link.|

<h3 id="delete-remote-issue-link-by-global-id-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the request is successful.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if a global ID isn't provided.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to link issues.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the issue or remote issue link is not found or the user does not have permission to view the issue.|None|

The tooltip takes the format "\[application name\] icon title". Blank items are excluded from the tooltip title. If both items are blank, the icon tooltop displays as "Web Link". Grouping and sorting of links may place links without an application name last.|
|» » type|body|string|false|The name-spaced type of the application, used by registered rendering apps.|
|» globalId|body|string|false|An identifier for the remote item in the remote system. For example, the global ID for a remote item in Confluence would consist of the app ID and page ID, like this: `appId=456&pageId=123`.<br><br>Setting this field enables the remote issue link details to be updated or deleted using remote system and item details as the record identifier, rather than using the record's Jira ID.<br><br>The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|» object|body|object|true|Details of the item linked to.|
|» » icon|body|object|false|Details of the icon for the item. If no icon is defined, the default link icon is used in Jira.|
|» » » link|body|string|false|The URL of the tooltip, used only for a status icon. If not set, the status icon in Jira is not clickable.|
|» » » title|body|string|false|The title of the icon. This is used as follows:<br><br> *  For a status icon it is used as a tooltip on the icon. If not set, the status icon doesn't display a tooltip in Jira.<br> *  For the remote object icon it is used in conjunction with the application name to display a tooltip for the link's icon. The tooltip takes the format "\[application name\] icon title". Blank itemsare excluded from the tooltip title. If both items are blank, the icon tooltop displays as "Web Link".|
|» » » url16x16|body|string|false|The URL of an icon that displays at 16x16 pixel in Jira.|
|» » status|body|object|false|The status of the item.|
|» » » icon|body|object|false|Details of the icon representing the status. If not provided, no status icon displays in Jira.|
|» » » » link|body|string|false|The URL of the tooltip, used only for a status icon. If not set, the status icon in Jira is not clickable.|
|» » » » title|body|string|false|The title of the icon. This is used as follows:<br><br> *  For a status icon it is used as a tooltip on the icon. If not set, the status icon doesn't display a tooltip in Jira.<br> *  For the remote object icon it is used in conjunction with the application name to display a tooltip for the link's icon. The tooltip takes the format "\[application name\] icon title". Blank itemsare excluded from the tooltip title. If both items are blank, the icon tooltop displays as "Web Link".|
|» » » » url16x16|body|string|false|The URL of an icon that displays at 16x16 pixel in Jira.|
|» » » resolved|body|boolean|false|Whether the item is resolved. If set to "true", the link to the issue is displayed in a strikethrough font, otherwise the link displays in normal font.|
|» » summary|body|string|false|The summary details of the item.|
|» » title|body|string|true|The title of the item.|
|» » url|body|string|true|The URL of the item.|
|» relationship|body|string|false|Description of the relationship between the issue and the linked item. If not set, the relationship description "links to" is used in Jira.|

```json
null
```

## Delete remote issue link by ID

<a id="opIddeleteRemoteIssueLinkById"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/10000/remotelink/10000 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/remotelink/{linkId}`

Deletes a remote issue link from an issue.

This operation requires [issue linking to be active](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yoXKM).

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects*, *Edit issues*, and *Link issues* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

<h3 id="delete-remote-issue-link-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|
|linkId|path|string|true|The ID of a remote issue link.|

<h3 id="delete-remote-issue-link-by-id-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the request is successful.|None|

|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to link issues.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the issue or remote issue link is not found or the user does not have permission to view the issue.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: write:jira-work )
</aside>

`GET /rest/api/3/resolution/search`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of resolutions. The list can contain all resolutions or a subset determined by any combination of these criteria:

 *  a list of resolutions IDs.
 *  whether the field configuration is a default. This returns resolutions from company-managed (classic) projects only, as there is no concept of default resolutions in team-managed projects.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Permission to access Jira.

|id|query|[string]|false|The list of resolutions IDs to be filtered out|
|onlyDefault|query|boolean|false|When set to true, return default only, when IDs provided, if none of them is default, return empty page. Default value is false|

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-search">Issue search</h1>

This resource represents various ways to search for issues. Use it to search for issues with a JQL query and find issues to populate an issue picker.

## Get issue picker suggestions

<a id="opIdgetIssuePickerResource"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/picker \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issue/picker`

Returns lists of issues matching a query string. Use this resource to provide auto-completion suggestions when the user is looking for an issue using a word or string.

This operation returns two lists:

 *  `History Search` which includes issues from the user's history of created, edited, or viewed issues that contain the string in the `query` parameter.
 *  `Current Search` which includes issues that match the JQL expression in `currentJQL` and contain the string in the `query` parameter.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** None.

<h3 id="get-issue-picker-suggestions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|A string to match against text fields in the issue such as title, description, or comments.|
|currentJQL|query|string|false|A JQL query defining a list of issues to search for the query term. Note that `username` and `userkey` cannot be used as search terms for this parameter, due to privacy reasons. Use `accountId` instead.|
|currentIssueKey|query|string|false|The key of an issue to exclude from search results. For example, the issue the user is viewing when they perform this query.|
|currentProjectId|query|string|false|The ID of a project that suggested issues must belong to.|
|showSubTasks|query|boolean|false|Indicate whether to include subtasks in the suggestions list.|
|showSubTaskParent|query|boolean|false|When `currentIssueKey` is a subtask, whether to include the parent issue in the suggestions if it matches the query.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response


## Check issues against JQL

<a id="opIdmatchIssues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/jql/match \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "issueIds": [
      10001,
      1000,
      10042
    ],
    "jqls": [
      "project = FOO",
      "issuetype = Bug",
      "summary ~ \"some text\" AND project in (FOO, BAR)"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/jql/match`

Checks whether one or more issues would be returned by one or more JQL queries. Up to 10 JQL queries can be specified and up to 50 issue IDs included in the request.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** None, however, issues are only matched against JQL queries where the user has:

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "issueIds": [
    10001,
    1000,
    10042
  ],
  "jqls": [
    "project = FOO",
    "issuetype = Bug",
    "summary ~ \"some text\" AND project in (FOO, BAR)"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="check-issues-against-jql-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IssuesAndJQLQueries](#schemaissuesandjqlqueries)|true|none|
|» issueIds|body|[integer(int64)]|true|A list of up to 50 issue IDs.|
|» jqls|body|[string]|true|A list of up to 10 JQL queries.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"matches\":[{\"matchedIssues\":[10000,10004],\"errors\":[]},{\"matchedIssues\":[100134,10025,10236],\"errors\":[]},{\"matchedIssues\":[],\"errors\":[]},{\"matchedIssues\":[],\"errors\":[\"Invalid JQL: broken = value\"]}]}"
```

<h3 id="check-issues-against-jql-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[IssueMatches](#schemaissuematches)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if `jqls` contains more than 10 JQL queries or `issueIds` contains more than 50 issue IDs.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Currently being removed. Search for issues using JQL (GET)

<a id="opIdsearchForIssuesUsingJql"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/search`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Endpoint is currently being removed. [More details](https://developer.atlassian.com/changelog/#CHANGE-2046)

Searches for issues using [JQL](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/egORLQ).

If the JQL query expression is too large to be encoded as a query parameter, use the [POST](#api-rest-api-3-search-post) version of this resource.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Issues are included in the response where the user has:

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project containing the issue.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

<h3 id="currently-being-removed-search-for-issues-using-jql-get-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|jql|query|string|false|The [JQL](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/egORLQ) that defines the search. Note:<br><br> *  If no JQL expression is provided, all issues are returned.<br> *  `username` and `userkey` cannot be used as search terms due to privacy reasons. Use `accountId` instead.<br> *  If a user has hidden their email address in their user profile, partial matches of the email address will not find the user. An exact match is required.|
|startAt|query|integer(int32)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page. To manage page size, Jira may return fewer items per page where a large number of fields or properties are requested. The greatest number of items returned per page is achieved when requesting `id` or `key` only.|
|validateQuery|query|string|false|Determines how to validate the JQL query and treat the validation results. Supported values are:<br><br> *  `strict` Returns a 400 response code if any errors are found, along with a list of all errors (and warnings).<br> *  `warn` Returns all errors as warnings.<br> *  `none` No validation is performed.<br> *  `true` *Deprecated* A legacy synonym for `strict`.<br> *  `false` *Deprecated* A legacy synonym for `warn`.<br><br>Note: If the JQL is not correctly formed a 400 response code is returned, regardless of the `validateQuery` value.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A list of fields to return for each issue, use it to retrieve a subset of fields. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `*all` Returns all fields.<br> *  `*navigable` Returns navigable fields.<br> *  Any issue field, prefixed with a minus to exclude.<br><br>Examples:<br><br> *  `summary,comment` Returns only the summary and comments fields.<br> *  `-description` Returns all navigable (default) fields except description.<br> *  `*all,-comment` Returns all fields except comments.<br><br>This parameter may be specified multiple times. For example, `fields=field1,field2&fields=field3`.<br><br>Note: All navigable fields are returned by default. This differs from [GET issue](#api-rest-api-3-issue-issueIdOrKey-get) where the default is all fields.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information about issues in the response. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `renderedFields` Returns field values rendered in HTML format.<br> *  `names` Returns the display name of each field.<br> *  `schema` Returns the schema describing a field type.<br> *  `transitions` Returns all possible transitions for the issue.<br> *  `operations` Returns all possible operations for the issue.<br> *  `editmeta` Returns information about how each field can be edited.<br> *  `changelog` Returns a list of recent updates to an issue, sorted by date, starting from the most recent.<br> *  `versionedRepresentations` Instead of `fields`, returns `versionedRepresentations` a JSON array containing each version of a field's value, with the highest numbered item representing the most recent version.|
|properties|query|[string]|false|A list of issue property keys for issue properties to include in the results. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Multiple properties can also be provided using an ampersand separated list. For example, `properties=prop1,prop2&properties=prop3`. A maximum of 5 issue property keys can be specified.|
|fieldsByKeys|query|boolean|false|Reference fields by their key (rather than ID).|
|failFast|query|boolean|false|Whether to fail the request quickly in case of an error while loading fields for an issue. For `failFast=true`, if one field fails, the entire operation fails. For `failFast=false`, the operation will continue even if a field fails. It will return a valid response, but without values for the failed field(s).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|validateQuery|strict|
|validateQuery|warn|
|validateQuery|none|
|validateQuery|true|
|validateQuery|false|

## Currently being removed. Search for issues using JQL (POST)

<a id="opIdsearchForIssuesUsingJqlPost"></a>

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "expand": [
      "names",

      "summary",

      "assignee"
    ],

    "startAt": 0
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/search`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Endpoint is currently being removed. [More details](https://developer.atlassian.com/changelog/#CHANGE-2046)

Searches for issues using [JQL](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/egORLQ).

There is a [GET](#api-rest-api-3-search-get) version of this resource that can be used for smaller JQL query expressions.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Issues are included in the response where the user has:

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project containing the issue.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expand": [
    "names",
    "schema",
    "operations"
  ],
  "fields": [
    "summary",
    "status",
    "assignee"
  ],
  "fieldsByKeys": false,
  "jql": "project = HSP",
  "maxResults": 15,
  "startAt": 0
}
```

<h3 id="currently-being-removed-search-for-issues-using-jql-post-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SearchRequestBean](#schemasearchrequestbean)|true|A JSON object containing the search request.|
|» expand|body|[string]|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information about issues in the response. Note that, unlike the majority of instances where `expand` is specified, `expand` is defined as a list of values. The expand options are:<br><br> *  `renderedFields` Returns field values rendered in HTML format.<br> *  `names` Returns the display name of each field.<br> *  `schema` Returns the schema describing a field type.<br> *  `transitions` Returns all possible transitions for the issue.<br> *  `operations` Returns all possible operations for the issue.<br> *  `editmeta` Returns information about how each field can be edited.<br> *  `changelog` Returns a list of recent updates to an issue, sorted by date, starting from the most recent.<br> *  `versionedRepresentations` Instead of `fields`, returns `versionedRepresentations` a JSON array containing each version of a field's value, with the highest numbered item representing the most recent version.|
|» fields|body|[string]|false|A list of fields to return for each issue, use it to retrieve a subset of fields. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `*all` Returns all fields.<br> *  `*navigable` Returns navigable fields.<br> *  Any issue field, prefixed with a minus to exclude.<br><br>The default is `*navigable`.<br><br>Examples:<br><br> *  `summary,comment` Returns the summary and comments fields only.<br> *  `-description` Returns all navigable (default) fields except description.<br> *  `*all,-comment` Returns all fields except comments.<br><br>Multiple `fields` parameters can be included in a request.<br><br>Note: All navigable fields are returned by default. This differs from [GET issue](#api-rest-api-3-issue-issueIdOrKey-get) where the default is all fields.|
|» fieldsByKeys|body|boolean|false|Reference fields by their key (rather than ID). The default is `false`.|
|» jql|body|string|false|A [JQL](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/egORLQ) expression.|
|» maxResults|body|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|» properties|body|[string]|false|A list of up to 5 issue properties to include in the results. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list.|
|» startAt|body|integer(int32)|false|The index of the first item to return in the page of results (page offset). The base index is `0`.|
|» validateQuery|body|string|false|Determines how to validate the JQL query and treat the validation results. Supported values:<br><br> *  `strict` Returns a 400 response code if any errors are found, along with a list of all errors (and warnings).<br> *  `warn` Returns all errors as warnings.<br> *  `none` No validation is performed.<br> *  `true` *Deprecated* A legacy synonym for `strict`.<br> *  `false` *Deprecated* A legacy synonym for `warn`.<br><br>The default is `strict`.<br><br>Note: If the JQL is not correctly formed a 400 response code is returned, regardless of the `validateQuery` value.|

## Count issues using JQL

<a id="opIdcountIssues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/search/approximate-count \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "jql": "project = HSP"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/search/approximate-count`

Provide an estimated count of the issues that match the [JQL](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/egORLQ). Recent updates might not be immediately visible in the returned output. This endpoint requires JQL to be bounded.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Issues are included in the response where the user has:

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project containing the issue.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "jql": "project = HSP"
}
```

<h3 id="count-issues-using-jql-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[JQLCountRequestBean](#schemajqlcountrequestbean)|true|A JSON object containing the search request.|
|» jql|body|string|false|A [JQL](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/egORLQ) expression. For performance reasons, this parameter requires a bounded query. A bounded query is a query with a search restriction.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"count\":153}"
```

<h3 id="count-issues-using-jql-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[JQLCountResultsBean](#schemajqlcountresultsbean)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the JQL query cannot be parsed.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Search for issues using JQL enhanced search (GET)

<a id="opIdsearchAndReconsileIssuesUsingJql"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/search/jql \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/search/jql`

Searches for issues using [JQL](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/egORLQ). Recent updates might not be immediately visible in the returned search results. If you need [read-after-write](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/search-and-reconcile/) consistency, you can utilize the `reconcileIssues` parameter to ensure stronger consistency assurances. This operation can be accessed anonymously.

If the JQL query expression is too large to be encoded as a query parameter, use the [POST](#api-rest-api-3-search-post) version of this resource.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Issues are included in the response where the user has:

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project containing the issue.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

<h3 id="search-for-issues-using-jql-enhanced-search-get-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|jql|query|string|false|A [JQL](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/egORLQ) expression. For performance reasons, this parameter requires a bounded query. A bounded query is a query with a search restriction.<br><br> *  Example of an unbounded query: `order by key desc`.<br> *  Example of a bounded query: `assignee = currentUser() order by key`.<br><br>Additionally, `orderBy` clause can contain a maximum of 7 fields.|
|nextPageToken|query|string|false|The token for a page to fetch that is not the first page. The first page has a `nextPageToken` of `null`. Use the `nextPageToken` to fetch the next page of issues.<br><br>Note: The `nextPageToken` field is **not included** in the response for the last page, indicating there is no next page.|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page. To manage page size, API may return fewer items per page where a large number of fields or properties are requested. The greatest number of items returned per page is achieved when requesting `id` or `key` only. It returns max 5000 issues.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A list of fields to return for each issue, use it to retrieve a subset of fields. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `*all` Returns all fields.<br> *  `*navigable` Returns navigable fields.<br> *  `id` Returns only issue IDs.<br> *  Any issue field, prefixed with a minus to exclude.<br><br>The default is `id`.<br><br>Examples:<br><br> *  `summary,comment` Returns only the summary and comments fields only.<br> *  `-description` Returns all navigable (default) fields except description.<br> *  `*all,-comment` Returns all fields except comments.<br><br>Multiple `fields` parameters can be included in a request.<br><br>Note: By default, this resource returns IDs only. This differs from [GET issue](#api-rest-api-3-issue-issueIdOrKey-get) where the default is all fields.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information about issues in the response. Note that, unlike the majority of instances where `expand` is specified, `expand` is defined as a comma-delimited string of values. The expand options are:<br><br> *  `renderedFields` Returns field values rendered in HTML format.<br> *  `names` Returns the display name of each field.<br> *  `schema` Returns the schema describing a field type.<br> *  `transitions` Returns all possible transitions for the issue.<br> *  `operations` Returns all possible operations for the issue.<br> *  `editmeta` Returns information about how each field can be edited.<br> *  `changelog` Returns a list of recent updates to an issue, sorted by date, starting from the most recent.<br> *  `versionedRepresentations` Instead of `fields`, returns `versionedRepresentations` a JSON array containing each version of a field's value, with the highest numbered item representing the most recent version.<br><br>Examples: `"names,changelog"` Returns the display name of each field as well as a list of recent updates to an issue.|
|properties|query|[string]|false|A list of up to 5 issue properties to include in the results. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list.|
|fieldsByKeys|query|boolean|false|Reference fields by their key (rather than ID). The default is `false`.|
|failFast|query|boolean|false|Fail this request early if we can't retrieve all field data.|
|reconcileIssues|query|[integer(int64)]|false|Strong consistency issue ids to be reconciled with search results. Accepts max 50 ids. This list of ids should be consistent with each paginated request across different pages.|
|includeArchivedProjects|query|boolean|false|Whether to also return issues that belong to [archived projects](https://support.atlassian.com/jira-cloud-administration/docs/archive-a-project/). Issues in archived projects are excluded by default. Setting this to `true` returns them alongside issues from active projects; the *Browse projects* permission is still required on the archived project. The default is `false`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

## Search for issues using JQL enhanced search (POST)

<a id="opIdsearchAndReconsileIssuesUsingJqlPost"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/search/jql \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "expand": "string",
    "fields": [
      "string"
    ],
    "fieldsByKeys": true,
    "includeArchivedProjects": true,
    "jql": "string",
    "maxResults": 50,
    "nextPageToken": "string",
    "properties": [
      "string"
    ],
    "reconcileIssues": [
      0
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/search/jql`

Searches for issues using [JQL](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/egORLQ). Recent updates might not be immediately visible in the returned search results. If you need [read-after-write](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/search-and-reconcile/) consistency, you can utilize the `reconcileIssues` parameter to ensure stronger consistency assurances. This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Issues are included in the response where the user has:

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project containing the issue.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expand": "string",
  "fields": [
    "string"
  ],
  "fieldsByKeys": true,
  "includeArchivedProjects": true,
  "jql": "string",
  "maxResults": 50,
  "nextPageToken": "string",
  "properties": [
    "string"
  ],
  "reconcileIssues": [
    0
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="search-for-issues-using-jql-enhanced-search-post-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SearchAndReconcileRequestBean](#schemasearchandreconcilerequestbean)|true|none|
|» expand|body|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information about issues in the response. Note that, unlike the majority of instances where `expand` is specified, `expand` is defined as a comma-delimited string of values. The expand options are:<br><br> *  `renderedFields` Returns field values rendered in HTML format.<br> *  `names` Returns the display name of each field.<br> *  `schema` Returns the schema describing a field type.<br> *  `transitions` Returns all possible transitions for the issue.<br> *  `operations` Returns all possible operations for the issue.<br> *  `editmeta` Returns information about how each field can be edited.<br> *  `changelog` Returns a list of recent updates to an issue, sorted by date, starting from the most recent.<br> *  `versionedRepresentations` Instead of `fields`, returns `versionedRepresentations` a JSON array containing each version of a field's value, with the highest numbered item representing the most recent version.<br><br>Examples: `"names,changelog"` Returns the display name of each field as well as a list of recent updates to an issue.|
|» fields|body|[string]|false|A list of fields to return for each issue. Use it to retrieve a subset of fields. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `*all` Returns all fields.<br> *  `*navigable` Returns navigable fields.<br> *  `id` Returns only issue IDs.<br> *  Any issue field, prefixed with a dash to exclude.<br><br>The default is `id`.<br><br>Examples:<br><br> *  `summary,comment` Returns the summary and comments fields only.<br> *  `*all,-comment` Returns all fields except comments.<br><br>Multiple `fields` parameters can be included in a request.<br><br>Note: By default, this resource returns IDs only. This differs from [GET issue](#api-rest-api-3-issue-issueIdOrKey-get) where the default is all fields.|
|» fieldsByKeys|body|boolean|false|Reference fields by their key (rather than ID). The default is `false`.|
|» includeArchivedProjects|body|boolean|false|Whether to also return issues that belong to archived projects. Archived projects are excluded by default. Requires *Browse projects* permission on the archived project. The default is `false`.|
|» jql|body|string|false|A [JQL](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/egORLQ) expression. For performance reasons, this parameter requires a bounded query. A bounded query is a query with a search restriction.<br><br> *  Example of an unbounded query: `order by key desc`.<br> *  Example of a bounded query: `assignee = currentUser() order by key`.<br><br>Additionally, `orderBy` clause can contain a maximum of 7 fields.|
|» maxResults|body|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page. To manage page size, API may return fewer items per page where a large number of fields are requested. The greatest number of items returned per page is achieved when requesting `id` or `key` only. It returns max 5000 issues.|
|» nextPageToken|body|string|false|The token for a page to fetch that is not the first page. The first page has a `nextPageToken` of `null`. Use the `nextPageToken` to fetch the next page of issues.|
|» properties|body|[string]|false|A list of up to 5 issue properties to include in the results. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list.|
|» reconcileIssues|body|[integer(int64)]|false|Strong consistency issue ids to be reconciled with search results. Accepts max 50 ids. This list of ids should be consistent with each paginated request across different pages.|

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-security-level">Issue security level</h1>

This resource represents issue security levels. Use it to obtain the details of any issue security level. For more information about issue security levels, see [Configuring issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg).

## Get issue security level members by issue security scheme

<a id="opIdgetIssueSecurityLevelMembers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes/0/members \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes/{issueSecuritySchemeId}/members`

Returns issue security level members.

Only issue security level members in context of classic projects are returned.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-issue-security-level-members-by-issue-security-scheme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueSecuritySchemeId|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the issue security scheme. Use the [Get issue security schemes](#api-rest-api-3-issuesecurityschemes-get) operation to get a list of issue security scheme IDs.|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|issueSecurityLevelId|query|[string]|false|The list of issue security level IDs. To include multiple issue security levels separate IDs with ampersand: `issueSecurityLevelId=10000&issueSecurityLevelId=10001`.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use expand to include additional information in the response. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `all` Returns all expandable information.<br> *  `field` Returns information about the custom field granted the permission.<br> *  `group` Returns information about the group that is granted the permission.<br> *  `projectRole` Returns information about the project role granted the permission.<br> *  `user` Returns information about the user who is granted the permission.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"isLast\":true,\"maxResults\":100,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":3,\"values\":[{\"id\":10000,\"issueSecurityLevelId\":10020,\"holder\":{\"expand\":\"user\",\"type\":\"user\",\"user\":{\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"active\":true,\"avatarUrls\":{\"16x16\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=16&s=16\",\"24x24\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=24&s=24\",\"32x32\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=32&s=32\",\"48x48\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=48&s=48\"},\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"emailAddress\":\"mia@example.com\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/user?accountId=5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"timeZone\":\"Australia/Sydney\"}}},{\"id\":10001,\"issueSecurityLevelId\":10020,\"holder\":{\"expand\":\"group\",\"parameter\":\"jira-core-users\",\"type\":\"group\",\"value\":\"9c559b11-6c5d-4f96-992c-a746cabab28b\"}},{\"id\":10002,\"issueSecurityLevelId\":10021,\"holder\":{\"type\":\"assignee\"}}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-issue-security-level-members-by-issue-security-scheme-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PageBeanIssueSecurityLevelMember](#schemapagebeanissuesecuritylevelmember)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if no issue security level members are found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

## Get issue security level

<a id="opIdgetIssueSecurityLevel"></a>

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/securitylevel/string \
```

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

```json
"{\"description\":\"Only the reporter and internal staff can see this issue.\",\"id\":\"10021\",\"name\":\"Reporter Only\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/securitylevel/10021\"}"
```

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-security-schemes">Issue security schemes</h1>

This resource represents issue security schemes. Use it to get an issue security scheme or a list of issue security schemes.

Issue security schemes control which users or groups of users can view an issue. When an issue security scheme is associated with a project, its security levels can be applied to issues in that project. Sub-tasks also inherit the security level of their parent issue.

## Get issue security schemes

<a id="opIdgetIssueSecuritySchemes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes`

Returns all [issue security schemes](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg).

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"issueSecuritySchemes\":[{\"defaultSecurityLevelId\":10021,\"description\":\"Description for the default issue security scheme\",\"id\":10000,\"name\":\"Default Issue Security Scheme\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes/10000\"}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-issue-security-schemes-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[SecuritySchemes](#schemasecurityschemes)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to administer issue security schemes.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )
</aside>

## Create issue security scheme

<a id="opIdcreateIssueSecurityScheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Newly created issue security scheme",
    "levels": [
      {
        "description": "Newly created level",
        "isDefault": true,
        "members": [
          {
            "parameter": "administrators",
            "type": "group"
          }
        ],
        "name": "New level"
      }
    ],
    "name": "New security scheme"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes`

Creates a security scheme with security scheme levels and levels' members. You can create up to 100 security scheme levels and security scheme levels' members per request.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Newly created issue security scheme",
  "levels": [
    {
      "description": "Newly created level",
      "isDefault": true,
      "members": [
        {
          "parameter": "administrators",
          "type": "group"
        }
      ],
      "name": "New level"
    }
  ],
  "name": "New security scheme"
}
```

<h3 id="create-issue-security-scheme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateIssueSecuritySchemeDetails](#schemacreateissuesecurityschemedetails)|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the issue security scheme.|
|» levels|body|[[SecuritySchemeLevelBean](#schemasecurityschemelevelbean)]|false|The list of scheme levels which should be added to the security scheme.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the issue security scheme. Must be unique (case-insensitive).|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
"{\"id\":\"10001\"}"
```

> 400 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"The length of the description must not exceed 4,000 characters.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errorMessages": [
    "string"
  ],
  "errors": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "status": 0
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"You are not authorized to perform this action. Administrator privileges are required.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

<h3 id="create-issue-security-scheme-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returned if the request is successful.|[SecuritySchemeId](#schemasecurityschemeid)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|[ErrorCollection](#schemaerrorcollection)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|[ErrorCollection](#schemaerrorcollection)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user doesn't have the necessary permission.|[ErrorCollection](#schemaerrorcollection)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

## Get issue security levels

<a id="opIdgetSecurityLevels"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes/level \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes/level`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of issue security levels.

Only issue security levels in the context of classic projects are returned.

Filtering using IDs is inclusive: if you specify both security scheme IDs and level IDs, the result will include both specified issue security levels and all issue security levels from the specified schemes.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-issue-security-levels-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startAt|query|string|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|string|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|id|query|[string]|false|The list of issue security scheme level IDs. To include multiple issue security levels, separate IDs with an ampersand: `id=10000&id=10001`.|
|schemeId|query|[string]|false|The list of issue security scheme IDs. To include multiple issue security schemes, separate IDs with an ampersand: `schemeId=10000&schemeId=10001`.|
|onlyDefault|query|boolean|false|When set to true, returns multiple default levels for each security scheme containing a default. If you provide scheme and level IDs not associated with the default, returns an empty page. The default value is false.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"isLast\":true,\"maxResults\":50,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":1,\"values\":[{\"description\":\"Only the reporter and internal staff can see this issue.\",\"id\":\"10021\",\"isDefault\":true,\"issueSecuritySchemeId\":\"10001\",\"name\":\"Reporter Only\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuesecurityscheme/level?id=10021\"}]}"
```

> 400 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"-1000 is not a valid value. id must be zero or a positive integer.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errorMessages": [
    "string"
  ],
  "errors": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "status": 0
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"You are not authorized to perform this action. Administrator privileges are required.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

<h3 id="get-issue-security-levels-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PageBeanSecurityLevel](#schemapagebeansecuritylevel)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|[ErrorCollection](#schemaerrorcollection)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|[ErrorCollection](#schemaerrorcollection)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user doesn't have the necessary permission.|[ErrorCollection](#schemaerrorcollection)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes/level/default \
```

## Associate security scheme to project

```bash

      }

    "schemeId": "20000"
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes/project`

Associates an issue security scheme with a project and remaps security levels of issues to the new levels, if provided.

This operation is [asynchronous](#async). Follow the `location` link in the response to determine the status of the task and use [Get task](#api-rest-api-3-task-taskId-get) to obtain subsequent updates.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "oldToNewSecurityLevelMappings": [
    {

      "oldLevelId": "30000"
    }
  ],
  "projectId": "10000",
  "schemeId": "20000"
}
```

|» schemeId|body|string|true|The ID of the issue security scheme. Providing null will clear the association with the issue security scheme.|

## Search issue security schemes

<a id="opIdsearchSecuritySchemes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes/search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes/search`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of issue security schemes.  
If you specify the project ID parameter, the result will contain issue security schemes and related project IDs you filter by. Use \{@link IssueSecuritySchemeResource\#searchProjectsUsingSecuritySchemes(String, String, Set, Set)\} to obtain all projects related to scheme.

Only issue security schemes in the context of classic projects are returned.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="search-issue-security-schemes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startAt|query|string|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|string|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|id|query|[string]|false|The list of issue security scheme IDs. To include multiple issue security scheme IDs, separate IDs with an ampersand: `id=10000&id=10001`.|
|projectId|query|[string]|false|The list of project IDs. To include multiple project IDs, separate IDs with an ampersand: `projectId=10000&projectId=10001`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"id\":10000,\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuesecurityscheme/10000\",\"name\":\"Default scheme\",\"description\":\"Default scheme description\",\"defaultLevel\":10001,\"projectIds\":[10002]}"
```

> 400 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"-1000 is not a valid value. id must be zero or a positive integer.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 403 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"You are not authorized to perform this action. Administrator privileges are required.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

<h3 id="search-issue-security-schemes-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PageBeanSecuritySchemeWithProjects](#schemapagebeansecurityschemewithprojects)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user doesn't have the necessary permission.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-type-properties">Issue type properties</h1>

This resource represents [issue type](#api-group-Issue-types) properties, which provides for storing custom data against an issue type. Use it to get, create, and delete issue type properties as well as obtain the keys of all properties on a issues type. Issue type properties are a type of [entity property](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/jira-entity-properties/).

## Get issue type property keys

<a id="opIdgetIssueTypePropertyKeys"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuetype/string/properties \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issuetype/{issueTypeId}/properties`

Returns all the [issue type property](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/storing-data-without-a-database/#a-id-jira-entity-properties-a-jira-entity-properties) keys of the issue type.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg) to get the property keys of any issue type.
 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) to get the property keys of any issue types associated with the projects the user has permission to browse.

<h3 id="get-issue-type-property-keys-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueTypeId|path|string|true|The ID of the issue type.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"keys\":[{\"key\":\"issue.support\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/EX-2/properties/issue.support\"}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-issue-type-property-keys-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PropertyKeys](#schemapropertykeys)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the issue type ID is invalid.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  the issue type is not found.<br> *  the user does not have the required permissions.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Get issue type property

<a id="opIdgetIssueTypeProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuetype/string/properties/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issuetype/{issueTypeId}/properties/{propertyKey}`

Returns the key and value of the [issue type property](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/storing-data-without-a-database/#a-id-jira-entity-properties-a-jira-entity-properties).

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg) to get the details of any issue type.
 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) to get the details of any issue types associated with the projects the user has permission to browse.

<h3 id="get-issue-type-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueTypeId|path|string|true|The ID of the issue type.|
|propertyKey|path|string|true|The key of the property. Use [Get issue type property keys](#api-rest-api-3-issuetype-issueTypeId-properties-get) to get a list of all issue type property keys.|

> Example responses
