```json
"{\"key\":\"issue.support\",\"value\":{\"system.conversation.id\":\"b1bf38be-5e94-4b40-a3b8-9278735ee1e6\",\"system.support.time\":\"1m\"}}"
```

<h3 id="get-issue-type-property-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[EntityProperty](#schemaentityproperty)|

|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the issue type or property is not found or the user does not have the required permissions.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Set issue type property

<a id="opIdsetIssueTypeProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuetype/string/properties/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "number": 5,
    "string": "string-value"
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/issuetype/{issueTypeId}/properties/{propertyKey}`

Creates or updates the value of the [issue type property](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/storing-data-without-a-database/#a-id-jira-entity-properties-a-jira-entity-properties). Use this resource to store and update data against an issue type.

The value of the request body must be a [valid](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4627), non-empty JSON blob. The maximum length is 32768 characters.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "number": 5,
  "string": "string-value"
}
```

<h3 id="set-issue-type-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueTypeId|path|string|true|The ID of the issue type.|
|propertyKey|path|string|true|The key of the issue type property. The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|body|body|object|true|The value of the property. The value has to be a valid, non-empty [JSON](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4627) value. The maximum length of the property value is 32768 bytes.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
null
```

> 201 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="set-issue-type-property-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the issue type property is updated.|Inline|
|201|Created|Returned if the issue type property is created.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if:<br><br> *  the issue type ID is invalid.<br> *  a property value is not provided.<br> *  the property value JSON content is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to modify the issue type.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  the issue type is not found.<br> *  the user does not have the permission view the issue type.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-type-schemes">Issue type schemes</h1>

This resource represents issue type schemes in classic projects. Use it to:

 *  get issue type schemes and a list of the projects that use them.
 *  associate issue type schemes with projects.
 *  add issue types to issue type schemes.
 *  delete issue types from issue type schemes.
 *  create, update, and delete issue type schemes.
 *  change the order of issue types in issue type schemes.

## Get all issue type schemes

<a id="opIdgetAllIssueTypeSchemes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuetypescheme \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issuetypescheme`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of issue type schemes.

Only issue type schemes used in classic projects are returned.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-all-issue-type-schemes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|id|query|[integer(int64)]|false|The list of issue type schemes IDs. To include multiple IDs, provide an ampersand-separated list. For example, `id=10000&id=10001`.|
|orderBy|query|string|false|[Order](#ordering) the results by a field:<br><br> *  `name` Sorts by issue type scheme name.<br> *  `id` Sorts by issue type scheme ID.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information in the response. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `projects` For each issue type schemes, returns information about the projects the issue type scheme is assigned to.<br> *  `issueTypes` For each issue type schemes, returns information about the issueTypes the issue type scheme have.|
|queryString|query|string|false|String used to perform a case-insensitive partial match with issue type scheme name.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|orderBy|name|
|orderBy|-name|
|orderBy|+name|
|orderBy|id|
|orderBy|-id|
|orderBy|+id|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"isLast\":true,\"maxResults\":100,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":3,\"values\":[{\"id\":\"10000\",\"name\":\"Default Issue Type Scheme\",\"description\":\"Default issue type scheme is the list of global issue types. All newly created issue types will automatically be added to this scheme.\",\"defaultIssueTypeId\":\"10003\",\"isDefault\":true},{\"id\":\"10001\",\"name\":\"SUP: Kanban Issue Type Scheme\",\"description\":\"A collection of issue types suited to use in a kanban style project.\",\"projects\":{\"isLast\":true,\"maxResults\":100,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":1,\"values\":[{\"avatarUrls\":{\"16x16\":\"secure/projectavatar?size=xsmall&pid=10000\",\"24x24\":\"secure/projectavatar?size=small&pid=10000\",\"32x32\":\"secure/projectavatar?size=medium&pid=10000\",\"48x48\":\"secure/projectavatar?size=large&pid=10000\"},\"id\":\"10000\",\"key\":\"EX\",\"name\":\"Example\",\"projectCategory\":{\"description\":\"Project category description\",\"id\":\"10000\",\"name\":\"A project category\"},\"projectTypeKey\":\"ProjectTypeKey{key='software'}\",\"self\":\"project/EX\",\"simplified\":false}]}},{\"id\":\"10002\",\"name\":\"HR: Scrum issue type scheme\",\"description\":\"\",\"defaultIssueTypeId\":\"10004\",\"issueTypes\":{\"isLast\":true,\"maxResults\":100,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":1,\"values\":[{\"description\":\"Improvement Issue Type\",\"hierarchyLevel\":-1,\"iconUrl\":\"www.example.com\",\"id\":\"1000L\",\"name\":\"Improvements\",\"subtask\":true}]}}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-all-issue-type-schemes-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PageBeanIssueTypeScheme](#schemapagebeanissuetypescheme)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the required permissions.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )

## Create issue type scheme

<a id="opIdcreateIssueTypeScheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuetypescheme \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "defaultIssueTypeId": "10002",
    "description": "A collection of issue types suited to use in a kanban style project.",
    "issueTypeIds": [
      "10001",
      "10002",
      "10003"
    ],
    "name": "Kanban Issue Type Scheme"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/issuetypescheme`

Creates an issue type scheme.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "defaultIssueTypeId": "10002",
  "description": "A collection of issue types suited to use in a kanban style project.",
  "issueTypeIds": [
    "10001",
    "10002",
    "10003"
  ],
  "name": "Kanban Issue Type Scheme"
}
```

<h3 id="create-issue-type-scheme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IssueTypeSchemeDetails](#schemaissuetypeschemedetails)|true|none|
|» defaultIssueTypeId|body|string|false|The ID of the default issue type of the issue type scheme. This ID must be included in `issueTypeIds`.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the issue type scheme. The maximum length is 4000 characters.|
|» issueTypeIds|body|[string]|true|The list of issue types IDs of the issue type scheme. At least one standard issue type ID is required.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the issue type scheme. The name must be unique. The maximum length is 255 characters.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
"{\"issueTypeSchemeId\":\"10010\"}"
```

> 400 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"The default issue type ID has to be present in issue type IDs list.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 403 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"Only Jira administrators can access issue type schemes.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 409 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"The name is used by another scheme.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

<h3 id="create-issue-type-scheme-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returned if the request is successful.|[IssueTypeSchemeID](#schemaissuetypeschemeid)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the required permissions.|None|
|409|Conflict|Returned if the scheme name is used by another scheme.|None|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )

## Assign issue type scheme to project

<a id="opIdassignIssueTypeSchemeToProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuetypescheme/project \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "issueTypeSchemeId": "10000",
    "projectId": "10000"
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/issuetypescheme/project`

Assigns an issue type scheme to a project.

If any issues in the project are assigned issue types not present in the new scheme, the operation will fail. To complete the assignment those issues must be updated to use issue types in the new scheme.

Issue type schemes can only be assigned to classic projects.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "issueTypeSchemeId": "10000",
  "projectId": "10000"
}
```

## Delete issue type scheme

<a id="opIddeleteIssueTypeScheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuetypescheme/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /rest/api/3/issuetypescheme/{issueTypeSchemeId}`

Deletes an issue type scheme.

Only issue type schemes used in classic projects can be deleted. Only issue type schemes not associated with a project can be deleted

A validation error will be returned if the specified scheme is associated with one or more projects. Use [Get issue type scheme API](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issue-type-schemes/#api-rest-api-3-issuetypescheme-get) (with the projects expand, and id query parameter) to get a list of projects. Then, use [Assign issue type scheme to project API](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issue-type-schemes/#api-rest-api-3-issuetypescheme-project-put) to associate all projects to another scheme before deleting.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="delete-issue-type-scheme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueTypeSchemeId|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the issue type scheme.|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
null
```

> 400 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"The default issue type scheme can't be removed.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 403 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"Only Jira administrators can access issue type schemes.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 404 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"The issue type scheme was not found.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

<h3 id="delete-issue-type-scheme-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the required permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the issue type scheme is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

## Change order of issue types

<a id="opIdreorderIssueTypesInIssueTypeScheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuetypescheme/0/issuetype/move \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "after": "10008",
    "issueTypeIds": [
      "10001",
      "10004",
      "10002"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/issuetypescheme/{issueTypeSchemeId}/issuetype/move`

Changes the order of issue types in an issue type scheme.

The request body parameters must meet the following requirements:

 *  all of the issue types must belong to the issue type scheme.
 *  either `after` or `position` must be provided.
 *  the issue type in `after` must not be in the issue type list.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "after": "10008",
  "issueTypeIds": [
    "10001",
    "10004",
    "10002"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="change-order-of-issue-types-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueTypeSchemeId|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the issue type scheme.|
|body|body|[OrderOfIssueTypes](#schemaorderofissuetypes)|true|none|
|» after|body|string|false|The ID of the issue type to place the moved issue types after. Required if `position` isn't provided.|
|» issueTypeIds|body|[string]|true|A list of the issue type IDs to move. The order of the issue type IDs in the list is the order they are given after the move.|
|» position|body|string|false|The position the issue types should be moved to. Required if `after` isn't provided.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» position|First|
|» position|Last|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
null
```

> 400 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"The issue type scheme does not include some of the specified issue types. Issue type IDs missing from the scheme are:  10007, 10008\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 403 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"Only Jira administrators can access issue type schemes.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 404 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"The issue type scheme was not found.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

<h3 id="change-order-of-issue-types-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|204|No Content|Returned if the request is successful.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-type-screen-schemes">Issue type screen schemes</h1>

This resource represents issue type screen schemes. Use it to:

 *  get issue type screen schemes and a list of the projects that use them.
 *  create issue type screen schemes.
 *  update issue type screen schemes.
 *  delete issue type screen schemes.
 *  associate issue type screen schemes with projects.
 *  append issue type to screen scheme mappings to issue type screen schemes.
 *  remove issue type to screen scheme mappings from issue type screen schemes.
 *  update default screen scheme of issue type screen scheme.

## Get issue type screen schemes

<a id="opIdgetIssueTypeScreenSchemes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuetypescreenscheme \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issuetypescreenscheme`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of issue type screen schemes.

Only issue type screen schemes used in classic projects are returned.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-issue-type-screen-schemes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|id|query|[integer(int64)]|false|The list of issue type screen scheme IDs. To include multiple IDs, provide an ampersand-separated list. For example, `id=10000&id=10001`.|
|queryString|query|string|false|String used to perform a case-insensitive partial match with issue type screen scheme name.|
|orderBy|query|string|false|[Order](#ordering) the results by a field:<br><br> *  `name` Sorts by issue type screen scheme name.<br> *  `id` Sorts by issue type screen scheme ID.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information in the response. This parameter accepts `projects` that, for each issue type screen schemes, returns information about the projects the issue type screen scheme is assigned to.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|orderBy|name|
|orderBy|-name|
|orderBy|+name|
|orderBy|id|
|orderBy|-id|
|orderBy|+id|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"isLast\":true,\"maxResults\":100,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":2,\"values\":[{\"id\":\"1\",\"name\":\"Default Issue Type Screen Scheme\",\"description\":\"The default issue type screen scheme\"},{\"id\":\"10000\",\"name\":\"Office issue type screen scheme\",\"description\":\"Managing office projects\",\"projects\":{\"isLast\":true,\"maxResults\":100,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":1,\"values\":[{\"avatarUrls\":{\"16x16\":\"secure/projectavatar?size=xsmall&pid=10000\",\"24x24\":\"secure/projectavatar?size=small&pid=10000\",\"32x32\":\"secure/projectavatar?size=medium&pid=10000\",\"48x48\":\"secure/projectavatar?size=large&pid=10000\"},\"id\":\"10000\",\"key\":\"EX\",\"name\":\"Example\",\"projectCategory\":{\"description\":\"Project category description\",\"id\":\"10000\",\"name\":\"A project category\"},\"projectTypeKey\":\"ProjectTypeKey{key='software'}\",\"self\":\"project/EX\",\"simplified\":false}]}}]}"
```

|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid.|None|

`POST /rest/api/3/issuetypescreenscheme`

Creates an issue type screen scheme.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "issueTypeMappings": [
    {
      "issueTypeId": "default",
      "screenSchemeId": "10001"
    },
    {
      "issueTypeId": "10001",
      "screenSchemeId": "10002"
    },
    {
      "issueTypeId": "10002",

    }
  ],
```

|» issueTypeMappings|body|[[IssueTypeScreenSchemeMapping](#schemaissuetypescreenschememapping)]|true|The IDs of the screen schemes for the issue type IDs and *default*. A *default* entry is required to create an issue type screen scheme, it defines the mapping for all issue types without a screen scheme.|

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-types">Issue types</h1>

This resource represents issues types. Use it to:

 *  get, create, update, and delete issue types.
 *  get all issue types for a user.
 *  get alternative issue types.
 *  set an avatar for an issue type.

## Get all issue types for user

<a id="opIdgetIssueAllTypes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuetype \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issuetype`

Returns all issue types.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Issue types are only returned as follows:

 *  if the user has the *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg), all issue types are returned.
 *  if the user has the *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for one or more projects, the issue types associated with the projects the user has permission to browse are returned.
 *  if the user is anonymous then they will be able to access projects with the *Browse projects* for anonymous users
 *  if the user authentication is incorrect they will fall back to anonymous

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"[{\"avatarId\":1,\"description\":\"A task that needs to be done.\",\"hierarchyLevel\":0,\"iconUrl\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/secure/viewavatar?size=xsmall&avatarId=10299&avatarType=issuetype\\\",\",\"id\":\"3\",\"name\":\"Task\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issueType/3\",\"subtask\":false},{\"avatarId\":10002,\"description\":\"A problem with the software.\",\"entityId\":\"9d7dd6f7-e8b6-4247-954b-7b2c9b2a5ba2\",\"hierarchyLevel\":0,\"iconUrl\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/secure/viewavatar?size=xsmall&avatarId=10316&avatarType=issuetype\\\",\",\"id\":\"1\",\"name\":\"Bug\",\"scope\":{\"project\":{\"id\":\"10000\"},\"type\":\"PROJECT\"},\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issueType/1\",\"subtask\":false}]"
```

<h3 id="get-all-issue-types-for-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-all-issue-types-for-user-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[IssueTypeDetails](#schemaissuetypedetails)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Create issue type

<a id="opIdcreateIssueType"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuetype \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "description",
    "name": "name",
    "type": "standard"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/issuetype`

Creates an issue type.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "description",
  "name": "name",
  "type": "standard"
}
```

<h3 id="create-issue-type-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IssueTypeCreateBean](#schemaissuetypecreatebean)|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the issue type.|
|» hierarchyLevel|body|integer(int32)|false|The hierarchy level of the issue type. Use:<br><br> *  `-1` for Subtask.<br> *  `0` for Base.<br><br>Defaults to `0`.|
|» name|body|string|true|The unique name for the issue type. The maximum length is 60 characters.|
|» type|body|string|false|Deprecated. Use `hierarchyLevel` instead. See the [deprecation notice](https://community.developer.atlassian.com/t/deprecation-of-the-epic-link-parent-link-and-other-related-fields-in-rest-apis-and-webhooks/54048) for details.<br><br>Whether the issue type is `subtype` or `standard`. Defaults to `standard`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|subtask|
|» type|standard|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "avatarId": 0,
  "description": "string",
  "entityId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "hierarchyLevel": 0,
  "iconUrl": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "scope": {
    "project": {
      "avatarUrls": {
        "16x16": "http://example.com",
        "24x24": "http://example.com",
        "32x32": "http://example.com",
        "48x48": "http://example.com"
      },
      "id": "string",
      "key": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "projectCategory": {
        "description": "string",
        "id": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "self": "string"
      },
      "projectTypeKey": "software",
      "self": "string",
      "simplified": true
    },
    "type": "PROJECT"
  },
  "self": "string",
  "subtask": true
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|201|Created|Returned if the request is successful.|[IssueTypeDetails](#schemaissuetypedetails)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid because:<br><br> *  no content is sent.<br> *  the issue type name exceeds 60 characters.<br> *  a subtask issue type is requested on an instance where subtasks are disabled.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|
|409|Conflict|Returned if the issue type name is in use or creation conflicts with another request.|None|

## Delete issue type

<a id="opIddeleteIssueType"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /rest/api/3/issuetype/{id}`

Deletes the issue type. If the issue type is in use, all uses are updated with the alternative issue type (`alternativeIssueTypeId`). A list of alternative issue types are obtained from the [Get alternative issue types](#api-rest-api-3-issuetype-id-alternatives-get) resource.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue type.|
|alternativeIssueTypeId|query|string|false|The ID of the replacement issue type.|

<h3 id="delete-issue-type-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the request is successful.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if any issues cannot be updated with the alternative issue type.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  the issue type is in use and an alternative issue type is not specified.<br> *  the issue type or alternative issue type is not found.|None|
|409|Conflict|Returned if the issue type is in use and:<br><br> *  also specified as the alternative issue type.<br> *  is a *standard* issue type and the alternative issue type is a *subtask*.|None|
|423|Locked|Returned if a resource related to deletion is locked.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

## Load issue type avatar

<a id="opIdcreateIssueTypeAvatar"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuetype/string/avatar2?size=0' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: */*' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /rest/api/3/issuetype/{id}/avatar2`

Loads an avatar for the issue type.

Specify the avatar's local file location in the body of the request. Also, include the following headers:

 *  `X-Atlassian-Token: no-check` To prevent XSRF protection blocking the request, for more information see [Special Headers](#special-request-headers).
 *  `Content-Type: image/image type` Valid image types are JPEG, GIF, or PNG.

For example:  
`curl --request POST \ --user email@example.com:<api_token> \ --header 'X-Atlassian-Token: no-check' \ --header 'Content-Type: image/< image_type>' \ --data-binary "<@/path/to/file/with/your/avatar>" \ --url 'https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuetype/{issueTypeId}'This`

The avatar is cropped to a square. If no crop parameters are specified, the square originates at the top left of the image. The length of the square's sides is set to the smaller of the height or width of the image.

The cropped image is then used to create avatars of 16x16, 24x24, 32x32, and 48x48 in size.

After creating the avatar, use [ Update issue type](#api-rest-api-3-issuetype-id-put) to set it as the issue type's displayed avatar.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="load-issue-type-avatar-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue type.|
|x|query|integer(int32)|false|The X coordinate of the top-left corner of the crop region.|
|y|query|integer(int32)|false|The Y coordinate of the top-left corner of the crop region.|
|size|query|integer(int32)|true|The length of each side of the crop region.|
|body|body|object|true|none|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
"{\"id\":\"1010\",\"isDeletable\":true,\"isSelected\":false,\"isSystemAvatar\":false}"
```

<h3 id="load-issue-type-avatar-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returned if the request is successful.|[Avatar](#schemaavatar)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if:<br><br> *  an image isn't included in the request.<br> *  the image type is unsupported.<br> *  the crop parameters extend the crop area beyond the edge of the image.<br> *  `cropSize` is missing.<br> *  the issue type ID is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the issue type is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-votes">Issue votes</h1>

This resource represents votes cast by users on an issue. Use it to get details of votes on an issue as well as cast and withdrawal votes.

## Get votes

<a id="opIdgetVotes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/string/votes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/votes`

Returns details about the votes on an issue.

This operation requires the **Allow users to vote on issues** option to be *ON*. This option is set in General configuration for Jira. See [Configuring Jira application options](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/uYXKM) for details.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is ini
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

Note that users with the necessary permissions for this operation but without the *View voters and watchers* project permissions are not returned details in the `voters` field.

<h3 id="get-votes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"hasVoted\":true,\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/issue/MKY-1/votes\",\"voters\":[{\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"accountType\":\"atlassian\",\"active\":false,\"avatarUrls\":{\"16x16\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=16&s=16\",\"24x24\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=24&s=24\",\"32x32\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=32&s=32\",\"48x48\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=48&s=48\"},\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"key\":\"\",\"name\":\"\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/user?accountId=5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\"}],\"votes\":24}"
```

`POST /rest/api/3/issue/watching`

## Add watcher

<a id="opIdaddWatcher"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/string/watchers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '"string"'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/watchers`

Adds a user as a watcher of an issue by passing the account ID of the user. For example, `"5b10ac8d82e05b22cc7d4ef5"`. If no user is specified the calling user is added.

This operation requires the **Allow users to watch issues** option to be *ON*. This option is set in General configuration for Jira. See [Configuring Jira application options](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/uYXKM) for details.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  To add users other than themselves to the watchlist, *Manage watcher list* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.

> Body parameter

```json
"string"
```

<h3 id="add-watcher-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|
|body|body|string|true|The account ID of the user. Note that username cannot be used due to privacy changes.|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="add-watcher-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the request is successful.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the permission to manage the watcher list.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the issue or the user is not found or the user does not have permission to view the issue.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: write:jira-work )
</aside>

Deletes a user as a watcher of an issue.

This operation requires the **Allow users to watch issues** option to be *ON*. This option is set in General configuration for Jira. See [Configuring Jira application options](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/uYXKM) for details.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-worklog-properties">Issue worklog properties</h1>

This resource represents [issue worklog](#api-group-Issue-worklogs) properties, which provides for storing custom data against an issue worklog. Use it to get, create, and delete issue worklog properties as well as obtain the keys of all properties on a issue worklog. Issue worklog properties are a type of [entity property](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/jira-entity-properties/).

## Get worklog property keys

<a id="opIdgetWorklogPropertyKeys"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/string/worklog/string/properties \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/worklog/{worklogId}/properties`

Returns the keys of all properties for a worklog.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  If the worklog has visibility restrictions, belongs to the group or has the role visibility is restricted to.

<h3 id="get-worklog-property-keys-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|
|worklogId|path|string|true|The ID of the worklog.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"keys\":[{\"key\":\"issue.support\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/EX-2/properties/issue.support\"}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-worklog-property-keys-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PropertyKeys](#schemapropertykeys)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the worklog ID is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  the issue or worklog is not found.<br> *  the user does not have permission to view the issue or worklog.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

`GET /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/worklog/{worklogId}/properties/{propertyKey}`

Returns the value of a worklog property.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  If the worklog has visibility restrictions, belongs to the group or has the role visibility is restricted to.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Set worklog property

<a id="opIdsetWorklogProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/string/worklog/string/properties/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d 'null'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/worklog/{worklogId}/properties/{propertyKey}`

Sets the value of a worklog property. Use this operation to store custom data against the worklog.

The value of the request body must be a [valid](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4627), non-empty JSON blob. The maximum length is 32768 characters.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  *Edit all worklogs*[ project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) to update any worklog or *Edit own worklogs* to update worklogs created by the user.
 *  If the worklog has visibility restrictions, belongs to the group or has the role visibility is restricted to.

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="set-worklog-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|
|worklogId|path|string|true|The ID of the worklog.|
|propertyKey|path|string|true|The key of the issue property. The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|body|body|object|true|The value of the property. The value has to be a valid, non-empty [JSON](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4627) value. The maximum length of the property value is 32768 bytes.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
null
```

> 201 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="set-worklog-property-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the worklog property is updated.|Inline|
|201|Created|Returned if the worklog property is created.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the worklog ID is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to edit the worklog.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  the issue or worklog is not found.<br> *  the user does not have permission to view the issue or worklog.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: write:jira-work )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issue-worklogs">Issue worklogs</h1>

This resource represents issue worklogs. Use it to:

 *  get, create, update, and delete worklogs.
 *  obtain lists of updated or deleted worklogs.

## Get issue worklogs

<a id="opIdgetIssueWorklog"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/string/worklog \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/worklog`

Returns worklogs for an issue (ordered by created time), starting from the oldest worklog or from the worklog started on or after a date and time.

Time tracking must be enabled in Jira, otherwise this operation returns an error. For more information, see [Configuring time tracking](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/qoXKM).

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Workloads are only returned where the user has:

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  If the worklog has visibility restrictions, belongs to the group or has the role visibility is restricted to.

<h3 id="get-issue-worklogs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|startedAfter|query|integer(int64)|false|The worklog start date and time, as a UNIX timestamp in milliseconds, after which worklogs are returned.|
|startedBefore|query|integer(int64)|false|The worklog start date and time, as a UNIX timestamp in milliseconds, before which worklogs are returned.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information about worklogs in the response. This parameter accepts`properties`, which returns worklog properties.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"maxResults\":1,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":1,\"worklogs\":[{\"author\":{\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"active\":false,\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/user?accountId=5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\"},\"comment\":{\"type\":\"doc\",\"version\":1,\"content\":[{\"type\":\"paragraph\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"I did some work here.\"}]}]},\"id\":\"100028\",\"issueId\":\"10002\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/10010/worklog/10000\",\"started\":\"2021-01-17T12:34:00.000+0000\",\"timeSpent\":\"3h 20m\",\"timeSpentSeconds\":12000,\"updateAuthor\":{\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"active\":false,\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/user?accountId=5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\"},\"updated\":\"2021-01-18T23:45:00.000+0000\",\"visibility\":{\"identifier\":\"276f955c-63d7-42c8-9520-92d01dca0625\",\"type\":\"group\",\"value\":\"jira-developers\"}}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-issue-worklogs-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful|[PageOfWorklogs](#schemapageofworklogs)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  the issue is not found or the user does not have permission to view the issue.<br> *  `startAt` or `maxResults` has non-numeric values.<br> *  time tracking is disabled.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Add worklog

<a id="opIdaddWorklog"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/string/worklog \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "comment": {
      "content": [
        {
          "content": [
            {
              "text": "I did some work here.",
              "type": "text"
            }
          ],
          "type": "paragraph"
        }
      ],
      "type": "doc",
      "version": 1
    },
    "started": "2021-01-17T12:34:00.000+0000",
    "timeSpentSeconds": 12000,
    "visibility": {
      "identifier": "276f955c-63d7-42c8-9520-92d01dca0625",
      "type": "group"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/worklog`

Adds a worklog to an issue.

Time tracking must be enabled in Jira, otherwise this operation returns an error. For more information, see [Configuring time tracking](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/qoXKM).

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* and *Work on issues* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": {
    "content": [
      {
        "content": [
          {
            "text": "I did some work here.",
            "type": "text"
          }
        ],
        "type": "paragraph"
      }
    ],
    "type": "doc",
    "version": 1
  },
  "started": "2021-01-17T12:34:00.000+0000",
  "timeSpentSeconds": 12000,
  "visibility": {
    "identifier": "276f955c-63d7-42c8-9520-92d01dca0625",
    "type": "group"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="add-worklog-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key the issue.|
|notifyUsers|query|boolean|false|Whether users watching the issue are notified by email.|
|adjustEstimate|query|string|false|Defines how to update the issue's time estimate, the options are:<br><br> *  `new` Sets the estimate to a specific value, defined in `newEstimate`.<br> *  `leave` Leaves the estimate unchanged.<br> *  `manual` Reduces the estimate by amount specified in `reduceBy`.<br> *  `auto` Reduces the estimate by the value of `timeSpent` in the worklog.|
|newEstimate|query|string|false|The value to set as the issue's remaining time estimate, as days (\#d), hours (\#h), or minutes (\#m or \#). For example, *2d*. Required when `adjustEstimate` is `new`.|
|reduceBy|query|string|false|The amount to reduce the issue's remaining estimate by, as days (\#d), hours (\#h), or minutes (\#m). For example, *2d*. Required when `adjustEstimate` is `manual`.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information about work logs in the response. This parameter accepts `properties`, which returns worklog properties.|
|overrideEditableFlag|query|boolean|false|Whether the worklog entry should be added to the issue even if the issue is not editable, because jira.issue.editable set to false or missing. For example, the issue is closed. Connect and Forge app users with *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg) can use this flag.|
|body|body|[Worklog](#schemaworklog)|true|none|
|» comment|body|object|false|A comment about the worklog in [Atlassian Document Format](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/apis/document/structure/). Optional when creating or updating a worklog.|
|» properties|body|[[EntityProperty](#schemaentityproperty)]|false|Details of properties for the worklog. Optional when creating or updating a worklog.|
|» started|body|string(date-time)|false|The datetime on which the worklog effort was started. Required when creating a worklog. Optional when updating a worklog.|
|» timeSpent|body|string|false|The time spent working on the issue as days (\#d), hours (\#h), or minutes (\#m or \#). Required when creating a worklog if `timeSpentSeconds` isn't provided. Optional when updating a worklog. Cannot be provided if `timeSpentSecond` is provided.|
|» timeSpentSeconds|body|integer(int64)|false|The time in seconds spent working on the issue. Required when creating a worklog if `timeSpent` isn't provided. Optional when updating a worklog. Cannot be provided if `timeSpent` is provided.|
|» visibility|body|object|false|Details about any restrictions in the visibility of the worklog. Optional when creating or updating a worklog.|
|» » identifier|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the group or the name of the role that visibility of this item is restricted to.|
|» » type|body|string|false|Whether visibility of this item is restricted to a group or role.|
|» » value|body|string|false|The name of the group or role that visibility of this item is restricted to. Please note that the name of a group is mutable, to reliably identify a group use `identifier`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|adjustEstimate|new|
|adjustEstimate|leave|
|adjustEstimate|manual|
|adjustEstimate|auto|
|» » type|group|
|» » type|role|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "author": {
    "accountId": "string",

      "16x16": "http://example.com",

    "value": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="add-worklog-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returned if the request is successful.|[Worklog](#schemaworklog)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if:<br><br> *  `adjustEstimate` is set to `new` but `newEstimate` is not provided or is invalid.<br> *  `adjustEstimate` is set to `manual` but `reduceBy` is not provided or is invalid.<br> *  the user does not have permission to add the worklog.<br> *  the request JSON is malformed.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the issue is not found or the user does not have permission to view it.|None|
|413|Payload Too Large|Returned if the per-issue limit has been breached for one of the following fields:<br><br> *  worklogs<br> *  attachments|None|

## Bulk delete worklogs

<a id="opIdbulkDeleteWorklogs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/string/worklog \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "ids": [
      1,
      2,
      5,
      10
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/worklog`

Deletes a list of worklogs from an issue. This is an experimental API with limitations:

 *  You can't delete more than 5000 worklogs at once.
 *  No notifications will be sent for deleted worklogs.

Time tracking must be enabled in Jira, otherwise this operation returns an error. For more information, see [Configuring time tracking](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/qoXKM).

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project containing the issue.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  *Delete all worklogs*[ project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) to delete any worklog.
 *  If any worklog has visibility restrictions, belongs to the group or has the role visibility is restricted to.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ids": [
    1,
    2,
    5,
    10
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-delete-worklogs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|
|adjustEstimate|query|string|false|Defines how to update the issue's time estimate, the options are:<br><br> *  `leave` Leaves the estimate unchanged.<br> *  `auto` Reduces the estimate by the aggregate value of `timeSpent` across all worklogs being deleted.|
|overrideEditableFlag|query|boolean|false|Whether the work log entries should be removed to the issue even if the issue is not editable, because jira.issue.editable set to false or missing. For example, the issue is closed. Connect and Forge app users with admin permission can use this flag.|
|body|body|[WorklogIdsRequestBean](#schemaworklogidsrequestbean)|true|A JSON object containing a list of worklog IDs.|
|» ids|body|[integer(int64)]|true|A list of worklog IDs.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|adjustEstimate|leave|
|adjustEstimate|auto|

<h3 id="bulk-delete-worklogs-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the bulk deletion request was partially successful, with a message indicating partial success.|None|
|204|No Content|Returned if the request is successful.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if:<br><br> *  `request` is not provided or is invalid<br> *  the user does not have permission to delete the worklogs<br> *  the number of worklogs being deleted exceeds the limit|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  the issue is not found or user does not have permission to view the issue<br> *  at least one of the worklogs is not associated with the provided issue<br> *  time tracking is disabled|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: write:jira-work )
</aside>

## Bulk move worklogs

<a id="opIdbulkMoveWorklogs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/string/worklog/move \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "ids": [
      1,
      2,
      5,
      10
    ],
    "issueIdOrKey": "ABC-1234"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/worklog/move`

Moves a list of worklogs from one issue to another. This is an experimental API with several limitations:

 *  You can't move more than 5000 worklogs at once.
 *  You can't move worklogs containing an attachment.
 *  You can't move worklogs restricted by project roles.
 *  No notifications will be sent for moved worklogs.
 *  No webhooks or events will be sent for moved worklogs.
 *  No issue history will be recorded for moved worklogs.

Time tracking must be enabled in Jira, otherwise this operation returns an error. For more information, see [Configuring time tracking](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/qoXKM).

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the projects containing the source and destination issues.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  *Delete all worklogs* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg)
 *  *Work on issues* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) to log work on an issue, that is to create a worklog entry, if time tracking is enabled. This permission is required as a prerequisite for applying the other time-tracking permissions
 *  If the worklog has visibility restrictions, belongs to the group or has the role visibility is restricted to.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ids": [
    1,
    2,
    5,
    10
  ],
  "issueIdOrKey": "ABC-1234"
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-move-worklogs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|none|
|adjustEstimate|query|string|false|Defines how to update the issues' time estimate, the options are:<br><br> *  `leave` Leaves the estimate unchanged.<br> *  `auto` Reduces the estimate by the aggregate value of `timeSpent` across all worklogs being moved in the source issue, and increases it in the destination issue.|
|overrideEditableFlag|query|boolean|false|Whether the work log entry should be moved to and from the issues even if the issues are not editable, because jira.issue.editable set to false or missing. For example, the issue is closed. Connect and Forge app users with admin permission can use this flag.|
|body|body|[WorklogsMoveRequestBean](#schemaworklogsmoverequestbean)|true|A JSON object containing a list of worklog IDs and the ID or key of the destination issue.|
|» ids|body|[integer(int64)]|false|A list of worklog IDs.|
|» issueIdOrKey|body|string|false|The issue id or key of the destination issue|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|adjustEstimate|leave|
|adjustEstimate|auto|

<h3 id="bulk-move-worklogs-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is partially successful.|None|
|204|No Content|Returned if the request is successful.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if:<br><br> *  `request` is not provided or is invalid<br> *  the user does not have permission to move the worklogs<br> *  the number of worklogs being moved exceeds the limit<br> *  the total size of worklogs being moved is too large<br> *  any worklog contains attachments|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  the source or destination issue is not found or the user does not have permission to view the issues<br> *  at least one of the worklogs is not associated with the provided issue<br> *  time tracking is disabled|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: write:jira-work )
</aside>

## Update worklog

<a id="opIdupdateWorklog"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/string/worklog/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "comment": {
      "content": [
        {
          "content": [
            {
              "text": "I did some work here.",
              "type": "text"
            }
          ],
          "type": "paragraph"
        }
      ],
      "type": "doc",
      "version": 1
    },
    "started": "2021-01-17T12:34:00.000+0000",
    "timeSpentSeconds": 12000,
    "visibility": {
      "identifier": "276f955c-63d7-42c8-9520-92d01dca0625",
      "type": "group"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/worklog/{id}`

Updates a worklog.

Time tracking must be enabled in Jira, otherwise this operation returns an error. For more information, see [Configuring time tracking](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/qoXKM).

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  *Edit all worklogs*[ project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) to update any worklog or *Edit own worklogs* to update worklogs created by the user.
 *  If the worklog has visibility restrictions, belongs to the group or has the role visibility is restricted to.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": {
    "content": [
      {
        "content": [
          {
            "text": "I did some work here.",
            "type": "text"
          }
        ],
        "type": "paragraph"
      }
    ],
    "type": "doc",
    "version": 1
  },
  "started": "2021-01-17T12:34:00.000+0000",
  "timeSpentSeconds": 12000,
  "visibility": {
    "identifier": "276f955c-63d7-42c8-9520-92d01dca0625",
    "type": "group"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-worklog-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key the issue.|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the worklog.|
|notifyUsers|query|boolean|false|Whether users watching the issue are notified by email.|
|adjustEstimate|query|string|false|Defines how to update the issue's time estimate, the options are:<br><br> *  `new` Sets the estimate to a specific value, defined in `newEstimate`.<br> *  `leave` Leaves the estimate unchanged.<br> *  `auto` Updates the estimate by the difference between the original and updated value of `timeSpent` or `timeSpentSeconds`.|
|newEstimate|query|string|false|The value to set as the issue's remaining time estimate, as days (\#d), hours (\#h), or minutes (\#m or \#). For example, *2d*. Required when `adjustEstimate` is `new`.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information about worklogs in the response. This parameter accepts `properties`, which returns worklog properties.|
|overrideEditableFlag|query|boolean|false|Whether the worklog should be added to the issue even if the issue is not editable. For example, because the issue is closed. Connect and Forge app users with *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg) can use this flag.|
|body|body|[Worklog](#schemaworklog)|true|none|
|» comment|body|object|false|A comment about the worklog in [Atlassian Document Format](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/apis/document/structure/). Optional when creating or updating a worklog.|
|» properties|body|[[EntityProperty](#schemaentityproperty)]|false|Details of properties for the worklog. Optional when creating or updating a worklog.|
|» started|body|string(date-time)|false|The datetime on which the worklog effort was started. Required when creating a worklog. Optional when updating a worklog.|
|» timeSpent|body|string|false|The time spent working on the issue as days (\#d), hours (\#h), or minutes (\#m or \#). Required when creating a worklog if `timeSpentSeconds` isn't provided. Optional when updating a worklog. Cannot be provided if `timeSpentSecond` is provided.|
|» timeSpentSeconds|body|integer(int64)|false|The time in seconds spent working on the issue. Required when creating a worklog if `timeSpent` isn't provided. Optional when updating a worklog. Cannot be provided if `timeSpent` is provided.|
|» visibility|body|object|false|Details about any restrictions in the visibility of the worklog. Optional when creating or updating a worklog.|
|» » identifier|body|string \| null|false|The ID of the group or the name of the role that visibility of this item is restricted to.|
|» » type|body|string|false|Whether visibility of this item is restricted to a group or role.|
|» » value|body|string|false|The name of the group or role that visibility of this item is restricted to. Please note that the name of a group is mutable, to reliably identify a group use `identifier`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|adjustEstimate|new|
|adjustEstimate|leave|
|adjustEstimate|manual|
|adjustEstimate|auto|
|» » type|group|
|» » type|role|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"author\":{\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"active\":false,\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/user?accountId=5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\"},\"comment\":{\"type\":\"doc\",\"version\":1,\"content\":[{\"type\":\"paragraph\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"I did some work here.\"}]}]},\"id\":\"100028\",\"issueId\":\"10002\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/10010/worklog/10000\",\"started\":\"2021-01-17T12:34:00.000+0000\",\"timeSpent\":\"3h 20m\",\"timeSpentSeconds\":12000,\"updateAuthor\":{\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"active\":false,\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/user?accountId=5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\"},\"updated\":\"2021-01-18T23:45:00.000+0000\",\"visibility\":{\"identifier\":\"276f955c-63d7-42c8-9520-92d01dca0625\",\"type\":\"group\",\"value\":\"jira-developers\"}}"
```

|---|---|---|---|

|400|Bad Request|Returned if:<br><br> *  `adjustEstimate` is set to `new` but `newEstimate` is not provided or is invalid.<br> *  the user does not have permission to update the worklog.<br> *  the request JSON is malformed.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  the issue is not found or user does not have permission to view the issue.<br> *  the worklog is not found or the user does not have permission to view it.<br> *  time tracking is disabled.|None|

`DELETE /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/worklog/{id}`

Deletes a worklog from an issue.

Time tracking must be enabled in Jira, otherwise this operation returns an error. For more information, see [Configuring time tracking](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/qoXKM).

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that the issue is in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
 *  *Delete all worklogs*[ project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) to delete any worklog or *Delete own worklogs* to delete worklogs created by the user,
 *  If the worklog has visibility restrictions, belongs to the group or has the role visibility is restricted to.

<h3 id="delete-worklog-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or key of the issue.|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the worklog.|

|newEstimate|query|string|false|The value to set as the issue's remaining time estimate, as days (\#d), hours (\#h), or minutes (\#m or \#). For example, *2d*. Required when `adjustEstimate` is `new`.|
|increaseBy|query|string|false|The amount to increase the issue's remaining estimate by, as days (\#d), hours (\#h), or minutes (\#m or \#). For example, *2d*. Required when `adjustEstimate` is `manual`.|
|overrideEditableFlag|query|boolean|false|Whether the work log entry should be added to the issue even if the issue is not editable, because jira.issue.editable set to false or missing. For example, the issue is closed. Connect and Forge app users with admin permission can use this flag.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|adjustEstimate|new|
|adjustEstimate|leave|
|adjustEstimate|manual|
|adjustEstimate|auto|

|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  the issue is not found or user does not have permission to view the issue.<br> *  the worklog is not found or the user does not have permission to view it.<br> *  time tracking is disabled.|None|

## Get IDs of deleted worklogs

<a id="opIdgetIdsOfWorklogsDeletedSince"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/worklog/deleted \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/worklog/deleted`

Returns a list of IDs and delete timestamps for worklogs deleted after a date and time.

This resource is paginated, with a limit of 1000 worklogs per page. Each page lists worklogs from oldest to youngest. If the number of items in the date range exceeds 1000, `until` indicates the timestamp of the youngest item on the page. Also, `nextPage` provides the URL for the next page of worklogs. The `lastPage` parameter is set to true on the last page of worklogs.

This resource does not return worklogs deleted during the minute preceding the request.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Permission to access Jira.

<h3 id="get-ids-of-deleted-worklogs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|since|query|integer(int64)|false|The date and time, as a UNIX timestamp in milliseconds, after which deleted worklogs are returned.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"lastPage\":true,\"nextPage\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/api/~ver~/worklog/deleted?since=1438013693136\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/api/~ver~/worklog/deleted?since=1438013671562\",\"since\":1438013671562,\"until\":1438013693136,\"values\":[{\"properties\":[],\"updatedTime\":1438013671562,\"worklogId\":103},{\"properties\":[],\"updatedTime\":1438013672165,\"worklogId\":104},{\"properties\":[],\"updatedTime\":1438013693136,\"worklogId\":105}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-ids-of-deleted-worklogs-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[ChangedWorklogs](#schemachangedworklogs)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

`POST /rest/api/3/worklog/list`

Returns worklog details for a list of worklog IDs.

The returned list of worklogs is limited to 1000 items.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Permission to access Jira, however, worklogs are only returned where either of the following is true:

 *  the user is a member of a project role or group with permission to view the worklog.

```json
  ]
```

<h3 id="get-worklogs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Get IDs of updated worklogs

<a id="opIdgetIdsOfWorklogsModifiedSince"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/worklog/updated \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/worklog/updated`

Returns a list of IDs and update timestamps for worklogs updated after a date and time.

This resource is paginated, with a limit of 1000 worklogs per page. Each page lists worklogs from oldest to youngest. If the number of items in the date range exceeds 1000, `until` indicates the timestamp of the youngest item on the page. Also, `nextPage` provides the URL for the next page of worklogs. The `lastPage` parameter is set to true on the last page of worklogs.

This resource does not return worklogs updated during the minute preceding the request.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Permission to access Jira, however, worklogs are only returned where either of the following is true:

 *  the worklog is set as *Viewable by All Users*.
 *  the user is a member of a project role or group with permission to view the worklog.

<h3 id="get-ids-of-updated-worklogs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|since|query|integer(int64)|false|The date and time, as a UNIX timestamp in milliseconds, after which updated worklogs are returned.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information about worklogs in the response. This parameter accepts `properties` that returns the properties of each worklog.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"lastPage\":true,\"nextPage\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/api/~ver~/worklog/updated?since=1438013693136\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/api/~ver~/worklog/updated?since=1438013671562\",\"since\":1438013671562,\"until\":1438013693136,\"values\":[{\"properties\":[],\"updatedTime\":1438013671562,\"worklogId\":103},{\"properties\":[],\"updatedTime\":1438013672165,\"worklogId\":104},{\"properties\":[],\"updatedTime\":1438013693136,\"worklogId\":105}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-ids-of-updated-worklogs-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[ChangedWorklogs](#schemachangedworklogs)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-issues">Issues</h1>

This resource represents Jira issues. Use it to:

 *  create or edit issues, individually or in bulk.
 *  retrieve metadata about the options for creating or editing issues.
 *  delete an issue.
 *  assign a user to an issue.
 *  get issue changelogs.
 *  send notifications about an issue.
 *  get details of the transitions available for an issue.
 *  transition an issue.
 *  Archive issues.
 *  Unarchive issues.
 *  Export archived issues.

## Bulk fetch changelogs

<a id="opIdgetBulkChangelogs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/changelog/bulkfetch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "fieldIds": [
      "string"
    ],
    "issueIdsOrKeys": [
      "string"
    ],
    "maxResults": 1000,
    "nextPageToken": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/changelog/bulkfetch`

Bulk fetch changelogs for multiple issues and filter by fields

Returns a paginated list of all changelogs for given issues sorted by changelog date and issue IDs, starting from the oldest changelog and smallest issue ID.

Issues are identified by their ID or key, and optionally changelogs can be filtered by their field IDs. You can request the changelogs of up to 1000 issues and can filter them by up to 10 field IDs.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the projects that the issues are in.
 *  If [issue-level security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issues.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "fieldIds": [
    "string"
  ],
  "issueIdsOrKeys": [
    "string"
  ],
  "maxResults": 1000,
  "nextPageToken": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-fetch-changelogs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[BulkChangelogRequestBean](#schemabulkchangelogrequestbean)|true|A JSON object containing the bulk fetch changelog request filters such as issue IDs and field IDs.|
|» fieldIds|body|[string]|false|List of field IDs to filter changelogs|
|» issueIdsOrKeys|body|[string]|true|List of issue IDs/keys to fetch changelogs for|
|» maxResults|body|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page|
|» nextPageToken|body|string|false|The cursor for pagination|

`POST /rest/api/3/issue`

Creates an issue or, where the option to create subtasks is enabled in Jira, a subtask. A transition may be applied, to move the issue or subtask to a workflow step other than the default start step, and issue properties set.

The content of the issue or subtask is defined using `update` and `fields`. The fields that can be set in the issue or subtask are determined using the [ Get create issue metadata](#api-rest-api-3-issue-createmeta-get). These are the same fields that appear on the issue's create screen. Note that the `description`, `environment`, and any `textarea` type custom fields (multi-line text fields) take Atlassian Document Format content. Single line custom fields (`textfield`) accept a string and don't handle Atlassian Document Format content.

Creating a subtask differs from creating an issue as follows:

 *  `issueType` must be set to a subtask issue type (use [ Get create issue metadata](#api-rest-api-3-issue-createmeta-get) to find subtask issue types).
 *  `parent` must contain the ID or key of the parent issue.

In a next-gen project any issue may be made a child providing that the parent and child are members of the same project.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Browse projects* and *Create issues* [project permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project in which the issue or subtask is created.
