## Update priority scheme

<a id="opIdupdatePriorityScheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/priorityscheme/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "defaultPriorityId": 10001,
    "description": "My priority scheme description",
    "mappings": {
      "in": {
        "10003": 10002,
        "10004": 10001
      },
      "out": {
        "10001": 10005,
        "10002": 10006
      }
    },
    "name": "My new priority scheme",
    "priorities": {
      "add": {
        "ids": [
          10001,
          10002
        ]
      },
      "remove": {
        "ids": [
          10003,
          10004
        ]
      }
    },
    "projects": {
      "add": {
        "ids": [
          10101,
          10102
        ]
      },
      "remove": {
        "ids": [
          10103,
          10104
        ]
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/priorityscheme/{schemeId}`

Updates a priority scheme. This includes its details, the lists of priorities and projects in it

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "defaultPriorityId": 10001,
  "description": "My priority scheme description",
  "mappings": {
    "in": {
      "10003": 10002,
      "10004": 10001
    },
    "out": {
      "10001": 10005,
      "10002": 10006
    }
  },
  "name": "My new priority scheme",
  "priorities": {
    "add": {
      "ids": [
        10001,
        10002
      ]
    },
    "remove": {
      "ids": [
        10003,
        10004
      ]
    }
  },
  "projects": {
    "add": {
      "ids": [
        10101,
        10102
      ]
    },
    "remove": {
      "ids": [
        10103,
        10104
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-priority-scheme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|schemeId|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the priority scheme.|
|body|body|[UpdatePrioritySchemeRequestBean](#schemaupdatepriorityschemerequestbean)|true|none|
|» defaultPriorityId|body|integer(int64)|false|The default priority of the scheme.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the priority scheme.|
|» mappings|body|object|false|Instructions to migrate the priorities of issues.<br><br>`in` mappings are used to migrate the priorities of issues to priorities used within the priority scheme.<br><br>`out` mappings are used to migrate the priorities of issues to priorities not used within the priority scheme.<br><br> *  When **priorities** are **added** to the priority scheme, no mapping needs to be provided as the new priorities are not used by any issues.<br> *  When **priorities** are **removed** from the priority scheme, issues that are using those priorities must be migrated to new priorities used by the priority scheme.<br>    <br>     *  An `in` mapping must be provided for each of these priorities.<br> *  When **projects** are **added** to the priority scheme, the priorities of issues in those projects might need to be migrated to new priorities used by the priority scheme. This can occur when the current scheme does not use all the priorities in the project(s)' priority scheme(s).<br>    <br>     *  An `in` mapping must be provided for each of these priorities.<br> *  When **projects** are **removed** from the priority scheme, the priorities of issues in those projects might need to be migrated to new priorities within the **Default Priority Scheme** that are not used by the priority scheme. This can occur when the **Default Priority Scheme** does not use all the priorities within the current scheme.<br>    <br>     *  An `out` mapping must be provided for each of these priorities.<br><br>For more information on `in` and `out` mappings, see the child properties documentation for the `PriorityMapping` object below.|
|» » in|body|object|false|The mapping of priorities for issues being migrated **into** this priority scheme. Key is the old priority ID, value is the new priority ID (must exist in this priority scheme).<br><br>E.g. The current priority scheme has priority ID `10001`. Issues with priority ID `10000` are being migrated into this priority scheme will need mapping to new priorities. The `in` mapping would be `{"10000": 10001}`.|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|integer(int64)|false|none|
|» » out|body|object|false|The mapping of priorities for issues being migrated **out of** this priority scheme. Key is the old priority ID (must exist in this priority scheme), value is the new priority ID (must exist in the default priority scheme). Required for updating an existing priority scheme. Not used when creating a new priority scheme.<br><br>E.g. The current priority scheme has priority ID `10001`. Issues with priority ID `10001` are being migrated out of this priority scheme will need mapping to new priorities. The `out` mapping would be `{"10001": 10000}`.|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|integer(int64)|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the priority scheme. Must be unique.|
|» priorities|body|object|false|The priorities in the scheme.|
|» » add|body|object|false|Priorities to add to a scheme|
|» » » ids|body|[integer(int64)]|true|Affected entity ids.|
|» » remove|body|object|false|Priorities to remove from a scheme|
|» » » ids|body|[integer(int64)]|true|Affected entity ids.|
|» projects|body|object|false|The projects in the scheme.|
|» » add|body|object|false|Projects to add to a scheme|
|» » » ids|body|[integer(int64)]|true|Affected entity ids.|
|» » remove|body|object|false|Projects to remove from a scheme|
|» » » ids|body|[integer(int64)]|true|Affected entity ids.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|202|Accepted|Returned if the request is accepted.|[UpdatePrioritySchemeResponseBean](#schemaupdatepriorityschemeresponsebean)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request isn't valid.<br><br>**Mappings Validation Errors**<br><br> *  ``The changes to priority schemes require mapping of priorities. Please provide a value for the 'in' mappings object.`` Priorities are being removed and/or projects are being added to the scheme, but ``in`` mappings are not provided.<br> *  ``The changes to priority schemes require mapping of priorities. Please provide a value for the 'out' mappings object.`` Projects are being removed from the scheme, but ``out`` mappings are not provided.<br> *  ``The priorities with IDs [ID 1, ID 2, ...] provided as keys for the 'in' mappings object do not exist. Please provide existing priority IDs.`` The listed priority ID(s) have been provided as keys for ``in`` mappings but do not exist. Please confirm the correct priority ID(s) have been provided, they should be priorities that exist on the Jira site which are used by projects being added to the current scheme, but are not in use by the current scheme.<br> *  ``The priorities with IDs [ID 1, ID 2, ...] provided as values for the 'in' mappings object do not exist. Please provide existing priority IDs used by the current priority scheme.`` The listed priority ID(s) have been provided as values for ``in`` mappings but do not exist. Please confirm the correct priority ID(s) have been provided, they should be priorities that exist on the Jira site and are in use by the current scheme.<br> *  ``The priorities with IDs [ID 1, ID 2, ...] provided as keys for the 'out' mappings object do not exist. Please provide existing priority IDs used by the current priority scheme.`` The listed priority ID(s) have been provided as keys for ``out`` mappings but are invalid. Please confirm the correct priority ID(s) have been provided, they should be priorities that exist on the Jira site and are in use by the current scheme.<br> *  ``The priorities with IDs [ID 1, ID 2, ...] provided as values for the 'out' mappings object do not exist. Please provide existing priority IDs used by the default scheme.`` The listed priority ID(s) have been provided as values for ``out`` mappings but are invalid. Please confirm the correct priority ID(s) have been provided, they should be priorities that exist on the Jira site and are in use by the Default Priority Scheme, but are not in use by the current scheme.<br> *  ``The priorities with IDs [ID 1, ID 2, ...] do not require mapping. Please remove these keys and their corresponding values from the 'in' mappings object.`` The listed priority ID(s) have been provided as keys for ``in`` mappings but are not required, they can be removed from the mappings object.<br> *  ``The priorities with IDs [ID 1, ID 2, ...] require mapping. Please provide mappings in the 'in' mappings object, where these priorities are the keys with corresponding values.`` The listed priority ID(s) have not been provided as keys for ``in`` mappings but are required, add them to the mappings object.<br> *  ``The priorities with IDs [ID 1, ID 2, ...] being mapped to are not in the current scheme. Please remove these values and their corresponding keys from the 'in' mappings object.`` The listed priority ID(s) have been provided as keys for ``in`` mappings but are not in use by the current scheme, they can be removed from the mappings object.<br> *  ``The priorities with IDs [ID 1, ID 2, ...] do not require mapping. Please remove these keys and their corresponding values from the 'out' mappings object.`` The listed priority ID(s) hve been provided as keys for ``out`` mappings but are not required, they can be removed from the mappings object.<br> *  ``The priorities with IDs [ID 1, ID 2, ...] require mapping. Please provide mappings in the 'out' mappings object, where these priorities are the keys with corresponding values.`` The listed priority ID(s) have not been provided as keys for ``out`` mappings but are required, add them to the mappings object.<br> *  ``The priorities with IDs [ID 1, ID 2, ...] being mapped to are not in the default scheme. Please remove these values and their corresponding keys from the 'out' mappings object.`` The listed priority ID(s) have been provided as keys for ``out`` mappings but are not in use by the Default Priority Scheme, they can be removed from the mappings object.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user doesn't have the necessary permissions.|None|
|409|Conflict|Returned if an action with this priority scheme is still in progress.|None|

## Load project avatar

<a id="opIdcreateProjectAvatar"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string/avatar2 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: */*' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/avatar2`

Loads an avatar for a project.

Specify the avatar's local file location in the body of the request. Also, include the following headers:

 *  `X-Atlassian-Token: no-check` To prevent XSRF protection blocking the request, for more information see [Special Headers](#special-request-headers).
 *  `Content-Type: image/image type` Valid image types are JPEG, GIF, or PNG.

For example:  
`curl --request POST `

`--user email@example.com:<api_token> `

`--header 'X-Atlassian-Token: no-check' `

`--header 'Content-Type: image/< image_type>' `

`--data-binary "<@/path/to/file/with/your/avatar>" `

`--url 'https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/avatar2'`

The avatar is cropped to a square. If no crop parameters are specified, the square originates at the top left of the image. The length of the square's sides is set to the smaller of the height or width of the image.

The cropped image is then used to create avatars of 16x16, 24x24, 32x32, and 48x48 in size.

After creating the avatar use [Set project avatar](#api-rest-api-3-project-projectIdOrKey-avatar-put) to set it as the project's displayed avatar.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
null
```

<h3 id="load-project-avatar-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or (case-sensitive) key of the project.|
|x|query|integer(int32)|false|The X coordinate of the top-left corner of the crop region.|
|y|query|integer(int32)|false|The Y coordinate of the top-left corner of the crop region.|
|size|query|integer(int32)|false|The length of each side of the crop region.|
|body|body|object|true|none|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
"{\"id\":\"1010\",\"isDeletable\":true,\"isSelected\":false,\"isSystemAvatar\":false}"
```

<h3 id="load-project-avatar-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returned if the request is successful.|[Avatar](#schemaavatar)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if:<br><br> *  an image isn't included in the request.<br> *  the image type is unsupported.<br> *  the crop parameters extend the crop area beyond the edge of the image.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to administer the project or an anonymous call is made to the operation.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project is not found or the user does not have permission to view the project.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-project-classification-levels">Project classification levels</h1>

This resource represents classification levels used in a project. Use it to view and manage classification levels in your projects.

## Get the classification configuration for a project

<a id="opIdgetProjectClassificationConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string/classification-config \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/classification-config`

Returns the consolidated classification configuration for a project's admin settings page.

This includes permitted classification levels (with status), the project's default classification level, the organization's default classification level, and the container override setting.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Browse Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.
 *  *Administer projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.
 *  *Administer jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-the-classification-configuration-for-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrKey|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case-sensitive).|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"classificationLevels\":[{\"id\":\"ari:cloud:platform::classification-tag/5bfa70f7-4af1-44f5-9e12-1ce185f15a38\",\"status\":\"published\",\"name\":\"Restricted\",\"rank\":1,\"description\":\"Data we hold that would be very damaging and would cause loss of trust with customers and present legal risk if mishandled\",\"guideline\":\"Access to data must be restricted to only individuals who need access in order to perform their job duties.\",\"color\":\"RED\"}],\"containerOverride\":\"ANY\",\"defaultClassificationLevel\":{\"id\":\"ari:cloud:platform::classification-tag/5bfa70f7-4af1-44f5-9e12-1ce185f15a38\",\"status\":\"published\",\"name\":\"Restricted\",\"rank\":1,\"description\":\"Data we hold that would be very damaging and would cause loss of trust with customers and present legal risk if mishandled\",\"guideline\":\"Access to data must be restricted to only individuals who need access in order to perform their job duties.\",\"color\":\"RED\"},\"organizationClassificationLevel\":{\"id\":\"ari:cloud:platform::classification-tag/a82d653e-1035-4aa2-b9de-4265511fd487\",\"status\":\"published\",\"name\":\"Confidential\",\"rank\":2,\"description\":\"Data we hold that would likely be damaging and could cause loss of trust with our customers if mishandled\",\"guideline\":\"Data should be encrypted at rest and in transit.\",\"color\":\"BLUE\"}}"
```

<h3 id="get-the-classification-configuration-for-a-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project is not found or the feature is disabled.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-project-components">Project components</h1>

This resource represents project components. Use it to get, create, update, and delete project components. Also get components for project and get a count of issues by component.

## Find components for projects

<a id="opIdfindComponentsForProjects"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/component \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/component`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of all components in a project, including global (Compass) components when applicable.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Browse Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.

<h3 id="find-components-for-projects-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdsOrKeys|query|[string]|false|The project IDs and/or project keys (case sensitive).|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|orderBy|query|string|false|[Order](#ordering) the results by a field:<br><br> *  `description` Sorts by the component description.<br> *  `name` Sorts by component name.|
|query|query|string|false|Filter the results using a literal string. Components with a matching `name` or `description` are returned (case insensitive).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|orderBy|description|
|orderBy|-description|
|orderBy|+description|
|orderBy|name|
|orderBy|-name|
|orderBy|+name|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"isLast\":false,\"maxResults\":2,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":2,\"values\":[{\"description\":\"This is a component\",\"id\":\"10000\",\"name\":\"Component1\",\"self\":\"http://www.example.com/jira/rest/api/2/component/10000\"},{\"ari\":\"ari:cloud:graph::integration-context/ecda99d9-9b42-4bf7-8b4f-ecb5fcf5868c/component/10001\",\"description\":\"This is a global component\",\"id\":\"10001\",\"metadata\":{\"key1\":\"value1\",\"key2\":\"value2\"},\"name\":\"Component2\",\"self\":\"http://www.example.com/jira/rest/api/2/component/10001\"}]}"
```

<h3 id="find-components-for-projects-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PageBean2ComponentJsonBean](#schemapagebean2componentjsonbean)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project is not found or the user does not have permission to view it.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Create component

<a id="opIdcreateComponent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/component \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "assigneeType": "PROJECT_LEAD",
    "description": "This is a Jira component",
    "isAssigneeTypeValid": false,
    "leadAccountId": "5b10a2844c20165700ede21g",
    "name": "Component 1",
    "project": "HSP"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/component`

Creates a component. Use components to provide containers for issues within a project. Use components to provide containers for issues within a project.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project in which the component is created or *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "assigneeType": "PROJECT_LEAD",
  "description": "This is a Jira component",
  "isAssigneeTypeValid": false,
  "leadAccountId": "5b10a2844c20165700ede21g",
  "name": "Component 1",
  "project": "HSP"
}
```

<h3 id="create-component-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ProjectComponent](#schemaprojectcomponent)|true|none|
|» assigneeType|body|string|false|The nominal user type used to determine the assignee for issues created with this component. See `realAssigneeType` for details on how the type of the user, and hence the user, assigned to issues is determined. Can take the following values:<br><br> *  `PROJECT_LEAD` the assignee to any issues created with this component is nominally the lead for the project the component is in.<br> *  `COMPONENT_LEAD` the assignee to any issues created with this component is nominally the lead for the component.<br> *  `UNASSIGNED` an assignee is not set for issues created with this component.<br> *  `PROJECT_DEFAULT` the assignee to any issues created with this component is nominally the default assignee for the project that the component is in.<br><br>Default value: `PROJECT_DEFAULT`.  <br>Optional when creating or updating a component.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description for the component. Optional when creating or updating a component.|
|» leadAccountId|body|string|false|The accountId of the component's lead user. The accountId uniquely identifies the user across all Atlassian products. For example, *5b10ac8d82e05b22cc7d4ef5*.|
|» leadUserName|body|string|false|This property is no longer available and will be removed from the documentation soon. See the [deprecation notice](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/) for details.|
|» name|body|string|false|The unique name for the component in the project. Required when creating a component. Optional when updating a component. The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|» project|body|string|false|The key of the project the component is assigned to. Required when creating a component. Can't be updated.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» assigneeType|PROJECT_DEFAULT|
|» assigneeType|COMPONENT_LEAD|
|» assigneeType|PROJECT_LEAD|
|» assigneeType|UNASSIGNED|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
"{\"ari\":\"ari:cloud:compass:fdb3fdec-4e70-be56-11ee-0242ac120002:component/fdb3fdec-4e70-11ee-be56-0242ac120002/fdb3fdec-11ee-4e70-be56-0242ac120002\",\"assignee\":{\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\",\"accountType\":\"atlassian\",\"active\":false,\"avatarUrls\":{\"16x16\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=16&s=16\",\"24x24\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=24&s=24\",\"32x32\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=32&s=32\",\"48x48\":\"https://avatar-management--avatars.server-location.prod.public.atl-paas.net/initials/MK-5.png?size=48&s=48\"},\"displayName\":\"Mia ## Update component
```

<a id="opIdupdateComponent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/component/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "assigneeType": "PROJECT_LEAD",
    "description": "This is a Jira component",
    "isAssigneeTypeValid": false,
    "leadAccountId": "5b10a2844c20165700ede21g",
    "name": "Component 1"
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/component/{id}`

Updates a component. Any fields included in the request are overwritten. If `leadAccountId` is an empty string ("") the component lead is removed.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project containing the component or *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "assigneeType": "PROJECT_LEAD",
  "description": "This is a Jira component",
  "isAssigneeTypeValid": false,
  "leadAccountId": "5b10a2844c20165700ede21g",
  "name": "Component 1"
}
```

<h3 id="update-component-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the component.|
|body|body|[ProjectComponent](#schemaprojectcomponent)|true|none|
|» assigneeType|body|string|false|The nominal user type used to determine the assignee for issues created with this component. See `realAssigneeType` for details on how the type of the user, and hence the user, assigned to issues is determined. Can take the following values:<br><br> *  `PROJECT_LEAD` the assignee to any issues created with this component is nominally the lead for the project the component is in.<br> *  `COMPONENT_LEAD` the assignee to any issues created with this component is nominally the lead for the component.<br> *  `UNASSIGNED` an assignee is not set for issues created with this component.<br> *  `PROJECT_DEFAULT` the assignee to any issues created with this component is nominally the default assignee for the project that the component is in.<br><br>Default value: `PROJECT_DEFAULT`.  <br>Optional when creating or updating a component.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description for the component. Optional when creating or updating a component.|
|» leadAccountId|body|string|false|The accountId of the component's lead user. The accountId uniquely identifies the user across all Atlassian products. For example, *5b10ac8d82e05b22cc7d4ef5*.|
|» leadUserName|body|string|false|This property is no longer available and will be removed from the documentation soon. See the [deprecation notice](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/) for details.|
|» name|body|string|false|The unique name for the component in the project. Required when creating a component. Optional when updating a component. The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|» project|body|string|false|The key of the project the component is assigned to. Required when creating a component. Can't be updated.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» assigneeType|PROJECT_DEFAULT|
|» assigneeType|COMPONENT_LEAD|
|» assigneeType|PROJECT_LEAD|
|» assigneeType|UNASSIGNED|

## Delete component

<a id="opIddeleteComponent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/component/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /rest/api/3/component/{id}`

Deletes a component.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project containing the component or *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="delete-component-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the component.|
|moveIssuesTo|query|string|false|The ID of the component to replace the deleted component. If this value is null no replacement is made.|

<h3 id="delete-component-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the request is successful.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to manage the project containing the component or does not have permission to administer Jira.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  the component is not found.<br> *  the replacement component is not found.<br> *  the user does not have permission to browse the project containing the component.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )
</aside>

## Get project components paginated

<a id="opIdgetProjectComponentsPaginated"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string/component \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/component`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of all components in a project. See the [Get project components](#api-rest-api-3-project-projectIdOrKey-components-get) resource if you want to get a full list of versions without pagination.

If your project uses Compass components, this API will return a list of Compass components that are linked to issues in that project.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Browse Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.

<h3 id="get-project-components-paginated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrKey|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case sensitive).|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|orderBy|query|string|false|[Order](#ordering) the results by a field:<br><br> *  `description` Sorts by the component description.<br> *  `issueCount` Sorts by the count of issues associated with the component.<br> *  `lead` Sorts by the user key of the component's project lead.<br> *  `name` Sorts by component name.|
|componentSource|query|string|false|The source of the components to return. Can be `jira` (default), `compass` or `auto`. When `auto` is specified, the API will return connected Compass components if the project is opted into Compass, otherwise it will return Jira components. Defaults to `jira`.|
|query|query|string|false|Filter the results using a literal string. Components with a matching `name` or `description` are returned (case insensitive).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|orderBy|description|
|orderBy|-description|
|orderBy|+description|
|orderBy|issueCount|
|orderBy|-issueCount|
|orderBy|+issueCount|
|orderBy|lead|
|orderBy|-lead|
|orderBy|+lead|
|orderBy|name|
|orderBy|-name|
|orderBy|+name|
|componentSource|jira|
|componentSource|compass|
|componentSource|auto|

## Get project components

<a id="opIdgetProjectComponents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string/components \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/components`

Returns all components in a project. See the [Get project components paginated](#api-rest-api-3-project-projectIdOrKey-component-get) resource if you want to get a full list of components with pagination.

If your project uses Compass components, this API will return a paginated list of Compass components that are linked to issues in that project.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Browse Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.

<h3 id="get-project-components-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrKey|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case sensitive).|
|componentSource|query|string|false|The source of the components to return. Can be `jira` (default), `compass` or `auto`. When `auto` is specified, the API will return connected Compass components if the project is opted into Compass, otherwise it will return Jira components. Defaults to `jira`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|componentSource|jira|
|componentSource|compass|
|componentSource|auto|

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-project-email">Project email</h1>

This resource represents the email address used to send a project's notifications. Use it to get and set the [project's sender email address](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/dolKLg).

## Get project's sender email

<a id="opIdgetProjectEmail"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/0/email \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/project/{projectId}/email`

Returns the [project's sender email address](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/dolKLg).

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.

<h3 id="get-projects-sender-email-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|path|integer(int64)|true|The project ID.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"emailAddress\":\"jira@example.customdomain.com\",\"emailAddressStatus\":[\"Email address or domain not verified.\"]}"
```

<h3 id="get-projects-sender-email-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[ProjectEmailAddress](#schemaprojectemailaddress)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to read project.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project or project's sender email address is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )
</aside>

## Set project's sender email

<a id="opIdupdateProjectEmail"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/0/email \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "emailAddress": "jira@example.atlassian.net"
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/project/{projectId}/email`

Sets the [project's sender email address](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/dolKLg).

If `emailAddress` is an empty string, the default email address is restored.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg) or *Administer Projects* [project permission.](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg)

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "emailAddress": "jira@example.atlassian.net"
}
```

<h3 id="set-projects-sender-email-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|path|integer(int64)|true|The project ID.|
|body|body|[ProjectEmailAddress](#schemaprojectemailaddress)|true|The project's sender email address to be set.|
|» emailAddress|body|string|false|The email address.|
|» emailAddressStatus|body|[string]|false|When using a custom domain, the status of the email address.|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="set-projects-sender-email-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the project's sender email address is successfully set.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid, if the email address is not valid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to administer the project.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-project-features">Project features</h1>

This resource represents project features. Use it to get the list of features for a project and modify the state of a feature. The project feature endpoint is available only for Jira Software, both for team- and company-managed projects.

## Get project features

<a id="opIdgetFeaturesForProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string/features \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/features`

Returns the list of features for a project.

<h3 id="get-project-features-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or (case-sensitive) key of the project.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"features\":[{\"feature\":\"jsw.classic.roadmap\",\"imageUri\":\"https://jira.atlassian.com/s/sb53l8/b/3/ab8a7691e4738b4f147e293f0864adfd5b8d3c85/_/download/resources/com.atlassian.jira.rest:classic-project-features/simple-roadmap-feature.svg\",\"localisedDescription\":\"Your roadmap is an optimized location to create and manage your epics.\",\"localisedName\":\"Roadmap\",\"prerequisites\":[],\"projectId\":10001,\"state\":\"ENABLED\",\"toggleLocked\":true},{\"feature\":\"jsw.classic.backlog\",\"imageUri\":\"https://jira.atlassian.com/s/sb53l8/b/3/ab8a7691e4738b4f147e293f0864adfd5b8d3c85/_/download/resources/com.atlassian.jira.rest:classic-project-features/simple-backlog-feature.svg\",\"localisedDescription\":\"Plan and prioritize work in a dedicated space. To enable and configure the backlog for each board, go to board settings.\",\"localisedName\":\"Backlog\",\"prerequisites\":[],\"projectId\":10001,\"state\":\"ENABLED\",\"toggleLocked\":true}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-project-features-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[ContainerForProjectFeatures](#schemacontainerforprojectfeatures)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the required permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Set project feature state

<a id="opIdtoggleFeatureForProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string/features/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "state": "ENABLED"
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/features/{featureKey}`

Sets the state of a project feature.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "state": "ENABLED"
}
```

<h3 id="set-project-feature-state-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrKey|path|string|true|The ID or (case-sensitive) key of the project.|
|featureKey|path|string|true|The key of the feature.|
|body|body|[ProjectFeatureState](#schemaprojectfeaturestate)|true|Details of the feature state change.|
|» state|body|string|false|The feature state.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» state|ENABLED|
|» state|DISABLED|
|» state|COMING_SOON|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"features\":[{\"feature\":\"jsw.classic.roadmap\",\"imageUri\":\"https://jira.atlassian.com/s/sb53l8/b/3/ab8a7691e4738b4f147e293f0864adfd5b8d3c85/_/download/resources/com.atlassian.jira.rest:classic-project-features/simple-roadmap-feature.svg\",\"localisedDescription\":\"Your roadmap is an optimized location to create and manage your epics.\",\"localisedName\":\"Roadmap\",\"prerequisites\":[],\"projectId\":10001,\"state\":\"ENABLED\",\"toggleLocked\":true},{\"feature\":\"jsw.classic.backlog\",\"imageUri\":\"https://jira.atlassian.com/s/sb53l8/b/3/ab8a7691e4738b4f147e293f0864adfd5b8d3c85/_/download/resources/com.atlassian.jira.rest:classic-project-features/simple-backlog-feature.svg\",\"localisedDescription\":\"Plan and prioritize work in a dedicated space. To enable and configure the backlog for each board, go to board settings.\",\"localisedName\":\"Backlog\",\"prerequisites\":[],\"projectId\":10001,\"state\":\"ENABLED\",\"toggleLocked\":true}]}"
```

<h3 id="set-project-feature-state-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[ContainerForProjectFeatures](#schemacontainerforprojectfeatures)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the required permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project or project feature is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-project-key-and-name-validation">Project key and name validation</h1>

This resource provides validation for project keys and names.

## Validate project key

<a id="opIdvalidateProjectKey"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/projectvalidate/key \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/projectvalidate/key`

Validates a project key by confirming the key is a valid string and not in use.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** None.

<h3 id="validate-project-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|query|string|false|The project key.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[],\"errors\":{\"projectKey\":\"A project with that project key already exists.\"}}"
```

<h3 id="validate-project-key-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[ErrorCollection](#schemaerrorcollection)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Get valid project key

<a id="opIdgetValidProjectKey"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/projectvalidate/validProjectKey \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/projectvalidate/validProjectKey`

Validates a project key and, if the key is invalid or in use, generates a valid random string for the project key.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** None.

<h3 id="get-valid-project-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|query|string|false|The project key.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"\"VPNE\""
```

<h3 id="get-valid-project-key-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Get valid project name

<a id="opIdgetValidProjectName"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/projectvalidate/validProjectName?name=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/projectvalidate/validProjectName`

Checks that a project name isn't in use. If the name isn't in use, the passed string is returned. If the name is in use, this operation attempts to generate a valid project name based on the one supplied, usually by adding a sequence number. If a valid project name cannot be generated, a 404 response is returned.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** None.

<h3 id="get-valid-project-name-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|string|true|The project name.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"\"Valid Project Name Example\""
```

<h3 id="get-valid-project-name-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if a valid project name cannot be generated.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-project-permission-schemes">Project permission schemes</h1>

This resource represents permission schemes for a project. Use this resource to:

 *  get details of a project's issue security levels available to the calling user.
 *  get the permission scheme associated with the project or assign different permission scheme to the project.
 *  get details of a project's issue security scheme.

See [Managing project permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for more information about permission schemes.

## Get project issue security scheme

<a id="opIdgetProjectIssueSecurityScheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string/issuesecuritylevelscheme \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/project/{projectKeyOrId}/issuesecuritylevelscheme`

Returns the [issue security scheme](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) associated with the project.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg) or the *Administer Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg).

<h3 id="get-project-issue-security-scheme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKeyOrId|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case sensitive).|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"defaultSecurityLevelId\":10021,\"description\":\"Description for the default issue security scheme\",\"id\":10000,\"levels\":[{\"description\":\"Only the reporter and internal staff can see this issue.\",\"id\":\"10021\",\"name\":\"Reporter Only\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/securitylevel/10021\"}],\"name\":\"Default Issue Security Scheme\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issuesecurityschemes/10000\"}"
```

<h3 id="get-project-issue-security-scheme-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[SecurityScheme](#schemasecurityscheme)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the project is visible to the user but the user doesn't have administrative permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project is not found or the user does not have permission to view it.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Get assigned permission scheme

<a id="opIdgetAssignedPermissionScheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string/permissionscheme \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/project/{projectKeyOrId}/permissionscheme`

Gets the [permission scheme](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) associated with the project.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg) or *Administer projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg).

<h3 id="get-assigned-permission-scheme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKeyOrId|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case sensitive).|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information in the response. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Note that permissions are included when you specify any value. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `all` Returns all expandable information.<br> *  `field` Returns information about the custom field granted the permission.<br> *  `group` Returns information about the group that is granted the permission.<br> *  `permissions` Returns all permission grants for each permission scheme.<br> *  `projectRole` Returns information about the project role granted the permission.<br> *  `user` Returns information about the user who is granted the permission.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"description\":\"description\",\"id\":10000,\"name\":\"Example permission scheme\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/permissionscheme/10000\"}"
```

<h3 id="get-assigned-permission-scheme-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PermissionScheme](#schemapermissionscheme)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to view the project's configuration.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project is not found or the user does not have permission to view the project.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Assign permission scheme

<a id="opIdassignPermissionScheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string/permissionscheme \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "id": 10000
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/project/{projectKeyOrId}/permissionscheme`

Assigns a permission scheme with a project. See [Managing project permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for more information about permission schemes.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg)

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": 10000
}
```

<h3 id="assign-permission-scheme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKeyOrId|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case sensitive).|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information in the response. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Note that permissions are included when you specify any value. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `all` Returns all expandable information.<br> *  `field` Returns information about the custom field granted the permission.<br> *  `group` Returns information about the group that is granted the permission.<br> *  `permissions` Returns all permission grants for each permission scheme.<br> *  `projectRole` Returns information about the project role granted the permission.<br> *  `user` Returns information about the user who is granted the permission.|
|body|body|[IdBean](#schemaidbean)|true|none|
|» id|body|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the permission scheme to associate with the project. Use the [Get all permission schemes](#api-rest-api-3-permissionscheme-get) resource to get a list of permission scheme IDs.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"description\":\"description\",\"id\":10000,\"name\":\"Example permission scheme\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/permissionscheme/10000\"}"
```

<h3 id="assign-permission-scheme-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PermissionScheme](#schemapermissionscheme)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if:<br><br> *  the user does not have the necessary permission to edit the project's configuration.<br> *  the Jira instance is Jira Core Free or Jira Software Free. Permission schemes cannot be assigned to projects on free plans.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project or permission scheme is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )
</aside>

## Get project issue security levels

<a id="opIdgetSecurityLevelsForProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string/securitylevel \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/project/{projectKeyOrId}/securitylevel`

Returns all [issue security](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/J4lKLg) levels for the project that the user has access to.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Browse projects* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg) for the project, however, issue security levels are only returned for authenticated user with *Set Issue Security* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg) for the project.

<h3 id="get-project-issue-security-levels-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectKeyOrId|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case sensitive).|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"levels\":[{\"description\":\"Only the reporter and internal staff can see this issue.\",\"id\":\"100000\",\"name\":\"Reporter Only\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/securitylevel/100000\"},{\"description\":\"Only internal staff can see this issue.\",\"id\":\"100001\",\"name\":\"Staff Only\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/securitylevel/100001\"}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-project-issue-security-levels-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[ProjectIssueSecurityLevels](#schemaprojectissuesecuritylevels)|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project is not found or the user does not have permission to view it.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-project-properties">Project properties</h1>

This resource represents [project](#api-group-Projects) properties, which provides for storing custom data against a project. Use it to get, create, and delete project properties as well as get a list of property keys for a project. Project properties are a type of [entity property](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/jira-entity-properties/).

## Get project property keys

<a id="opIdgetProjectPropertyKeys"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string/properties \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/properties`

Returns all [project property](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/storing-data-without-a-database/#a-id-jira-entity-properties-a-jira-entity-properties) keys for the project.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Browse Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.

<h3 id="get-project-property-keys-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrKey|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case sensitive).|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"keys\":[{\"key\":\"issue.support\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/EX-2/properties/issue.support\"}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-project-property-keys-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PropertyKeys](#schemapropertykeys)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to view the project.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Get project property

<a id="opIdgetProjectProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string/properties/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/properties/{propertyKey}`

Returns the value of a [project property](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/storing-data-without-a-database/#a-id-jira-entity-properties-a-jira-entity-properties).

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Browse Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project containing the property.

<h3 id="get-project-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrKey|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case sensitive).|
|propertyKey|path|string|true|The project property key. Use [Get project property keys](#api-rest-api-3-project-projectIdOrKey-properties-get) to get a list of all project property keys.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"key\":\"issue.support\",\"value\":{\"system.conversation.id\":\"b1bf38be-5e94-4b40-a3b8-9278735ee1e6\",\"system.support.time\":\"1m\"}}"
```

<h3 id="get-project-property-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[EntityProperty](#schemaentityproperty)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to view the project.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project or property is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Set project property

<a id="opIdsetProjectProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string/properties/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "number": 5,
    "string": "string-value"
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/properties/{propertyKey}`

Sets the value of the [project property](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/storing-data-without-a-database/#a-id-jira-entity-properties-a-jira-entity-properties). You can use project properties to store custom data against the project.

The value of the request body must be a [valid](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4627), non-empty JSON blob. The maximum length is 32768 characters.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg) or *Administer Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project in which the property is created.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "number": 5,
  "string": "string-value"
}
```

<h3 id="set-project-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrKey|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case sensitive).|
|propertyKey|path|string|true|The key of the project property. The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|body|body|object|true|The value of the property. The value has to be a valid, non-empty [JSON](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4627) value. The maximum length of the property value is 32768 bytes.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
null
```

> 201 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="set-project-property-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the project property is updated.|Inline|
|201|Created|Returned if the project property is created.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the project key or id is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to administer the project.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )
</aside>

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg) or *Administer Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project containing the property.

|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to administer the project.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project or property is not found.|None|

basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-project-role-actors">Project role actors</h1>

This resource represents the users assigned to [project roles](#api-group-Issue-comments). Use it to get, add, and remove default users from project roles. Also use it to add and remove users from a project role associated with a project.

## Set actors for project role

<a id="opIdsetActors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string/role/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "categorisedActors": {
      "atlassian-group-role-actor-id": [
        "952d12c3-5b5b-4d04-bb32-44d383afc4b2"
      ],
      "atlassian-user-role-actor": [
        "12345678-9abc-def1-2345-6789abcdef12"

    }
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/role/{id}`

Sets the actors for a project role for a project, replacing all existing actors.

To add actors to the project without overwriting the existing list, use [Add actors to project role](#api-rest-api-3-project-projectIdOrKey-role-id-post).

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project or *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "categorisedActors": {
    "atlassian-group-role-actor-id": [
      "952d12c3-5b5b-4d04-bb32-44d383afc4b2"
    ],
    "atlassian-user-role-actor": [
      "12345678-9abc-def1-2345-6789abcdef12"
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="set-actors-for-project-role-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrKey|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case sensitive).|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the project role. Use [Get all project roles](#api-rest-api-3-role-get) to get a list of project role IDs.|
|body|body|[ProjectRoleActorsUpdateBean](#schemaprojectroleactorsupdatebean)|true|The groups or users to associate with the project role for this project. Provide the user account ID, group name, or group ID. As a group's name can change, use of group ID is recommended.|
|» categorisedActors|body|object|false|The actors to add to the project role.<br><br>Add groups using:<br><br> *  `atlassian-group-role-actor` and a list of group names.<br> *  `atlassian-group-role-actor-id` and a list of group IDs.<br><br>As a group's name can change, use of `atlassian-group-role-actor-id` is recommended. For example, `"atlassian-group-role-actor-id":["eef79f81-0b89-4fca-a736-4be531a10869","77f6ab39-e755-4570-a6ae-2d7a8df0bcb8"]`.<br><br>Add users using `atlassian-user-role-actor` and a list of account IDs. For example, `"atlassian-user-role-actor":["12345678-9abc-def1-2345-6789abcdef12", "abcdef12-3456-789a-bcde-f123456789ab"]`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[string]|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"actors\":[{\"actorGroup\":{\"displayName\":\"jira-developers\",\"groupId\":\"952d12c3-5b5b-4d04-bb32-44d383afc4b2\",\"name\":\"jira-developers\"},\"displayName\":\"jira-developers\",\"id\":10240,\"name\":\"jira-developers\",\"type\":\"atlassian-group-role-actor\",\"user\":\"jira-developers\"},{\"actorUser\":{\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\"},\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"id\":10241,\"type\":\"atlassian-user-role-actor\"}],\"description\":\"A project role that represents developers in a project\",\"id\":10360,\"name\":\"Developers\",\"scope\":{\"project\":{\"id\":\"10000\",\"key\":\"KEY\",\"name\":\"Next Gen Project\"},\"type\":\"PROJECT\"},\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/MKY/role/10360\"}"
```

`POST /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/role/{id}`

Adds actors to a project role for the project.

To replace all actors for the project, use [Set actors for project role](#api-rest-api-3-project-projectIdOrKey-role-id-put).

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project or *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "groupId": [
    "952d12c3-5b5b-4d04-bb32-44d383afc4b2"
  ]
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrKey|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case sensitive).|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the project role. Use [Get all project roles](#api-rest-api-3-role-get) to get a list of project role IDs.|
|body|body|[ActorsMap](#schemaactorsmap)|true|The groups or users to associate with the project role for this project. Provide the user account ID, group name, or group ID. As a group's name can change, use of group ID is recommended.|
|» group|body|[string]|false|The name of the group to add. This parameter cannot be used with the `groupId` parameter. As a group's name can change, use of `groupId` is recommended.|
|» groupId|body|[string]|false|The ID of the group to add. This parameter cannot be used with the `group` parameter.|
|» user|body|[string]|false|The user account ID of the user to add.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"actors\":[{\"actorGroup\":{\"displayName\":\"jira-developers\",\"groupId\":\"952d12c3-5b5b-4d04-bb32-44d383afc4b2\",\"name\":\"jira-developers\"},\"displayName\":\"jira-developers\",\"id\":10240,\"name\":\"jira-developers\",\"type\":\"atlassian-group-role-actor\",\"user\":\"jira-developers\"},{\"actorUser\":{\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\"},\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"id\":10241,\"type\":\"atlassian-user-role-actor\"}],\"description\":\"A project role that represents developers in a project\",\"id\":10360,\"name\":\"Developers\",\"scope\":{\"project\":{\"id\":\"10000\",\"key\":\"KEY\",\"name\":\"Next Gen Project\"},\"type\":\"PROJECT\"},\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/MKY/role/10360\"}"
```

For the response below to be returned as a result of that request, the user *Mia Krystof* would have previously been added as a `user` actor for this project.|[ProjectRole](#schemaprojectrole)|

basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )

## Add default actors to project role

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/role/0/actors \

    ]
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/role/{id}/actors`

Adds [default actors](#api-rest-api-3-resolution-get) to a role. You may add groups or users, but you cannot add groups and users in the same request.

Changing a project role's default actors does not affect project role members for projects already created.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user": [
    "admin"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-default-actors-to-project-role-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the project role. Use [Get all project roles](#api-rest-api-3-role-get) to get a list of project role IDs.|
|body|body|[ActorInputBean](#schemaactorinputbean)|true|none|
|» group|body|[string]|false|The name of the group to add as a default actor. This parameter cannot be used with the `groupId` parameter. As a group's name can change,use of `groupId` is recommended. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. For example, `"group":["project-admin", "jira-developers"]`.|
|» groupId|body|[string]|false|The ID of the group to add as a default actor. This parameter cannot be used with the `group` parameter This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. For example, `"groupId":["77f6ab39-e755-4570-a6ae-2d7a8df0bcb8", "0c011f85-69ed-49c4-a801-3b18d0f771bc"]`.|
|» user|body|[string]|false|The account IDs of the users to add as default actors. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. For example, `"user":["5b10a2844c20165700ede21g", "5b109f2e9729b51b54dc274d"]`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"actors\":[{\"actorGroup\":{\"name\":\"jira-developers\",\"displayName\":\"jira-developers\",\"groupId\":\"952d12c3-5b5b-4d04-bb32-44d383afc4b2\"},\"displayName\":\"jira-developers\",\"id\":10240,\"name\":\"jira-developers\",\"type\":\"atlassian-group-role-actor\"}]}"
```

<h3 id="add-default-actors-to-project-role-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|

|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have administrative permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project role is not found.|None|

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-project-roles">Project roles</h1>

This resource represents the roles that users can play in projects. Use this resource to get, create, update, and delete project roles.

## Get project roles for project

<a id="opIdgetProjectRoles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string/role \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/role`

Returns a list of [project roles](https://support.atlassian.com/jira-cloud-administration/docs/manage-project-roles/) for the project returning the name and self URL for each role.

Note that all project roles are shared with all projects in Jira Cloud. See [Get all project roles](#api-rest-api-3-role-get) for more information.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for any project on the site or *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

|projectIdOrKey|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case sensitive).|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"Administrators\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/MKY/role/10002\",\"Developers\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/MKY/role/10000\",\"Users\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/MKY/role/10001\"}"
```

|404|Not Found|Returned if the project is not found or or if the user does not have administrative permissions for the project.|None|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**additionalProperties**|string(uri)|false|none|none|

|excludeInactiveUsers|query|boolean|false|Exclude inactive users.|
