## Get all project roles

<a id="opIdgetAllProjectRoles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/role \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/role`

Gets a list of all project roles, complete with project role details and default actors.

### About project roles ###

[Project roles](https://support.atlassian.com/jira-cloud-administration/docs/manage-project-roles/) are a flexible way to to associate users and groups with projects. In Jira Cloud, the list of project roles is shared globally with all projects, but each project can have a different set of actors associated with it (unlike groups, which have the same membership throughout all Jira applications).

Project roles are used in [permission schemes](#api-rest-api-3-permissionscheme-get), [email notification schemes](#api-rest-api-3-notificationscheme-get), [issue security levels](#api-rest-api-3-issuesecurityschemes-get), [comment visibility](#api-rest-api-3-comment-list-post), and workflow conditions.

#### Members and actors ####

In the Jira REST API, a member of a project role is called an *actor*. An *actor* is a group or user associated with a project role.

Actors may be set as [default members](https://support.atlassian.com/jira-cloud-administration/docs/manage-project-roles/#Specifying-'default-members'-for-a-project-role) of the project role or set at the project level:

 *  Default actors: Users and groups that are assigned to the project role for all newly created projects. The default actors can be removed at the project level later if desired.
 *  Actors: Users and groups that are associated with a project role for a project, which may differ from the default actors. This enables you to assign a user to different roles in different projects.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"[{\"actors\":[{\"actorGroup\":{\"displayName\":\"jira-developers\",\"groupId\":\"952d12c3-5b5b-4d04-bb32-44d383afc4b2\",\"name\":\"jira-developers\"},\"displayName\":\"jira-developers\",\"id\":10240,\"name\":\"jira-developers\",\"type\":\"atlassian-group-role-actor\",\"user\":\"jira-developers\"},{\"actorUser\":{\"accountId\":\"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g\"},\"displayName\":\"Mia Krystof\",\"id\":10241,\"type\":\"atlassian-user-role-actor\"}],\"description\":\"A project role that represents developers in a project\",\"id\":10360,\"name\":\"Developers\",\"scope\":{\"project\":{\"id\":\"10000\",\"key\":\"KEY\",\"name\":\"Next Gen Project\"},\"type\":\"PROJECT\"},\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/MKY/role/10360\"}]"
```

<h3 id="get-all-project-roles-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have administrative permissions.|None|

<h3 id="get-all-project-roles-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[ProjectRole](#schemaprojectrole)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

## Create project role

<a id="opIdcreateProjectRole"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/role \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "A project role that represents developers in a project",
    "name": "Developers"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/role`

Creates a new project role with no [default actors](#api-rest-api-3-resolution-get). You can use the [Add default actors to project role](#api-rest-api-3-role-id-actors-post) operation to add default actors to the project role after creating it.

*Note that although a new project role is available to all projects upon creation, any default actors that are associated with the project role are not added to projects that existed prior to the role being created.*<

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "A project role that represents developers in a project",
  "name": "Developers"
}
```

<h3 id="create-project-role-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateUpdateRoleRequestBean](#schemacreateupdaterolerequestbean)|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the project role. Required when fully updating a project role. Optional when creating or partially updating a project role.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the project role. Must be unique. Cannot begin or end with whitespace. The maximum length is 255 characters. Required when creating a project role. Optional when partially updating a project role.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"description\":\"A project role that represents developers in a project\",\"id\":10360,\"name\":\"Developers\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/MKY/role/10360\"}"
```

<h3 id="create-project-role-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[ProjectRole](#schemaprojectrole)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid. The `name` cannot be empty or start or end with whitespace.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have administrative permissions.|None|
|409|Conflict|Returned if a project role with the provided name already exists.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

## Delete project role

<a id="opIddeleteProjectRole"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/role/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /rest/api/3/role/{id}`

Deletes a project role. You must specify a replacement project role if you wish to delete a project role that is in use.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="delete-project-role-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the project role to delete. Use [Get all project roles](#api-rest-api-3-role-get) to get a list of project role IDs.|
|swap|query|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the project role that will replace the one being deleted. The swap will attempt to swap the role in schemes (notifications, permissions, issue security), workflows, worklogs and comments.|

<h3 id="delete-project-role-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the request is successful.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid or if the replacement project role is not found.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have administrative permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project role being deleted is not found.|None|
|409|Conflict|Returned if the project role being deleted is in use and a replacement project role is not specified in the request.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

`POST /rest/api/3/project-template`

Creates a project based on a custom template provided in the request.

The request body should contain the project details and the capabilities that comprise the project:

 *  `details` \- represents the project details settings
 *  `template` \- represents a list of capabilities responsible for creating specific parts of a project

A capability is defined as a unit of configuration for the project you want to create.

This operation is:

 *  [asynchronous](#async). Follow the `Location` link in the response header to determine the status of the task and use [Get task](#api-rest-api-3-task-taskId-get) to obtain subsequent updates.

***Note: This API is only supported for Jira Enterprise edition.***

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

## Edit a custom project template

<a id="opIdeditTemplate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project-template/edit-template \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "templateDescription": "string",
    "templateGenerationOptions": {
      "enableScreenDelegatedAdminSupport": true,
      "enableWorkflowDelegatedAdminSupport": true
    },
    "templateKey": "string",
    "templateName": "string"
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/project-template/edit-template`

Edit custom template

This API endpoint allows you to edit an existing customised template.

***Note: Custom Templates are only supported for Jira Enterprise edition.***

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "templateDescription": "string",
  "templateGenerationOptions": {
    "enableScreenDelegatedAdminSupport": true,
    "enableWorkflowDelegatedAdminSupport": true
  },
  "templateKey": "string",
  "templateName": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="edit-a-custom-project-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[EditTemplateRequest](#schemaedittemplaterequest)|true|The object containing the updated template details: name, description|
|» templateDescription|body|string|false|The description of the template|
|» templateGenerationOptions|body|[CustomTemplateOptions](#schemacustomtemplateoptions)|false|none|
|» templateKey|body|string|false|The unique identifier of the template|
|» templateName|body|string|false|The name of the template|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="edit-a-custom-project-template-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|200 response|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )

***Note: Custom Templates are only supported for Jira Enterprise edition.***

|projectId|query|string|false|optional - The \{@link String\} containing the project key linked to the custom template to retrieve|
|templateKey|query|string|false|optional - The \{@link String\} containing the key of the custom template to retrieve|

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-project-versions">Project versions</h1>

This resource represents project versions. Use it to get, get lists of, create, update, move, merge, and delete project versions. This resource also provides counts of issues by version.

## Get project versions paginated

<a id="opIdgetProjectVersionsPaginated"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string/version \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/version`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of all versions in a project. See the [Get project versions](#api-rest-api-3-project-projectIdOrKey-versions-get) resource if you want to get a full list of versions without pagination.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Browse Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.

<h3 id="get-project-versions-paginated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrKey|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case sensitive).|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|orderBy|query|string|false|[Order](#ordering) the results by a field:<br><br> *  `description` Sorts by version description.<br> *  `name` Sorts by version name.<br> *  `releaseDate` Sorts by release date, starting with the oldest date. Versions with no release date are listed last.<br> *  `sequence` Sorts by the order of appearance in the user interface.<br> *  `startDate` Sorts by start date, starting with the oldest date. Versions with no start date are listed last.|
|query|query|string|false|Filter the results using a literal string. Versions with matching `name` or `description` are returned (case insensitive).|
|status|query|string|false|A list of status values used to filter the results by version status. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. The status values are `released`, `unreleased`, and `archived`.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information in the response. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `issuesstatus` Returns the number of issues in each status category for each version.<br> *  `operations` Returns actions that can be performed on the specified version.<br> *  `driver` Returns the Atlassian account ID of the version driver.<br> *  `approvers` Returns a list containing the approvers for this version.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|orderBy|description|
|orderBy|-description|
|orderBy|+description|
|orderBy|name|
|orderBy|-name|
|orderBy|+name|
|orderBy|releaseDate|
|orderBy|-releaseDate|
|orderBy|+releaseDate|
|orderBy|sequence|
|orderBy|-sequence|
|orderBy|+sequence|
|orderBy|startDate|
|orderBy|-startDate|
|orderBy|+startDate|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"isLast\":false,\"maxResults\":2,\"nextPage\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/PR/version?startAt=2&maxResults=2\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/PR/version?startAt=0&maxResults=2\",\"startAt\":0,\"total\":7,\"values\":[{\"archived\":false,\"description\":\"An excellent version\",\"id\":\"10000\",\"name\":\"New Version 1\",\"overdue\":true,\"projectId\":10000,\"releaseDate\":\"2010-07-06\",\"released\":true,\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/version/10000\",\"userReleaseDate\":\"6/Jul/2010\"},{\"archived\":false,\"description\":\"Minor Bugfix version\",\"id\":\"10010\",\"issuesStatusForFixVersion\":{\"done\":100,\"inProgress\":20,\"toDo\":10,\"unmapped\":0},\"name\":\"Next Version\",\"overdue\":false,\"projectId\":10000,\"released\":false,\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/version/10010\"}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-project-versions-paginated-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PageBeanVersion](#schemapagebeanversion)|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project is not found or the user does not have permission to view it.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Create version

<a id="opIdcreateVersion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/version \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "archived": false,
    "description": "An excellent version",
    "name": "New Version 1",
    "projectId": 10000,
    "releaseDate": "2010-07-06",
    "released": true
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/version`

Creates a project version.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg) or *Administer Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project the version is added to.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "archived": false,
  "description": "An excellent version",
  "name": "New Version 1",
  "projectId": 10000,
  "releaseDate": "2010-07-06",
  "released": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[Version](#schemaversion)|true|none|
|» archived|body|boolean|false|Indicates that the version is archived. Optional when creating or updating a version.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the version. Optional when creating or updating a version. The maximum size is 16,384 bytes.|
|» driver|body|string|false|The Atlassian account ID of the version driver. Optional when creating or updating a version. If the expand option `driver` is used, returns the Atlassian account ID of the driver.|
|» expand|body|string|false|Use [expand](em>#expansion) to include additional information about version in the response. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `operations` Returns the list of operations available for this version.<br> *  `issuesstatus` Returns the count of issues in this version for each of the status categories *to do*, *in progress*, *done*, and *unmapped*. The *unmapped* property contains a count of issues with a status other than *to do*, *in progress*, and *done*.<br> *  `driver` Returns the Atlassian account ID of the version driver.<br> *  `approvers` Returns a list containing approvers for this version.<br><br>Optional for create and update.|
|» moveUnfixedIssuesTo|body|string(uri)|false|The URL of the self link to the version to which all unfixed issues are moved when a version is released. Not applicable when creating a version. Optional when updating a version.|
|» name|body|string|false|The unique name of the version. Required when creating a version. Optional when updating a version. The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|» project|body|string|false|Deprecated. Use `projectId`.|
|» projectId|body|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the project to which this version is attached. Required when creating a version. Not applicable when updating a version.|
|» releaseDate|body|string(date)|false|The release date of the version. Expressed in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-mm-dd). Optional when creating or updating a version.|
|» released|body|boolean|false|Indicates that the version is released. If the version is released a request to release again is ignored. Not applicable when creating a version. Optional when updating a version.|
|» startDate|body|string(date)|false|The start date of the version. Expressed in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-mm-dd). Optional when creating or updating a version.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
"{\"archived\":false,\"description\":\"An excellent version\",\"id\":\"10000\",\"name\":\"New Version 1\",\"project\":\"PXA\",\"projectId\":10000,\"releaseDate\":\"2010-07-06\",\"released\":true,\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/version/10000\",\"userReleaseDate\":\"6/Jul/2010\"}"
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "current_count": 0,
  "entity_type": "string",
  "error_code": "string",
  "limit_type": "string",
  "max_allowed_limit": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "scope_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-version-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returned if the request is successful.|[Version](#schemaversion)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  the project is not found.<br> *  the user does not have the required permissions.|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|422 response|[LimitExceededResponseBean](#schemalimitexceededresponsebean)|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )
</aside>

Deletes a project version.

Deprecated, use [ Delete and replace version](#api-rest-api-3-version-id-removeAndSwap-post) that supports swapping version values in custom fields, in addition to the swapping for `fixVersion` and `affectedVersion` provided in this resource.

Alternative versions can be provided to update issues that use the deleted version in `fixVersion` or `affectedVersion`. If alternatives are not provided, occurrences of `fixVersion` and `affectedVersion` that contain the deleted version are cleared.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg) or *Administer Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that contains the version.

<h3 id="delete-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the version.|
|moveFixIssuesTo|query|string|false|The ID of the version to update `fixVersion` to when the field contains the deleted version. The replacement version must be in the same project as the version being deleted and cannot be the version being deleted.|
|moveAffectedIssuesTo|query|string|false|The ID of the version to update `affectedVersion` to when the field contains the deleted version. The replacement version must be in the same project as the version being deleted and cannot be the version being deleted.|

<h3 id="delete-version-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the version is deleted.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if:<br><br> *  the authentication credentials are incorrect.<br> *  the user does not have the required permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the version is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )
</aside>

## Merge versions

<a id="opIdmergeVersions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/version/string/mergeto/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/version/{id}/mergeto/{moveIssuesTo}`

Merges two project versions. The merge is completed by deleting the version specified in `id` and replacing any occurrences of its ID in `fixVersion` with the version ID specified in `moveIssuesTo`.

Consider using [ Delete and replace version](#api-rest-api-3-version-id-removeAndSwap-post) instead. This resource supports swapping version values in `fixVersion`, `affectedVersion`, and custom fields.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg) or *Administer Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that contains the version.

<h3 id="merge-versions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the version to delete.|
|moveIssuesTo|path|string|true|The ID of the version to merge into.|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="merge-versions-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the version is deleted.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if:<br><br> *  the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.<br> *  the user does not have the required permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the version to be deleted or the version to merge to are not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )
</aside>

## Move version

<a id="opIdmoveVersion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/version/string/move \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "after": "https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/~ver~/version/10000"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/version/{id}/move`

Modifies the version's sequence within the project, which affects the display order of the versions in Jira.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Browse projects* project permission for the project that contains the version.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "after": "https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/~ver~/version/10000"
}
```

<h3 id="move-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the version to be moved.|
|body|body|[VersionMoveBean](#schemaversionmovebean)|true|none|
|» after|body|string(uri)|false|The URL (self link) of the version after which to place the moved version. Cannot be used with `position`.|
|» position|body|string|false|An absolute position in which to place the moved version. Cannot be used with `after`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» position|Earlier|
|» position|Later|
|» position|First|
|» position|Last|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"archived\":false,\"description\":\"An excellent version\",\"id\":\"10000\",\"name\":\"New Version 1\",\"overdue\":true,\"projectId\":10000,\"releaseDate\":\"2010-07-06\",\"released\":true,\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/version/10000\",\"userReleaseDate\":\"6/Jul/2010\"}"
```

<h3 id="move-version-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[Version](#schemaversion)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if:<br><br> *  no body parameters are provided.<br> *  `after` and `position` are provided.<br> *  `position` is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if:<br><br> *  the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br> *  the user does not have the required commissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the version or move after version are not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )
</aside>

## Delete and replace version

<a id="opIddeleteAndReplaceVersion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/version/string/removeAndSwap \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "customFieldReplacementList": [
      {
        "customFieldId": 0,
        "moveTo": 0
      }
    ],
    "moveAffectedIssuesTo": 0,
    "moveFixIssuesTo": 0
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/version/{id}/removeAndSwap`

Deletes a project version.

Alternative versions can be provided to update issues that use the deleted version in `fixVersion`, `affectedVersion`, or any version picker custom fields. If alternatives are not provided, occurrences of `fixVersion`, `affectedVersion`, and any version picker custom field, that contain the deleted version, are cleared. Any replacement version must be in the same project as the version being deleted and cannot be the version being deleted.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg) or *Administer Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project that contains the version.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "customFieldReplacementList": [
    {
      "customFieldId": 0,
      "moveTo": 0
    }
  ],
  "moveAffectedIssuesTo": 0,
  "moveFixIssuesTo": 0
}
```

<h3 id="delete-and-replace-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the version.|
|body|body|[DeleteAndReplaceVersionBean](#schemadeleteandreplaceversionbean)|true|none|
|» customFieldReplacementList|body|[[CustomFieldReplacement](#schemacustomfieldreplacement)]|false|An array of custom field IDs (`customFieldId`) and version IDs (`moveTo`) to update when the fields contain the deleted version.|
|» moveAffectedIssuesTo|body|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the version to update `affectedVersion` to when the field contains the deleted version.|
|» moveFixIssuesTo|body|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the version to update `fixVersion` to when the field contains the deleted version.|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="delete-and-replace-version-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the version is deleted.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if:<br><br> *  the version to delete is not found.<br> *  the user does not have the required permissions.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-projects">Projects</h1>

This resource represents projects. Use it to get, create, update, and delete projects. Also get statuses available to a project, a project's notification schemes, and update a project's type.

<a id="opIdcreateProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "assigneeType": "PROJECT_LEAD",
    "avatarId": 10200,
    "categoryId": 10120,
    "description": "Cloud migration initiative",
    "issueSecurityScheme": 10001,
    "key": "EX",
    "leadAccountId": "5b10a0effa615349cb016cd8",
    "name": "Example",
    "notificationScheme": 10021,
    "permissionScheme": 10011,
    "projectTemplateKey": "com.atlassian.jira-core-project-templates:jira-core-simplified-process-control",
    "projectTypeKey": "business",
    "url": "http://atlassian.com"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/project`

Creates a project based on a project type template, as shown in the following table:

| Project Type Key | Project Template Key |  
|--|--|  
| `business` | `com.atlassian.jira-core-project-templates:jira-core-simplified-content-management`, `com.atlassian.jira-core-project-templates:jira-core-simplified-document-approval`, `com.atlassian.jira-core-project-templates:jira-core-simplified-lead-tracking`, `com.atlassian.jira-core-project-templates:jira-core-simplified-process-control`, `com.atlassian.jira-core-project-templates:jira-core-simplified-procurement`, `com.atlassian.jira-core-project-templates:jira-core-simplified-project-management`, `com.atlassian.jira-core-project-templates:jira-core-simplified-recruitment`, `com.atlassian.jira-core-project-templates:jira-core-simplified-task-tracking` |  
| `service_desk` | `com.atlassian.servicedesk:simplified-it-service-management`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:simplified-external-service-desk`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:simplified-hr-service-desk`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:simplified-facilities-service-desk`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:simplified-legal-service-desk`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:simplified-analytics-service-desk`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:simplified-marketing-service-desk`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:simplified-design-service-desk`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:simplified-sales-service-desk`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:simplified-finance-service-desk`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:company-managed-blank-service-project`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:company-managed-general-service-project`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:team-managed-general-service-project`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:next-gen-it-service-desk`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:next-gen-hr-service-desk`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:next-gen-legal-service-desk`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:next-gen-marketing-service-desk`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:next-gen-facilities-service-desk`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:next-gen-analytics-service-desk`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:next-gen-finance-service-desk`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:next-gen-design-service-desk`, `com.atlassian.servicedesk:next-gen-sales-service-desk` |  
| `software` | `com.pyxis.greenhopper.jira:gh-simplified-agility-kanban`, `com.pyxis.greenhopper.jira:gh-simplified-agility-scrum`, `com.pyxis.greenhopper.jira:gh-simplified-basic`, `com.pyxis.greenhopper.jira:gh-simplified-kanban-classic`, `com.pyxis.greenhopper.jira:gh-simplified-scrum-classic` |  
| `customer_service` | `com.atlassian.jcs:customer-service-management` |  
The project types are available according to the installed Jira features as follows:

 *  Jira Core, the default, enables `business` projects.
 *  Jira Service Management enables `service_desk` projects.
 *  Jira Software enables `software` projects.
 *  Jira Customer Service enables `customer_service` projects.

To determine which features are installed, go to **Jira settings** > **Apps** > **Manage apps** and review the System Apps list. To add Jira Software or Jira Service Management into a JIRA instance, use **Jira settings** > **Apps** > **Finding new apps**. For more information, see [ Managing add-ons](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/S31NLg).

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "assigneeType": "PROJECT_LEAD",
  "avatarId": 10200,
  "categoryId": 10120,
  "description": "Cloud migration initiative",
  "issueSecurityScheme": 10001,
  "key": "EX",
  "leadAccountId": "5b10a0effa615349cb016cd8",
  "name": "Example",
  "notificationScheme": 10021,
  "permissionScheme": 10011,
  "projectTemplateKey": "com.atlassian.jira-core-project-templates:jira-core-simplified-process-control",
  "projectTypeKey": "business",
  "url": "http://atlassian.com"
}
```

<h3 id="create-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateProjectDetails](#schemacreateprojectdetails)|true|The JSON representation of the project being created.|
|» assigneeType|body|string|false|The default assignee when creating issues for this project.|
|» avatarId|body|integer(int64)|false|An integer value for the project's avatar.|
|» categoryId|body|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the project's category. A complete list of category IDs is found using the [Get all project categories](#api-rest-api-3-projectCategory-get) operation.|
|» description|body|string|false|A brief description of the project.|
|» fieldConfigurationScheme|body|integer(int64)|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated use [fieldScheme](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-field-schemes/#api-group-field-schemes) instead. The ID of the field configuration scheme for the project. Use the [Get all field configuration schemes](#api-rest-api-3-fieldconfigurationscheme-get) operation to get a list of field configuration scheme IDs. If you specify the field configuration scheme you cannot specify the project template key.|
|» fieldScheme|body|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the field scheme for the project. Use the [Get field schemes](#api-rest-api-3-config-fieldschemes-get) operation to get a list of field scheme IDs. If you specify the field scheme you cannot specify the project template key.|
|» issueSecurityScheme|body|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the issue security scheme for the project, which enables you to control who can and cannot view issues. Use the [Get issue security schemes](#api-rest-api-3-issuesecurityschemes-get) resource to get all issue security scheme IDs.|
|» issueTypeScheme|body|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the issue type scheme for the project. Use the [Get all issue type schemes](#api-rest-api-3-issuetypescheme-get) operation to get a list of issue type scheme IDs. If you specify the issue type scheme you cannot specify the project template key.|
|» issueTypeScreenScheme|body|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the issue type screen scheme for the project. Use the [Get all issue type screen schemes](#api-rest-api-3-issuetypescreenscheme-get) operation to get a list of issue type screen scheme IDs. If you specify the issue type screen scheme you cannot specify the project template key.|
|» key|body|string|true|Project keys must be unique and start with an uppercase letter followed by one or more uppercase alphanumeric characters. The maximum length is 10 characters.|
|» lead|body|string|false|This parameter is deprecated because of privacy changes. Use `leadAccountId` instead. See the [migration guide](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/) for details. The user name of the project lead. Either `lead` or `leadAccountId` must be set when creating a project. Cannot be provided with `leadAccountId`.|
|» leadAccountId|body|string|false|The account ID of the project lead. Either `lead` or `leadAccountId` must be set when creating a project. Cannot be provided with `lead`.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the project.|
|» notificationScheme|body|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the notification scheme for the project. Use the [Get notification schemes](#api-rest-api-3-notificationscheme-get) resource to get a list of notification scheme IDs.|
|» permissionScheme|body|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the permission scheme for the project. Use the [Get all permission schemes](#api-rest-api-3-permissionscheme-get) resource to see a list of all permission scheme IDs.|
|» projectTemplateKey|body|string|false|A predefined configuration for a project. The type of the `projectTemplateKey` must match with the type of the `projectTypeKey`.|
|» projectTypeKey|body|string|false|The [project type](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/GwiiLQ#Jiraapplicationsoverview-Productfeaturesandprojecttypes), which defines the application-specific feature set. If you don't specify the project template you have to specify the project type.|
|» url|body|string|false|A link to information about this project, such as project documentation|
|» workflowScheme|body|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the workflow scheme for the project. Use the [Get all workflow schemes](#api-rest-api-3-workflowscheme-get) operation to get a list of workflow scheme IDs. If you specify the workflow scheme you cannot specify the project template key.|

## Get recent projects

<a id="opIdgetRecent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/recent \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/project/recent`

Returns a list of up to 20 projects recently viewed by the user that are still visible to the user.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Projects are returned only where the user has one of:

 *  *Browse Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.
 *  *Administer Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.
 *  *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-recent-projects-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information in the response. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expanded options include:<br><br> *  `description` Returns the project description.<br> *  `projectKeys` Returns all project keys associated with a project.<br> *  `lead` Returns information about the project lead.<br> *  `issueTypes` Returns all issue types associated with the project.<br> *  `url` Returns the URL associated with the project.<br> *  `permissions` Returns the permissions associated with the project.<br> *  `insight` EXPERIMENTAL. Returns the insight details of total issue count and last issue update time for the project.<br> *  `*` Returns the project with all available expand options.|
|properties|query|[[StringList](#schemastringlist)]|false|EXPERIMENTAL. A list of project properties to return for the project. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Invalid property names are ignored.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"[{\"avatarUrls\":{\"16x16\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/secure/projectavatar?size=xsmall&pid=10000\",\"24x24\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/secure/projectavatar?size=small&pid=10000\",\"32x32\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/secure/projectavatar?size=medium&pid=10000\",\"48x48\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/secure/projectavatar?size=large&pid=10000\"},\"id\":\"10000\",\"insight\":{\"lastIssueUpdateTime\":1619069825000,\"totalIssueCount\":100},\"key\":\"EX\",\"name\":\"Example\",\"projectCategory\":{\"description\":\"First Project Category\",\"id\":\"10000\",\"name\":\"FIRST\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/projectCategory/10000\"},\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/EX\",\"simplified\":false,\"style\":\"CLASSIC\"},{\"avatarUrls\":{\"16x16\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/secure/projectavatar?size=xsmall&pid=10001\",\"24x24\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/secure/projectavatar?size=small&pid=10001\",\"32x32\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/secure/projectavatar?size=medium&pid=10001\",\"48x48\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/secure/projectavatar?size=large&pid=10001\"},\"id\":\"10001\",\"insight\":{\"lastIssueUpdateTime\":1619069825000,\"totalIssueCount\":100},\"key\":\"ABC\",\"name\":\"Alphabetical\",\"projectCategory\":{\"description\":\"First Project Category\",\"id\":\"10000\",\"name\":\"FIRST\",\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/projectCategory/10000\"},\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/ABC\",\"simplified\":false,\"style\":\"CLASSIC\"}]"
```

## Get projects paginated

<a id="opIdsearchProjects"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/project/search`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of projects visible to the user.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Projects are returned only where the user has one of:

 *  *Browse Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.
 *  *Administer Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.
 *  *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-projects-paginated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page. Must be less than or equal to 100. If a value greater than 100 is provided, the `maxResults` parameter will default to 100.|
|orderBy|query|string|false|[Order](#ordering) the results by a field.<br><br> *  `category` Sorts by project category. A complete list of category IDs is found using [Get all project categories](#api-rest-api-3-projectCategory-get).<br> *  `issueCount` Sorts by the total number of issues in each project.<br> *  `key` Sorts by project key.<br> *  `lastIssueUpdatedTime` Sorts by the last issue update time.<br> *  `name` Sorts by project name.<br> *  `owner` Sorts by project lead.<br> *  `archivedDate` EXPERIMENTAL. Sorts by project archived date.<br> *  `deletedDate` EXPERIMENTAL. Sorts by project deleted date.|
|id|query|[integer(int64)]|false|The project IDs to filter the results by. To include multiple IDs, provide an ampersand-separated list. For example, `id=10000&id=10001`. Up to 50 project IDs can be provided.|
|keys|query|[string]|false|The project keys to filter the results by. To include multiple keys, provide an ampersand-separated list. For example, `keys=PA&keys=PB`. Up to 50 project keys can be provided.|
|query|query|string|false|Filter the results using a literal string. Projects with a matching `key` or `name` are returned (case insensitive).|
|typeKey|query|string|false|Orders results by the [project type](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/GwiiLQ#Jiraapplicationsoverview-Productfeaturesandprojecttypes). This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Valid values are `business`, `service_desk`, and `software`.|
|categoryId|query|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the project's category. A complete list of category IDs is found using the [Get all project categories](#api-rest-api-3-projectCategory-get) operation.|
|action|query|string|false|Filter results by projects for which the user can:<br><br> *  `view` the project, meaning that they have one of the following permissions:<br>    <br>     *  *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.<br>     *  *Administer projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.<br>     *  *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).<br> *  `browse` the project, meaning that they have the *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.<br> *  `edit` the project, meaning that they have one of the following permissions:<br>    <br>     *  *Administer projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.<br>     *  *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).<br> *  `create` the project, meaning that they have the *Create issues* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project in which the issue is created.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information in the response. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expanded options include:<br><br> *  `description` Returns the project description.<br> *  `projectKeys` Returns all project keys associated with a project.<br> *  `lead` Returns information about the project lead.<br> *  `issueTypes` Returns all issue types associated with the project.<br> *  `url` Returns the URL associated with the project.<br> *  `insight` EXPERIMENTAL. Returns the insight details of total issue count and last issue update time for the project.|
|status|query|[string]|false|EXPERIMENTAL. Filter results by project status:<br><br> *  `live` Search live projects.<br> *  `archived` Search archived projects.<br> *  `deleted` Search deleted projects, those in the recycle bin.|
|properties|query|[[StringList](#schemastringlist)]|false|EXPERIMENTAL. A list of project properties to return for the project. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list.|
|propertyQuery|query|string|false|EXPERIMENTAL. A query string used to search properties. The query string cannot be specified using a JSON object. For example, to search for the value of `nested` from `{"something":{"nested":1,"other":2}}` use `[thepropertykey].something.nested=1`. Note that the propertyQuery key is enclosed in square brackets to enable searching where the propertyQuery key includes dot (.) or equals (=) characters. Note that `thepropertykey` is only returned when included in `properties`.|

> Example responses

## Get project

<a id="opIdgetProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}`

Returns the [project details](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/ahLpNw) for a project.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.

<h3 id="get-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrKey|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case sensitive).|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information in the response. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Note that the project description, issue types, and project lead are included in all responses by default. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `description` The project description.<br> *  `issueTypes` The issue types associated with the project.<br> *  `lead` The project lead.<br> *  `projectKeys` All project keys associated with the project.<br> *  `issueTypeHierarchy` The project issue type hierarchy.|
|properties|query|[string]|false|A list of project properties to return for the project. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Note that only the properties named here are returned in `properties` in the response; that object is empty when this parameter is omitted.|

## Update project

<a id="opIdupdateProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/10001 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "assigneeType": "PROJECT_LEAD",
    "avatarId": 10200,
    "categoryId": 10120,
    "description": "Cloud migration initiative",
    "issueSecurityScheme": 10001,
    "key": "EX",
    "leadAccountId": "5b10a0effa615349cb016cd8",
    "name": "Example",
    "notificationScheme": 10021,
    "permissionScheme": 10011,
    "url": "http://atlassian.com"
  }'
```

`PUT /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}`

Updates the [project details](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/ahLpNw) of a project.

All parameters are optional in the body of the request. Schemes will only be updated if they are included in the request, any omitted schemes will be left unchanged.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg). is only needed when changing the schemes or project key. Otherwise you will only need *Administer Projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg)

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "assigneeType": "PROJECT_LEAD",
  "avatarId": 10200,
  "categoryId": 10120,
  "description": "Cloud migration initiative",
  "issueSecurityScheme": 10001,
  "key": "EX",
  "leadAccountId": "5b10a0effa615349cb016cd8",
  "name": "Example",
  "notificationScheme": 10021,
  "permissionScheme": 10011,
  "url": "http://atlassian.com"
}
```

<h3 id="update-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrKey|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case sensitive).|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information in the response. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Note that the project description, issue types, and project lead are included in all responses by default. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `description` The project description.<br> *  `issueTypes` The issue types associated with the project.<br> *  `lead` The project lead.<br> *  `projectKeys` All project keys associated with the project.|
|body|body|[UpdateProjectDetails](#schemaupdateprojectdetails)|true|The project details to be updated.|
|» assigneeType|body|string|false|The default assignee when creating issues for this project.|
|» avatarId|body|integer(int64)|false|An integer value for the project's avatar.|
|» categoryId|body|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the project's category. A complete list of category IDs is found using the [Get all project categories](#api-rest-api-3-projectCategory-get) operation. To remove the project category from the project, set the value to `-1.`|
|» description|body|string|false|A brief description of the project.|
|» issueSecurityScheme|body|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the issue security scheme for the project, which enables you to control who can and cannot view issues. Use the [Get issue security schemes](#api-rest-api-3-issuesecurityschemes-get) resource to get all issue security scheme IDs.|
|» key|body|string|false|Project keys must be unique and start with an uppercase letter followed by one or more uppercase alphanumeric characters. The maximum length is 10 characters.|
|» lead|body|string|false|This parameter is deprecated because of privacy changes. Use `leadAccountId` instead. See the [migration guide](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/) for details. The user name of the project lead. Cannot be provided with `leadAccountId`.|
|» leadAccountId|body|string|false|The account ID of the project lead. Cannot be provided with `lead`.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the project.|
|» notificationScheme|body|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the notification scheme for the project. Use the [Get notification schemes](#api-rest-api-3-notificationscheme-get) resource to get a list of notification scheme IDs.|
|» permissionScheme|body|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the permission scheme for the project. Use the [Get all permission schemes](#api-rest-api-3-permissionscheme-get) resource to see a list of all permission scheme IDs.|
|» releasedProjectKeys|body|[string]|false|Previous project keys to be released from the current project. Released keys must belong to the current project and not contain the current project key|
|» url|body|string|false|A link to information about this project, such as project documentation|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» assigneeType|PROJECT_LEAD|
|» assigneeType|UNASSIGNED|

## Delete project

<a id="opIddeleteProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/10001 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}`

Deletes a project.

You can't delete a project if it's archived. To delete an archived project, restore the project and then delete it. To restore a project, use the Jira UI.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="delete-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrKey|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case sensitive).|
|enableUndo|query|boolean|false|Whether this project is placed in the Jira recycle bin where it will be available for restoration.|

<h3 id="delete-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the project is deleted.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project is not found or the user does not have permission to delete it.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

## Archive project

<a id="opIdarchiveProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string/archive \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/archive`

Archives a project. You can't delete a project if it's archived. To delete an archived project, restore the project and then delete it. To restore a project, use the Jira UI.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="archive-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrKey|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case sensitive).|

## Delete project asynchronously

<a id="opIddeleteProjectAsynchronously"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/string/delete \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/delete`

Deletes a project asynchronously.

This operation is:

 *  transactional, that is, if part of the delete fails the project is not deleted.
 *  [asynchronous](#async). Follow the `location` link in the response to determine the status of the task and use [Get task](#api-rest-api-3-task-taskId-get) to obtain subsequent updates.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="delete-project-asynchronously-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectIdOrKey|path|string|true|The project ID or project key (case sensitive).|

> Example responses

> 303 Response

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "elapsedRuntime": 0,
  "finished": 0,
  "id": "string",
  "lastUpdate": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "progress": 0,
  "result": null,
  "self": "http://example.com",
  "started": 0,
  "status": "ENQUEUED",
  "submitted": 0,
  "submittedBy": 0
}
```

<h3 id="delete-project-asynchronously-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|303|See Other|Returned if the request is successful.|[TaskProgressBeanObject](#schemataskprogressbeanobject)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project is not found or the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-configuration )
</aside>

## Get all statuses for project

`GET /rest/api/3/project/{projectIdOrKey}/statuses`

Returns the valid statuses for a project. The statuses are grouped by issue type, as each project has a set of valid issue types and each issue type has a set of valid statuses.

This operation can be accessed anonymously.

## Get project issue type hierarchy

<a id="opIdgetHierarchy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/project/0/hierarchy \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/project/{projectId}/hierarchy`

Get the issue type hierarchy for a next-gen project.

The issue type hierarchy for a project consists of:

 *  *Epic* at level 1 (optional).
 *  One or more issue types at level 0 such as *Story*, *Task*, or *Bug*. Where the issue type *Epic* is defined, these issue types are used to break down the content of an epic.
 *  *Subtask* at level -1 (optional). This issue type enables level 0 issue types to be broken down into components. Issues based on a level -1 issue type must have a parent issue.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Browse projects* [project permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg) for the project.

<h3 id="get-project-issue-type-hierarchy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the project.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"hierarchy\":[{\"issueTypes\":[{\"avatarId\":10324,\"entityId\":\"ce32639b-8911-4689-81da-65681f451516\",\"id\":10008,\"name\":\"Story\"},{\"avatarId\":10324,\"entityId\":\"ffdbced5-fbfc-4370-a848-94e2ce3751af\",\"id\":10001,\"name\":\"Bug\"}],\"level\":0,\"name\":\"Base\"},{\"issueTypes\":[{\"avatarId\":10179,\"entityId\":\"80f20d47-34dc-4680-8937-936b7e762a35\",\"id\":10007,\"name\":\"Epic\"}],\"level\":1,\"name\":\"Epic\"},{\"issueTypes\":[{\"avatarId\":10573,\"entityId\":\"210b4879-15cc-414c-9746-f8f6b6be0a72\",\"id\":10009,\"name\":\"Subtask\"}],\"level\":-1,\"name\":\"Subtask\"}],\"projectId\":10030}"
```

<h3 id="get-project-issue-type-hierarchy-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[ProjectIssueTypeHierarchy](#schemaprojectissuetypehierarchy)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the project is not found or the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-screen-schemes">Screen schemes</h1>

This resource represents screen schemes in classic projects. Use it to get, create, update, and delete screen schemes.

## Get screen schemes

<a id="opIdgetScreenSchemes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/screenscheme \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/screenscheme`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of screen schemes.

Only screen schemes used in classic projects are returned.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-screen-schemes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|id|query|[integer(int64)]|false|The list of screen scheme IDs. To include multiple IDs, provide an ampersand-separated list. For example, `id=10000&id=10001`.|

|orderBy|query|string|false|[Order](#ordering) the results by a field:<br><br> *  `id` Sorts by screen scheme ID.<br> *  `name` Sorts by screen scheme name.|

## Create screen scheme

`POST /rest/api/3/screenscheme`

Creates a screen scheme.

```json
{
  "description": "Manage employee data",
```

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-screens">Screens</h1>

This resource represents the screens used to record issue details. Use it to:

 *  get details of all screens.
 *  get details of all the fields available for use on screens.
 *  create screens.
 *  delete screens.
 *  update screens.
 *  add a field to the default screen.

## Get screens for a field

<a id="opIdgetScreensForField"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/field/string/screens \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/field/{fieldId}/screens`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of the screens a field is used in.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-screens-for-a-field-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fieldId|path|string|true|The ID of the field to return screens for.|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|expand|query|string|false|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information about screens in the response. This parameter accepts `tab` which returns details about the screen tabs the field is used in.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"isLast\":false,\"maxResults\":1,\"startAt\":0,\"total\":5,\"values\":[{\"id\":10001,\"name\":\"Default Screen\",\"description\":\"Provides for the update of all system fields.\",\"tab\":{\"id\":10000,\"name\":\"Fields Tab\"}}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-screens-for-a-field-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PageBeanScreenWithTab](#schemapagebeanscreenwithtab)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )
</aside>

## Get screens

<a id="opIdgetScreens"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/screens \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/screens`

Returns a [paginated](#pagination) list of all screens or those specified by one or more screen IDs.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

<h3 id="get-screens-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|id|query|[integer(int64)]|false|The list of screen IDs. To include multiple IDs, provide an ampersand-separated list. For example, `id=10000&id=10001`.|
|queryString|query|string|false|String used to perform a case-insensitive partial match with screen name.|
|scope|query|[string]|false|The scope filter string. To filter by multiple scope, provide an ampersand-separated list. For example, `scope=GLOBAL&scope=PROJECT`.|
|orderBy|query|string|false|[Order](#ordering) the results by a field:<br><br> *  `id` Sorts by screen ID.<br> *  `name` Sorts by screen name.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|scope|GLOBAL|
|scope|TEMPLATE|
|scope|PROJECT|
|orderBy|name|
|orderBy|-name|
|orderBy|+name|
|orderBy|id|
|orderBy|-id|
|orderBy|+id|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"isLast\":true,\"maxResults\":100,\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/screens\",\"startAt\":0,\"total\":3,\"values\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":\"Default Screen\",\"description\":\"Provides for the update all system fields.\"},{\"id\":2,\"name\":\"Workflow Screen\",\"description\":\"This screen is used in the workflow and enables you to assign issues.\"},{\"id\":3,\"name\":\"Resolve Issue Screen\",\"description\":\"Offers the ability to set resolution, change fix versions, and assign an issue.\"}]}"
```

<h3 id="get-screens-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[PageBeanScreen](#schemapagebeanscreen)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )
</aside>

## Create screen

<a id="opIdcreateScreen"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/screens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Enables changes to resolution and linked issues.",
    "name": "Resolve Security Issue Screen"
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/screens`

Creates a screen with a default field tab.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Enables changes to resolution and linked issues.",
  "name": "Resolve Security Issue Screen"
}
```

<h3 id="create-screen-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ScreenDetails](#schemascreendetails)|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the screen. The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the screen. The name must be unique. The maximum length is 255 characters.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
"{\"id\":10005,\"name\":\"Resolve Security Issue Screen\",\"description\":\"Enables changes to resolution and linked issues.\"}"
```

> 400 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"The name is used by another screen.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

> 403 Response

```json
"{\"errorMessages\":[\"Only Jira administrators can manage screens.\"],\"errors\":{}}"
```

<h3 id="create-screen-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returned if the request is successful.|[Screen](#schemascreen)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is not valid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the required permissions.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: manage:jira-project )
</aside>

## Search statuses paginated

<a id="opIdsearch"></a>

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/statuses/search`

Returns a [paginated](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/intro/#pagination) list of statuses that match a search on name or project.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:**

 *  *Administer projects* [project permission.](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/yodKLg)

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|query|string|false|The project the status is part of or null for global statuses.|
|startAt|query|integer(int64)|false|The index of the first item to return in a page of results (page offset).|
|maxResults|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|searchString|query|string|false|Term to match status names against or null to search for all statuses in the search scope.|
|statusCategory|query|string|false|Category of the status to filter by. The supported values are: `TODO`, `IN_PROGRESS`, and `DONE`.|

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-tasks">Tasks</h1>

This resource represents a [long-running asynchronous tasks](#async-operations). Use it to obtain details about the progress of a long-running task or cancel a long-running task.

## Get task

<a id="opIdgetTask"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/task/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/task/{taskId}`

Returns the status of a [long-running asynchronous task](#async).

When a task has finished, this operation returns the JSON blob applicable to the task. See the documentation of the operation that created the task for details. Task details are not permanently retained. As of September 2019, details are retained for 14 days although this period may change without notice.

**Deprecation notice:** The required OAuth 2.0 scopes will be updated on June 15, 2024.

 *  `read:jira-work`

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** either of:

 *  *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).
 *  Creator of the task.

<h3 id="get-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|taskId|path|string|true|The ID of the task.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"self\":\"https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/task/1\",\"id\":\"1\",\"description\":\"Task description\",\"status\":\"COMPLETE\",\"result\":\"the task result, this may be any JSON\",\"submittedBy\":10000,\"progress\":100,\"elapsedRuntime\":156,\"submitted\":1501708132800,\"started\":1501708132900,\"finished\":1501708133000,\"lastUpdate\":1501708133000}"
```

<h3 id="get-task-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|[TaskProgressBeanObject](#schemataskprogressbeanobject)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the necessary permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the task is not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, OAuth2 ( Scopes: read:jira-work )
</aside>

## Add Atlassian team to plan

<a id="opIdaddAtlassianTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/plans/plan/0/team/atlassian \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "capacity": 200,
    "id": "AtlassianTeamId",
    "issueSourceId": 0,
    "planningStyle": "Scrum",
    "sprintLength": 2
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/plans/plan/{planId}/team/atlassian`

Adds an existing Atlassian team to a plan and configures their plannning settings.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "capacity": 200,
  "id": "AtlassianTeamId",
  "issueSourceId": 0,
  "planningStyle": "Scrum",
  "sprintLength": 2
}
```

<h3 id="add-atlassian-team-to-plan-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|planId|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the plan.|
|body|body|[AddAtlassianTeamRequest](#schemaaddatlassianteamrequest)|true|none|
|» capacity|body|number(double)|false|The capacity for the Atlassian team.|
|» id|body|string|true|The Atlassian team ID.|
|» issueSourceId|body|integer(int64)|false|The ID of the issue source for the Atlassian team.|
|» planningStyle|body|string|true|The planning style for the Atlassian team. This must be "Scrum" or "Kanban".|
|» sprintLength|body|integer(int64)|false|The sprint length for the Atlassian team.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» planningStyle|Scrum|
|» planningStyle|Kanban|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
null
```

## Create plan-only team

<a id="opIdcreatePlanOnlyTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/plans/plan/0/team/planonly \
  -X POST \

  -d '{
    "capacity": 200,
    "issueSourceId": 0,
    "memberAccountIds": [
      "member1AccountId",

    ],
    "name": "Team1",
    "planningStyle": "Scrum",
    "sprintLength": 2
  }'
```

`POST /rest/api/3/plans/plan/{planId}/team/planonly`

Creates a plan-only team and configures their planning settings.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "capacity": 200,
  "issueSourceId": 0,
  "memberAccountIds": [
    "member1AccountId",
    "member2AccountId"
  ],
  "name": "Team1",
  "planningStyle": "Scrum",

}
```

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-time-tracking">Time tracking</h1>

This resource represents time tracking and time tracking providers. Use it to get and set the time tracking provider, get and set the time tracking options, and disable time tracking.

## Get selected time tracking provider

<a id="opIdgetSelectedTimeTrackingImplementation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/configuration/timetracking \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/configuration/timetracking`

Returns the time tracking provider that is currently selected. Note that if time tracking is disabled, then a successful but empty response is returned.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** *Administer Jira* [global permission](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/x4dKLg).

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"{\"key\":\"Jira\",\"name\":\"JIRA provided time tracking\",\"url\":\"/example/config/url\"}"
```

> 204 Response

```json
null
```

<h1 id="the-jira-cloud-platform-rest-api-ui-modifications-apps">UI modifications (apps)</h1>

UI modifications is a feature available for **Forge apps only**. It enables Forge apps to control how selected Jira and Jira Service Management fields behave on the following views:

 *  Jira global issue create
 *  Jira issue view
 *  Jira issue transition
 *  Jira Service Management request portal create.

For example: hide specific fields, set them as required, etc.

## Get UI modifications

<a id="opIdgetUiModifications"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/uiModifications \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /rest/api/3/uiModifications`

Gets UI modifications. UI modifications can only be retrieved by Forge apps.

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** None.

The new `read:app-data:jira` OAuth scope is 100% optional now, and not using it won't break your app. However, we recommend adding it to your app's scope list because we will eventually make it mandatory.

|expand|query|string|false|Use expand to include additional information in the response. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `data` Returns UI modification data.<br> *  `contexts` Returns UI modification contexts.|
