Details of a request to bulk edit shareable entity.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|Allowed action for bulk edit shareable entity|
|changeOwnerDetails|object|false|none|The details of change owner action.|
|entityIds|[integer(int64)]|true|none|The id list of shareable entities to be changed.|
|extendAdminPermissions|boolean|false|none|Whether the actions are executed by users with Administer Jira global permission.|
|permissionDetails|object|false|none|The permission details to be changed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|action|changeOwner|
|action|changePermission|
|action|addPermission|
|action|removePermission|

|expand|[string]|false|none|Use [expand](#expansion) to include additional information about issues in the response. Note that, unlike the majority of instances where `expand` is specified, `expand` is defined as a list of values. The expand options are:<br><br> *  `renderedFields` Returns field values rendered in HTML format.<br> *  `names` Returns the display name of each field.<br> *  `schema` Returns the schema describing a field type.<br> *  `transitions` Returns all possible transitions for the issue.<br> *  `operations` Returns all possible operations for the issue.<br> *  `editmeta` Returns information about how each field can be edited.<br> *  `changelog` Returns a list of recent updates to an issue, sorted by date, starting from the most recent. This returns a maximum of 40 changelogs. If you require more, please refer to [Bulk fetch changelogs](#api-rest-api-3-changelog-bulkfetch-post).<br> *  `versionedRepresentations` Instead of `fields`, returns `versionedRepresentations` a JSON array containing each version of a field's value, with the highest numbered item representing the most recent version.<br><br>To request up to 1000 issues in a single call, do not include `changelog`, `editmeta`, `operations`, `renderedFields`, `transitions`, or `versionedRepresentations` in `expand`. Requests that include any of these can include at most 100 issues; larger requests are rejected with a 400 error.|
|fields|[string]|false|none|A list of fields to return for each issue, use it to retrieve a subset of fields. This parameter accepts a comma-separated list. Expand options include:<br><br> *  `*all` Returns all fields.<br> *  `*navigable` Returns navigable fields.<br> *  Any issue field, prefixed with a minus to exclude.<br><br>The default is `*navigable`.<br><br>Examples:<br><br> *  `summary,comment` Returns the summary and comments fields only.<br> *  `-description` Returns all navigable (default) fields except description.<br> *  `*all,-comment` Returns all fields except comments.<br><br>Multiple `fields` parameters can be included in a request.<br><br>Note: All navigable fields are returned by default. This differs from [GET issue](#api-rest-api-3-issue-issueIdOrKey-get) where the default is all fields.<br><br>To request up to 1000 issues in a single call, explicitly list the fields you need: at least one field must be a positive include (a request containing only exclusions is not eligible), the `*all` and `*navigable` wildcards and the default navigable field set are not eligible for the higher limit, no more than 100 fields may be listed, and none of the included fields returns multiple values (for example `comment`, `worklog`, or `attachment`). Requests that do not meet these conditions can include at most 100 issues; larger requests are rejected with a 400 error.|
|fieldsByKeys|boolean|false|none|Reference fields by their key (rather than ID). The default is `false`.|
|issueIdsOrKeys|[string]|true|none|An array of issue IDs or issue keys to fetch. You can mix issue IDs and keys in the same query. You can request up to 100 issues per call. Requests can include up to 1000 issues per call when they meet all of the conditions described for the `fields` and `expand` parameters. Requests that exceed the applicable limit are rejected with a 400 error.|
|properties|[string]|false|none|A list of issue property keys of issue properties to be included in the results. A maximum of 5 issue property keys can be specified.|

|created|string(date-time)|false|none|A timestamp of when the task was submitted.|

|processedAccessibleIssues|[integer(int64)]|false|none|List of issue IDs for which the operation was successful and that the user has permission to view.|
|progressPercent|integer(int64)|false|none|Progress of the task as a percentage.|
|started|string(date-time)|false|none|A timestamp of when the task was started.|
|status|string|false|none|The status of the task.|
|submittedBy|[User](#schemauser)|false|none|A user with details as permitted by the user's Atlassian Account privacy settings. However, be aware of these exceptions:<br><br> *  User record deleted from Atlassian: This occurs as the result of a right to be forgotten request. In this case, `displayName` provides an indication and other parameters have default values or are blank (for example, email is blank).<br> *  User record corrupted: This occurs as a results of events such as a server import and can only happen to deleted users. In this case, `accountId` returns *unknown* and all other parameters have fallback values.<br> *  User record unavailable: This usually occurs due to an internal service outage. In this case, all parameters have fallback values.|
|taskId|string|false|read-only|The ID of the task.|
|totalIssueCount|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of issues that the bulk operation was attempted on.|
|updated|string(date-time)|false|none|A timestamp of when the task progress was last updated.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|ENQUEUED|
|status|RUNNING|
|status|COMPLETE|
|status|FAILED|
|status|CANCEL_REQUESTED|
|status|CANCELLED|
|status|DEAD|

```json
{
```

```json
    {
      "contentItem": {
        "entityId": "summary",
        "entityType": "issuefieldvalue",
        "id": "10000"
      },

      "reason": "PII data",
      "redactionPosition": {
        "adfPointer": "/content/0/content/0/text",

    }

}
```

A comment.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|author|object|false|read-only|The ID of the user who created the comment.|
|body|object|false|none|The comment text in [Atlassian Document Format](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/apis/document/structure/).|
|created|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The date and time at which the comment was created.|
|id|string|false|read-only|The ID of the comment.|
|jsdAuthorCanSeeRequest|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the comment was added from an email sent by a person who is not part of the issue. See [Allow external emails to be added as comments on issues](https://support.atlassian.com/jira-service-management-cloud/docs/allow-external-emails-to-be-added-as-comments-on-issues/)for information on setting up this feature.|
|jsdPublic|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the comment is visible in Jira Service Desk. Defaults to true when comments are created in the Jira Cloud Platform. This includes when the site doesn't use Jira Service Desk or the project isn't a Jira Service Desk project and, therefore, there is no Jira Service Desk for the issue to be visible on. To create a comment with its visibility in Jira Service Desk set to false, use the Jira Service Desk REST API [Create request comment](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/service-desk/rest/#api-rest-servicedeskapi-request-issueIdOrKey-comment-post) operation.|
|properties|[[EntityProperty](#schemaentityproperty)]|false|none|A list of comment properties. Optional on create and update.|
|renderedBody|string|false|read-only|The rendered version of the comment.|
|self|string|false|read-only|The URL of the comment.|
|updateAuthor|object|false|read-only|The ID of the user who updated the comment last.|
|updated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The date and time at which the comment was updated last.|
|visibility|object|false|none|The group or role to which this comment is visible. Optional on create and update.|

Details about a component with a count of the issues it contains.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assignee|object|false|none|The details of the user associated with `assigneeType`, if any. See `realAssignee` for details of the user assigned to issues created with this component.|
|assigneeType|string|false|read-only|The nominal user type used to determine the assignee for issues created with this component. See `realAssigneeType` for details on how the type of the user, and hence the user, assigned to issues is determined. Takes the following values:<br><br> *  `PROJECT_LEAD` the assignee to any issues created with this component is nominally the lead for the project the component is in.<br> *  `COMPONENT_LEAD` the assignee to any issues created with this component is nominally the lead for the component.<br> *  `UNASSIGNED` an assignee is not set for issues created with this component.<br> *  `PROJECT_DEFAULT` the assignee to any issues created with this component is nominally the default assignee for the project that the component is in.|
|description|string|false|read-only|The description for the component.|
|id|string|false|read-only|The unique identifier for the component.|
|isAssigneeTypeValid|boolean|false|read-only|Whether a user is associated with `assigneeType`. For example, if the `assigneeType` is set to `COMPONENT_LEAD` but the component lead is not set, then `false` is returned.|
|issueCount|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Count of issues for the component.|
|lead|object|false|none|The user details for the component's lead user.|
|name|string|false|read-only|The name for the component.|
|project|string|false|read-only|The key of the project to which the component is assigned.|
|projectId|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Not used.|
|realAssignee|object|false|none|The user assigned to issues created with this component, when `assigneeType` does not identify a valid assignee.|
|realAssigneeType|string|false|read-only|The type of the assignee that is assigned to issues created with this component, when an assignee cannot be set from the `assigneeType`. For example, `assigneeType` is set to `COMPONENT_LEAD` but no component lead is set. This property is set to one of the following values:<br><br> *  `PROJECT_LEAD` when `assigneeType` is `PROJECT_LEAD` and the project lead has permission to be assigned issues in the project that the component is in.<br> *  `COMPONENT_LEAD` when `assignee`Type is `COMPONENT_LEAD` and the component lead has permission to be assigned issues in the project that the component is in.<br> *  `UNASSIGNED` when `assigneeType` is `UNASSIGNED` and Jira is configured to allow unassigned issues.<br> *  `PROJECT_DEFAULT` when none of the preceding cases are true.|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL for this count of the issues contained in the component.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|assigneeType|PROJECT_DEFAULT|
|assigneeType|COMPONENT_LEAD|
|assigneeType|PROJECT_LEAD|
|assigneeType|UNASSIGNED|
|realAssigneeType|PROJECT_DEFAULT|
|realAssigneeType|COMPONENT_LEAD|
|realAssigneeType|PROJECT_LEAD|
|realAssigneeType|UNASSIGNED|

<h2 id="tocS_CompoundClause">CompoundClause</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacompoundclause"></a>
<a id="schema_CompoundClause"></a>
<a id="tocScompoundclause"></a>
<a id="tocscompoundclause"></a>

```json
{
  "clauses": [
    {}
  ],
  "operator": "and"
}
```

A JQL query clause that consists of nested clauses. For example, `(labels in (urgent, blocker) OR lastCommentedBy = currentUser()). Note that, where nesting is not defined, the parser nests JQL clauses based on the operator precedence. For example, "A OR B AND C" is parsed as "(A OR B) AND C". See Setting the precedence of operators for more information about precedence in JQL queries.`

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clauses|[[JqlQueryClause](#schemajqlqueryclause)]|true|none|The list of nested clauses.|
|operator|string|true|none|The operator between the clauses.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|operator|and|
|operator|or|
|operator|not|

### Properties

|mappings|object|false|none|Instructions to migrate the priorities of issues.<br><br>`in` mappings are used to migrate the priorities of issues to priorities used within the priority scheme.<br><br>`out` mappings are used to migrate the priorities of issues to priorities not used within the priority scheme.<br><br> *  When **priorities** are **added** to the new priority scheme, no mapping needs to be provided as the new priorities are not used by any issues.<br> *  When **priorities** are **removed** from the new priority scheme, no mapping needs to be provided as the removed priorities are not used by any issues.<br> *  When **projects** are **added** to the priority scheme, the priorities of issues in those projects might need to be migrated to new priorities used by the priority scheme. This can occur when the current scheme does not use all the priorities in the project(s)' priority scheme(s).<br>    <br>     *  An `in` mapping must be provided for each of these priorities.<br> *  When **projects** are **removed** from the priority scheme, no mapping needs to be provided as the removed projects are not using the priorities of the new priority scheme.<br><br>For more information on `in` and `out` mappings, see the child properties documentation for the `PriorityMapping` object below.|
|name|string|true|write-only|The name of the priority scheme. Must be unique.|
|priorityIds|[integer(int64)]|true|write-only|The IDs of priorities in the scheme.|
|projectIds|[integer(int64)]|false|write-only|The IDs of projects that will use the priority scheme.|

<h2 id="tocS_CustomFieldDefinitionJsonBean">CustomFieldDefinitionJsonBean</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomfielddefinitionjsonbean"></a>
<a id="schema_CustomFieldDefinitionJsonBean"></a>
<a id="tocScustomfielddefinitionjsonbean"></a>
<a id="tocscustomfielddefinitionjsonbean"></a>

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "searcherKey": "com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:cascadingselectsearcher",
  "type": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|false|none|The description of the custom field, which is displayed in Jira.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the custom field, which is displayed in Jira. This is not the unique identifier.|
|searcherKey|string|false|none|The searcher defines the way the field is searched in Jira. For example, *com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:grouppickersearcher*.  <br>The search UI (basic search and JQL search) will display different operations and values for the field, based on the field searcher. You must specify a searcher that is valid for the field type, as listed below (abbreviated values shown):<br><br> *  `cascadingselect`: `cascadingselectsearcher`<br> *  `datepicker`: `daterange`<br> *  `datetime`: `datetimerange`<br> *  `float`: `exactnumber` or `numberrange`<br> *  `grouppicker`: `grouppickersearcher`<br> *  `importid`: `exactnumber` or `numberrange`<br> *  `labels`: `labelsearcher`<br> *  `multicheckboxes`: `multiselectsearcher`<br> *  `multigrouppicker`: `multiselectsearcher`<br> *  `multiselect`: `multiselectsearcher`<br> *  `multiuserpicker`: `userpickergroupsearcher`<br> *  `multiversion`: `versionsearcher`<br> *  `project`: `projectsearcher`<br> *  `radiobuttons`: `multiselectsearcher`<br> *  `readonlyfield`: `textsearcher`<br> *  `select`: `multiselectsearcher`<br> *  `textarea`: `textsearcher`<br> *  `textfield`: `textsearcher`<br> *  `url`: `exacttextsearcher`<br> *  `userpicker`: `userpickergroupsearcher`<br> *  `version`: `versionsearcher`<br><br>If no searcher is provided, the field isn't searchable. However, [Forge custom fields](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/modules/#jira-custom-field-type--beta-) have a searcher set automatically, so are always searchable.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the custom field. These built-in custom field types are available:<br><br> *  `cascadingselect`: Enables values to be selected from two levels of select lists (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:cascadingselect`)<br> *  `datepicker`: Stores a date using a picker control (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:datepicker`)<br> *  `datetime`: Stores a date with a time component (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:datetime`)<br> *  `float`: Stores and validates a numeric (floating point) input (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:float`)<br> *  `grouppicker`: Stores a user group using a picker control (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:grouppicker`)<br> *  `importid`: A read-only field that stores the ID the issue had in the system it was imported from (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:importid`)<br> *  `labels`: Stores labels (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:labels`)<br> *  `multicheckboxes`: Stores multiple values using checkboxes (value: ``)<br> *  `multigrouppicker`: Stores multiple user groups using a picker control (value: ``)<br> *  `multiselect`: Stores multiple values using a select list (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:multicheckboxes`)<br> *  `multiuserpicker`: Stores multiple users using a picker control (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:multigrouppicker`)<br> *  `multiversion`: Stores multiple versions from the versions available in a project using a picker control (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:multiversion`)<br> *  `project`: Stores a project from a list of projects that the user is permitted to view (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:project`)<br> *  `radiobuttons`: Stores a value using radio buttons (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:radiobuttons`)<br> *  `readonlyfield`: Stores a read-only text value, which can only be populated via the API (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:readonlyfield`)<br> *  `select`: Stores a value from a configurable list of options (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:select`)<br> *  `textarea`: Stores a long text string using a multiline text area (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:textarea`)<br> *  `textfield`: Stores a text string using a single-line text box (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:textfield`)<br> *  `url`: Stores a URL (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:url`)<br> *  `userpicker`: Stores a user using a picker control (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:userpicker`)<br> *  `version`: Stores a version using a picker control (value: `com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.customfieldtypes:version`)<br><br>To create a field based on a [Forge custom field type](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/modules/#jira-custom-field-type--beta-), use the ID of the Forge custom field type as the value. For example, `ari:cloud:ecosystem::extension/e62f20a2-4b61-4dbe-bfb9-9a88b5e3ac84/548c5df1-24aa-4f7c-bbbb-3038d947cb05/static/my-cf-type-key`.|

|---|---|

<h2 id="tocS_CustomFieldPayload">CustomFieldPayload</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomfieldpayload"></a>
<a id="schema_CustomFieldPayload"></a>
<a id="tocScustomfieldpayload"></a>
<a id="tocscustomfieldpayload"></a>

```json
{
  "cfType": "See https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issue-fields/#api-rest-api-3-field-post `type` for values",
  "description": "This is a custom field",
  "name": "My Custom Field",
  "onConflict": "FAIL",
  "pcri": "pcri:permissionScheme:id:10001",
  "scope": "GLOBAL",
  "searcherKey": "See https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issue-fields/#api-rest-api-3-field-post `searcherKey` for values"
}
```

Defines the payload for the custom field definitions. See https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issue-fields/\#api-rest-api-3-field-post

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cfType|string|false|none|The type of the custom field|
|description|string|false|none|The description of the custom field|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the custom field|
|onConflict|string|false|none|The strategy to use when there is a conflict with an existing custom field. FAIL - Fail execution, this always needs to be unique; USE - Use the existing entity and ignore new entity parameters|
|pcri|[ProjectCreateResourceIdentifier](#schemaprojectcreateresourceidentifier)|false|none|Every project-created entity has an ID that must be unique within the scope of the project creation. PCRI (Project Create Resource Identifier) is a standard format for creating IDs and references to other project entities. PCRI format is defined as follows: pcri:\[entityType\]:\[type\]:\[entityId\] entityType - the type of an entity, e.g. status, role, workflow type - PCRI type, either `id` - The ID of an entity that already exists in the target site, or `ref` - A unique reference to an entity that is being created entityId - entity identifier, if type is `id` - must be an existing entity ID that exists in the Jira site, if `ref` - must be unique across all entities in the scope of this project template creation|
|scope|string|false|none|Allows an overwrite to declare the new Custom Field to be created as a GLOBAL-scoped field. Leave this as empty or null to use the project's default scope.|
|searcherKey|string|false|none|The searcher key of the custom field|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|onConflict|FAIL|
|onConflict|USE|
|onConflict|NEW|
|scope|GLOBAL|
|scope|TEMPLATE|
|scope|PROJECT|


A list of issue IDs and the value to update a custom field to.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueIds|[integer(int64)]|true|write-only|The list of issue IDs.|
|value|object|true|none|The value for the custom field. The value must be compatible with the [custom field type](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/modules/jira-custom-field/#data-types) as follows:<br><br> *  `string` the value must be a string.<br> *  `number` the value must be a number.<br> *  `datetime` the value must be a string that represents a date in the ISO format or the simplified extended ISO format. For example, `"2023-01-18T12:00:00-03:00"` or `"2023-01-18T12:00:00.000Z"`. However, the milliseconds part is ignored.<br> *  `user` the value must be an object that contains the `accountId` field.<br> *  `group` the value must be an object that contains the group `name` or `groupId` field. Because group names can change, we recommend using `groupId`.<br><br>A list of appropriate values must be provided if the field is of the `list` [collection type](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/modules/jira-custom-field/#collection-types).|

The specific request object for creating a project with template.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|boardFeatures|[BoardFeaturesPayload](#schemaboardfeaturespayload)|false|none|Configuration of features for one or more boards. Replaces the deprecated features field on BoardPayload|
|boards|[BoardsPayload](#schemaboardspayload)|false|none|none|
|field|[FieldCapabilityPayload](#schemafieldcapabilitypayload)|false|none|Defines the payload for the fields, screens, screen schemes, issue type screen schemes, field layouts, and field layout schemes|
|issueType|[IssueTypeProjectCreatePayload](#schemaissuetypeprojectcreatepayload)|false|none|The payload for creating issue types in a project|
|notification|[NotificationSchemePayload](#schemanotificationschemepayload)|false|none|The payload for creating a notification scheme. The user has to supply the ID for the default notification scheme. For CMP this is provided in the project payload and should be left empty, for TMP it's provided using this payload|
|permissionScheme|[PermissionPayloadDTO](#schemapermissionpayloaddto)|false|none|The payload to create a permission scheme|
|project|[ProjectPayload](#schemaprojectpayload)|false|none|The payload for creating a project|
|role|[RolesCapabilityPayload](#schemarolescapabilitypayload)|false|none|none|
|scope|[ScopePayload](#schemascopepayload)|false|none|The payload for creating a scope. Defines if a project is team-managed project or company-managed project|
|security|[SecuritySchemePayload](#schemasecurityschemepayload)|false|none|The payload for creating a security scheme. See https://support.atlassian.com/jira-cloud-administration/docs/configure-issue-security-schemes/|
|workflow|[WorkflowCapabilityPayload](#schemaworkflowcapabilitypayload)|false|none|The payload for creating a workflows. See https://www.atlassian.com/software/jira/guides/workflows/overview\#what-is-a-jira-workflow|

Project Details

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accessLevel|string|false|none|The access level of the project. Only used by team-managed project|
|additionalProperties|object|false|none|Additional properties of the project|
|assigneeType|string|false|none|The default assignee when creating issues in the project|
|avatarId|integer(int64)|false|none|The ID of the project's avatar. Use the \[Get project avatars\](\#api-rest-api-3-project-projectIdOrKey-avatar-get) operation to list the available avatars in a project.|
|categoryId|integer(int64)|false|none|The ID of the project's category. A complete list of category IDs is found using the [Get all project categories](#api-rest-api-3-projectCategory-get) operation.|
|description|string|false|none|Brief description of the project|
|enableComponents|boolean|false|none|Whether components are enabled for the project. Only used by company-managed project|
|key|string|false|none|Project keys must be unique and start with an uppercase letter followed by one or more uppercase alphanumeric characters. The maximum length is 10 characters.|
|language|string|false|none|The default language for the project|
|leadAccountId|string|false|none|The account ID of the project lead. Either `lead` or `leadAccountId` must be set when creating a project. Cannot be provided with `lead`.|
|name|string|false|none|Name of the project|
|url|string|false|none|A link to information about this project, such as project documentation|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|accessLevel|open|
|accessLevel|limited|
|accessLevel|private|
|accessLevel|free|
|assigneeType|PROJECT_DEFAULT|
|assigneeType|COMPONENT_LEAD|
|assigneeType|PROJECT_LEAD|
|assigneeType|UNASSIGNED|

Details of a dashboard.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|automaticRefreshMs|integer(int32)|false|read-only|The automatic refresh interval for the dashboard in milliseconds.|
|description|string|false|none|none|
|editPermissions|[[SharePermission](#schemasharepermission)]|false|read-only|The details of any edit share permissions for the dashboard.|
|id|string|false|read-only|The ID of the dashboard.|
|isFavourite|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the dashboard is selected as a favorite by the user.|
|isWritable|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the current user has permission to edit the dashboard.|
|name|string|false|read-only|The name of the dashboard.|
|owner|object|false|read-only|The owner of the dashboard.|
|popularity|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The number of users who have this dashboard as a favorite.|
|rank|integer(int32)|false|read-only|The rank of this dashboard.|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL of these dashboard details.|
|sharePermissions|[[SharePermission](#schemasharepermission)]|false|read-only|The details of any view share permissions for the dashboard.|
|systemDashboard|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the current dashboard is system dashboard.|
|view|string|false|read-only|The URL of the dashboard.|

```json
  },
```

Details of the settings for a dashboard gadget.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|color|string|false|write-only|The color of the gadget. Should be one of `blue`, `red`, `yellow`, `green`, `cyan`, `purple`, `gray`, or `white`.|
|ignoreUriAndModuleKeyValidation|boolean|false|write-only|Whether to ignore the validation of module key and URI. For example, when a gadget is created that is a part of an application that isn't installed.|
|moduleKey|string|false|write-only|The module key of the gadget type. Can't be provided with `uri`.|
|position|object|false|none|The position of the gadget. When the gadget is placed into the position, other gadgets in the same column are moved down to accommodate it.|
|title|string|false|write-only|The title of the gadget.|
|uri|string|false|write-only|The URI of the gadget type. Can't be provided with `moduleKey`.|

See https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issue-type-screen-schemes/\#api-rest-api-3-issuetypescreenscheme-post|
|screenScheme|[[ScreenSchemePayload](#schemascreenschemepayload)]|false|none|The screen schemes See https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-screen-schemes/\#api-rest-api-3-screenscheme-post|

<h2 id="tocS_FieldChangedClause">FieldChangedClause</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafieldchangedclause"></a>
<a id="schema_FieldChangedClause"></a>
<a id="tocSfieldchangedclause"></a>
<a id="tocsfieldchangedclause"></a>

```json
{
  "field": {
    "encodedName": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "property": [
      {
        "entity": "issue",
        "key": "stats",
        "path": "comments.count",
        "type": "number"
      }
    ]
  },
  "operator": "changed",
  "predicates": [
    {
      "operand": {
        "encodedOperand": "string",
        "values": [
          {
            "encodedValue": "string",
            "value": "string"
          }
        ]
      },
      "operator": "before"
    }
  ]
}
```

A clause that asserts whether a field was changed. For example, `status CHANGED AFTER startOfMonth(-1M)`.See [CHANGED](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/dgiiLQ#Advancedsearching-operatorsreference-CHANGEDCHANGED) for more information about the CHANGED operator.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|field|[JqlQueryField](#schemajqlqueryfield)|true|none|A field used in a JQL query. See [Advanced searching - fields reference](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/dAiiLQ) for more information about fields in JQL queries.|
|operator|string|true|none|The operator applied to the field.|
|predicates|[[JqlQueryClauseTimePredicate](#schemajqlqueryclausetimepredicate)]|true|none|The list of time predicates.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|operator|changed|

<h2 id="tocS_FieldLayoutConfiguration">FieldLayoutConfiguration</h2>

<a id="schemafieldlayoutconfiguration"></a>

<a id="tocsfieldlayoutconfiguration"></a>

```json
{
  "field": true,
  "pcri": "pcri:permissionScheme:id:10001",
  "required": true
}
```

Defines the payload for the field layout configuration. See https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issue-field-configurations/\#api-rest-api-3-fieldconfiguration-post

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|field|boolean|false|none|Whether to show the field|
|pcri|[ProjectCreateResourceIdentifier](#schemaprojectcreateresourceidentifier)|false|none|Every project-created entity has an ID that must be unique within the scope of the project creation. PCRI (Project Create Resource Identifier) is a standard format for creating IDs and references to other project entities. PCRI format is defined as follows: pcri:\[entityType\]:\[type\]:\[entityId\] entityType - the type of an entity, e.g. status, role, workflow type - PCRI type, either `id` - The ID of an entity that already exists in the target site, or `ref` - A unique reference to an entity that is being created entityId - entity identifier, if type is `id` - must be an existing entity ID that exists in the Jira site, if `ref` - must be unique across all entities in the scope of this project template creation|
|required|boolean|false|none|Whether the field is required|

```json
{
  "configuration": [
    {
      "field": true,
      "pcri": "pcri:permissionScheme:id:10001",
      "required": true
    }
  ],
  "description": "This is a field layout",
  "name": "My Field Layout",
  "pcri": "pcri:permissionScheme:id:10001"
}
```

Defines the payload for the field layouts. See https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issue-field-configurations/\#api-group-issue-field-configurations" + fieldlayout is what users would see as "Field Configuration" in Jira's UI - https://support.atlassian.com/jira-cloud-administration/docs/manage-issue-field-configurations/

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|configuration|[[FieldLayoutConfiguration](#schemafieldlayoutconfiguration)]|false|none|The field layout configuration. See https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issue-field-configurations/\#api-rest-api-3-fieldconfiguration-post|
|description|string|false|none|The description of the field layout|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the field layout|
|pcri|[ProjectCreateResourceIdentifier](#schemaprojectcreateresourceidentifier)|false|none|Every project-created entity has an ID that must be unique within the scope of the project creation. PCRI (Project Create Resource Identifier) is a standard format for creating IDs and references to other project entities. PCRI format is defined as follows: pcri:\[entityType\]:\[type\]:\[entityId\] entityType - the type of an entity, e.g. status, role, workflow type - PCRI type, either `id` - The ID of an entity that already exists in the target site, or `ref` - A unique reference to an entity that is being created entityId - entity identifier, if type is `id` - must be an existing entity ID that exists in the Jira site, if `ref` - must be unique across all entities in the scope of this project template creation|

|description|string|false|none|The description of the field layout scheme|

|pcri|[ProjectCreateResourceIdentifier](#schemaprojectcreateresourceidentifier)|false|none|Every project-created entity has an ID that must be unique within the scope of the project creation. PCRI (Project Create Resource Identifier) is a standard format for creating IDs and references to other project entities. PCRI format is defined as follows: pcri:\[entityType\]:\[type\]:\[entityId\] entityType - the type of an entity, e.g. status, role, workflow type - PCRI type, either `id` - The ID of an entity that already exists in the target site, or `ref` - A unique reference to an entity that is being created entityId - entity identifier, if type is `id` - must be an existing entity ID that exists in the Jira site, if `ref` - must be unique across all entities in the scope of this project template creation|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|onConflict|USE|
|onConflict|NEW|

The default parameters to apply to the field across all work types in the specified schemes, may be null if only work type-specific updates are needed

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|false|none|The custom description for the field, null to preserve current description|
|isRequired|boolean|false|none|Whether the field is required, null to preserve current requirement setting|
|rendererType|string|false|none|The renderer type for the field, null to preserve current renderer type|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|rendererType|jira-text-renderer|
|rendererType|atlassian-wiki-renderer|

The list of work type-specific parameter overrides, may be empty if only default parameters are being updated

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|false|none|The custom description for the field for this work type, null to use default or preserve current|
|isRequired|boolean|false|none|Whether the field is required for this work type, null to use default or preserve current|
|rendererType|string|false|none|The renderer type for the field for this work type, null to use default or preserve current|
|workTypeId|integer(int64)|false|none|The ID of the work type (issue type) for which these parameters apply|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|rendererType|jira-text-renderer|
|rendererType|atlassian-wiki-renderer|

Details about a filter.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|approximateLastUsed|string(date-time)|false|read-only|\[Experimental\] Approximate last used time. Returns the date and time when the filter was last used. Returns `null` if the filter hasn't been used after tracking was enabled. For performance reasons, timestamps aren't updated in real time and therefore may not be exactly accurate.|
|description|string|false|none|A description of the filter.|
|editPermissions|[[SharePermission](#schemasharepermission)]|false|none|The groups and projects that can edit the filter.|
|favourite|boolean|false|none|Whether the filter is selected as a favorite.|
|favouritedCount|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The count of how many users have selected this filter as a favorite, including the filter owner.|
|id|string|false|read-only|The unique identifier for the filter.|
|jql|string|false|none|The JQL query for the filter. For example, *project = SSP AND issuetype = Bug*.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the filter. Must be unique.|
|owner|object|false|read-only|The user who owns the filter. This is defaulted to the creator of the filter, however Jira administrators can change the owner of a shared filter in the admin settings.|
|searchUrl|string(uri)|false|read-only|A URL to view the filter results in Jira, using the [Search for issues using JQL](#api-rest-api-3-filter-search-get) operation with the filter's JQL string to return the filter results. For example, *https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/search?jql=project+%3D+SSP+AND+issuetype+%3D+Bug*.|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL of the filter.|
|sharePermissions|[[SharePermission](#schemasharepermission)]|false|none|The groups and projects that the filter is shared with.|
|sharedUsers|object|false|read-only|A paginated list of the users that the filter is shared with. This includes users that are members of the groups or can browse the projects that the filter is shared with.|
|subscriptions|object|false|read-only|A paginated list of the users that are subscribed to the filter.|
|viewUrl|string(uri)|false|read-only|A URL to view the filter results in Jira, using the ID of the filter. For example, *https://your-domain.atlassian.net/issues/?filter=10100*.|

Details of a filter.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|approximateLastUsed|string(date-time)|false|read-only|\[Experimental\] Approximate last used time. Returns the date and time when the filter was last used. Returns `null` if the filter hasn't been used after tracking was enabled. For performance reasons, timestamps aren't updated in real time and therefore may not be exactly accurate.|
|description|string|false|none|The description of the filter.|
|editPermissions|[[SharePermission](#schemasharepermission)]|false|none|The groups and projects that can edit the filter. This can be specified when updating a filter, but not when creating a filter.|
|expand|string|false|read-only|Expand options that include additional filter details in the response.|
|favourite|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the filter is selected as a favorite by any users, not including the filter owner.|
|favouritedCount|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The count of how many users have selected this filter as a favorite, including the filter owner.|
|id|string|false|read-only|The unique identifier for the filter.|
|jql|string|false|read-only|The JQL query for the filter. For example, *project = SSP AND issuetype = Bug*.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the filter.|
|owner|object|false|read-only|The user who owns the filter. Defaults to the creator of the filter, however, Jira administrators can change the owner of a shared filter in the admin settings.|
|searchUrl|string(uri)|false|read-only|A URL to view the filter results in Jira, using the [Search for issues using JQL](#api-rest-api-3-filter-search-get) operation with the filter's JQL string to return the filter results. For example, *https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/search?jql=project+%3D+SSP+AND+issuetype+%3D+Bug*.|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL of the filter.|
|sharePermissions|[[SharePermission](#schemasharepermission)]|false|none|The groups and projects that the filter is shared with. This can be specified when updating a filter, but not when creating a filter.|
|subscriptions|[[FilterSubscription](#schemafiltersubscription)]|false|read-only|The users that are subscribed to the filter.|
|viewUrl|string(uri)|false|read-only|A URL to view the filter results in Jira, using the ID of the filter. For example, *https://your-domain.atlassian.net/issues/?filter=10100*.|

The pin status of an issue panel (added by a Forge app) for a single project.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|string|false|none|The reason the pin status could not be read for the project. Null if the pin status was read successfully.|
|pinned|boolean|false|none|Whether the issue panel is currently pinned to the project.|
|pinnedAt|integer(int64)|false|none|The time the issue panel was pinned to the project, in epoch milliseconds.|
|projectIdOrKey|string|false|none|The project ID or key supplied in the request.|

If not set, the status icon doesn't display a tooltip in Jira.<br> *  For the remote object icon it is used in conjunction with the application name to display a tooltip for the link's icon. The tooltip takes the format "\[application name\] icon title". Blank itemsare excluded from the tooltip title. If both items are blank, the icon tooltop displays as "Web Link".|
|url16x16|string|false|none|The URL of an icon that displays at 16x16 pixel in Jira.|

Issue Bulk Edit Payload

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|editedFieldsInput|object|true|none|An object that defines the values to be updated in specified fields of an issue. The structure and content of this parameter vary depending on the type of field being edited. Although the order is not significant, ensure that field IDs align with those in selectedActions.|
|selectedActions|[string]|true|write-only|List of all the field IDs that are to be bulk edited. Each field ID in this list corresponds to a specific attribute of an issue that is set to be modified in the bulk edit operation. The relevant field ID can be obtained by calling the Bulk Edit Get Fields REST API (documentation available on this page itself).|
|selectedIssueIdsOrKeys|[string]|true|write-only|List of issue IDs or keys which are to be bulk edited. These IDs or keys can be from different projects and issue types.|
|sendBulkNotification|boolean \| null|false|write-only|A boolean value that indicates whether to send a bulk change notification when the issues are being edited.<br><br>If `true`, dispatches a bulk notification email to users about the updates.|

Issue Bulk Move Payload

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sendBulkNotification|boolean \| null|false|write-only|A boolean value that indicates whether to send a bulk change notification when the issues are being moved.<br><br>If `true`, dispatches a bulk notification email to users about the updates.|
|targetToSourcesMapping|object|false|none|An object representing the mapping of issues and data related to destination entities, like fields and statuses, that are required during a bulk move.<br><br>The key is a string that is created by concatenating the following three entities in order, separated by commas. The format is `<project ID or key>,<issueType ID>,<parent ID or key>`. It should be unique across mappings provided in the payload. If you provide multiple mappings for the same key, only one will be processed. However, the operation won't fail, so the error may be hard to track down.<br><br> *  ***Destination project*** (Required): ID or key of the project to which the issues are being moved.<br> *  ***Destination issueType*** (Required): ID of the issueType to which the issues are being moved.<br> *  ***Destination parent ID or key*** (Optional): ID or key of the issue which will become the parent of the issues being moved. Only required when the destination issueType is a subtask.|

|itemKey|[ProjectCreateResourceIdentifier](#schemaprojectcreateresourceidentifier)|false|none|Every project-created entity has an ID that must be unique within the scope of the project creation. PCRI (Project Create Resource Identifier) is a standard format for creating IDs and references to other project entities. PCRI format is defined as follows: pcri:\[entityType\]:\[type\]:\[entityId\] entityType - the type of an entity, e.g. status, role, workflow type - PCRI type, either `id` - The ID of an entity that already exists in the target site, or `ref` - A unique reference to an entity that is being created entityId - entity identifier, if type is `id` - must be an existing entity ID that exists in the Jira site, if `ref` - must be unique across all entities in the scope of this project template creation|
|properties|object|false|none|Additional properties for this item. This field is only used when the type is FIELD.|
|sectionType|string|false|none|The item section type|
|type|string|false|none|The item type. Currently only support FIELD|

|sectionType|primaryContext|
|sectionType|secondaryContext|

<h2 id="tocS_IssueLinkType">IssueLinkType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaissuelinktype"></a>
<a id="schema_IssueLinkType"></a>
<a id="tocSissuelinktype"></a>
<a id="tocsissuelinktype"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "inward": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "outward": "string",
  "self": "http://example.com"
}
```

This object is used as follows:

 *  In the [ issueLink](#api-rest-api-3-issueLink-post) resource it defines and reports on the type of link between the issues. Find a list of issue link types with [Get issue link types](#api-rest-api-3-issueLinkType-get).
 *  In the [ issueLinkType](#api-rest-api-3-issueLinkType-post) resource it defines and reports on issue link types.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|The ID of the issue link type and is used as follows:<br><br> *  In the [ issueLink](#api-rest-api-3-issueLink-post) resource it is the type of issue link. Required on create when `name` isn't provided. Otherwise, read only.<br> *  In the [ issueLinkType](#api-rest-api-3-issueLinkType-post) resource it is read only.|
|inward|string|false|none|The description of the issue link type inward link and is used as follows:<br><br> *  In the [ issueLink](#api-rest-api-3-issueLink-post) resource it is read only.<br> *  In the [ issueLinkType](#api-rest-api-3-issueLinkType-post) resource it is required on create and optional on update. Otherwise, read only.|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the issue link type and is used as follows:<br><br> *  In the [ issueLink](#api-rest-api-3-issueLink-post) resource it is the type of issue link. Required on create when `id` isn't provided. Otherwise, read only.<br> *  In the [ issueLinkType](#api-rest-api-3-issueLinkType-post) resource it is required on create and optional on update. Otherwise, read only.|
|outward|string|false|none|The description of the issue link type outward link and is used as follows:<br><br> *  In the [ issueLink](#api-rest-api-3-issueLink-post) resource it is read only.<br> *  In the [ issueLinkType](#api-rest-api-3-issueLinkType-post) resource it is required on create and optional on update. Otherwise, read only.|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL of the issue link type. Read only.|

PCRI (Project Create Resource Identifier) is a standard format for creating IDs and references to other project entities. PCRI format is defined as follows: pcri:\[entityType\]:\[type\]:\[entityId\] entityType - the type of an entity, e.g. status, role, workflow type - PCRI type, either `id` - The ID of an entity that already exists in the target site, or `ref` - A unique reference to an entity that is being created entityId - entity identifier, if type is `id` - must be an existing entity ID that exists in the Jira site, if `ref` - must be unique across all entities in the scope of this project template creation|

The result of evaluating a Jira expression.This bean will be replacing `JiraExpressionResultBean` bean as part of new evaluate endpoint

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|meta|object|false|none|Contains various characteristics of the performed expression evaluation.|
|value|object|true|none|The value of the evaluated expression. It may be a primitive JSON value or a Jira REST API object. (Some expressions do not produce any meaningful results—for example, an expression that returns a lambda function—if that's the case a simple string representation is returned. These string representations should not be relied upon and may change without notice.)|

<h2 id="tocS_JexpEvaluateCtxJqlIssues">JexpEvaluateCtxJqlIssues</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemajexpevaluatectxjqlissues"></a>
<a id="schema_JexpEvaluateCtxJqlIssues"></a>
<a id="tocSjexpevaluatectxjqlissues"></a>
<a id="tocsjexpevaluatectxjqlissues"></a>

```json
{
  "maxResults": 0,
  "nextPageToken": "string",
  "query": "string"
}
```

The JQL specifying the issues available in the evaluated Jira expression under the `issues` context variable. Not all issues returned by the JQL query are loaded, only those described by the `nextPageToken` and `maxResults` properties. This bean will be replacing JexpJqlIssues bean as part of new `evaluate` endpoint

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|maxResults|integer(int32)|false|none|The maximum number of issues to return from the JQL query. max results value considered may be lower than the number specific here.|
|nextPageToken|string|false|none|The token for a page to fetch that is not the first page. The first page has a `nextPageToken` of `null`. Use the `nextPageToken` to fetch the next page of issues.|
|query|string|false|none|The JQL query, required to be bounded. Additionally, `orderBy` clause can contain a maximum of 7 fields|

<h2 id="tocS_JexpJqlIssues">JexpJqlIssues</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemajexpjqlissues"></a>
<a id="schema_JexpJqlIssues"></a>
<a id="tocSjexpjqlissues"></a>
<a id="tocsjexpjqlissues"></a>

```json
{
  "maxResults": 0,
  "query": "string",
  "startAt": 0,
  "validation": "strict"
}
```

The JQL specifying the issues available in the evaluated Jira expression under the `issues` context variable. Not all issues returned by the JQL query are loaded, only those described by the `startAt` and `maxResults` properties. To determine whether it is necessary to iterate to ensure all the issues returned by the JQL query are evaluated, inspect `meta.issues.jql.count` in the response.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|maxResults|integer(int32)|false|none|The maximum number of issues to return from the JQL query. Inspect `meta.issues.jql.maxResults` in the response to ensure the maximum value has not been exceeded.|
|query|string|false|none|The JQL query.|
|startAt|integer(int64)|false|none|The index of the first issue to return from the JQL query.|
|validation|string|false|none|Determines how to validate the JQL query and treat the validation results.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|validation|strict|
|validation|warn|
|validation|none|

<h2 id="tocS_JiraExpressionAnalysis">JiraExpressionAnalysis</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemajiraexpressionanalysis"></a>
<a id="schema_JiraExpressionAnalysis"></a>
<a id="tocSjiraexpressionanalysis"></a>
<a id="tocsjiraexpressionanalysis"></a>

```json
{
  "complexity": {
    "expensiveOperations": "string",
    "variables": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  },
  "errors": [
    {
      "column": 0,
      "expression": "string",
      "line": 0,
      "message": "!, -, typeof, (, IDENTIFIER, null, true, false, NUMBER, STRING, TEMPLATE_LITERAL, new, [ or { expected, > encountered.",
      "type": "syntax"
    }
  ],
  "expression": "string",
  "type": "string",
  "valid": true
}
```

Details about the analysed Jira expression.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|complexity|[JiraExpressionComplexity](#schemajiraexpressioncomplexity)|false|none|Details about the complexity of the analysed Jira expression.|
|errors|[[JiraExpressionValidationError](#schemajiraexpressionvalidationerror)]|false|none|A list of validation errors. Not included if the expression is valid.|
|expression|string|true|none|The analysed expression.|
|type|string|false|none|EXPERIMENTAL. The inferred type of the expression.|
|valid|boolean|true|none|Whether the expression is valid and the interpreter will evaluate it. Note that the expression may fail at runtime (for example, if it executes too many expensive operations).|

<h2 id="tocS_JiraExpressionComplexity">JiraExpressionComplexity</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemajiraexpressioncomplexity"></a>
<a id="schema_JiraExpressionComplexity"></a>
<a id="tocSjiraexpressioncomplexity"></a>
<a id="tocsjiraexpressioncomplexity"></a>

```json
{
  "expensiveOperations": "string",
  "variables": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  }
}
```

Details about the complexity of the analysed Jira expression.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expensiveOperations|string|true|none|Information that can be used to determine how many [expensive operations](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/jira-expressions/#expensive-operations) the evaluation of the expression will perform. This information may be a formula or number. For example:<br><br> *  `issues.map(i => i.comments)` performs as many expensive operations as there are issues on the issues list. So this parameter returns `N`, where `N` is the size of issue list.<br> *  `new Issue(10010).comments` gets comments for one issue, so its complexity is `2` (`1` to retrieve issue 10010 from the database plus `1` to get its comments).|
|variables|object|false|none|Variables used in the formula, mapped to the parts of the expression they refer to.|

<h2 id="tocS_JiraExpressionEvalContextBean">JiraExpressionEvalContextBean</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemajiraexpressionevalcontextbean"></a>
<a id="schema_JiraExpressionEvalContextBean"></a>
<a id="tocSjiraexpressionevalcontextbean"></a>
<a id="tocsjiraexpressionevalcontextbean"></a>

```json
{
  "board": 0,
  "custom": [
    {
      "accountId": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ],
  "customerRequest": 0,
  "issue": {
    "id": 0,
    "key": "string"
  },
  "issues": {
    "jql": {
      "maxResults": 0,
      "query": "string",
      "startAt": 0,
      "validation": "strict"
    }
  },
  "project": {
    "id": 0,
    "key": "string"
  },
  "serviceDesk": 0,
  "sprint": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|board|integer(int64)|false|none|The ID of the board that is available under the `board` variable when evaluating the expression.|
|custom|[[CustomContextVariable](#schemacustomcontextvariable)]|false|none|Custom context variables and their types. These variable types are available for use in a custom context:<br><br> *  `user`: A [user](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/jira-expressions-type-reference#user) specified as an Atlassian account ID.<br> *  `issue`: An [issue](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/jira-expressions-type-reference#issue) specified by ID or key. All the fields of the issue object are available in the Jira expression.<br> *  `json`: A JSON object containing custom content.<br> *  `list`: A JSON list of `user`, `issue`, or `json` variable types.|
|customerRequest|integer(int64)|false|none|The ID of the customer request that is available under the `customerRequest` variable when evaluating the expression. This is the same as the ID of the underlying Jira issue, but the customer request context variable will have a different type.|
|issue|object|false|none|The issue that is available under the `issue` variable when evaluating the expression.|
|issues|object|false|none|The collection of issues that is available under the `issues` variable when evaluating the expression.|
|project|object|false|none|The project that is available under the `project` variable when evaluating the expression.|
|serviceDesk|integer(int64)|false|none|The ID of the service desk that is available under the `serviceDesk` variable when evaluating the expression.|
|sprint|integer(int64)|false|none|The ID of the sprint that is available under the `sprint` variable when evaluating the expression.|

<h2 id="tocS_JqlQueryClause">JqlQueryClause</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

```json
    {}
  ],
  "operator": "and"
}
```

A JQL query clause.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[CompoundClause](#schemacompoundclause)|false|none|A JQL query clause that consists of nested clauses. For example, `(labels in (urgent, blocker) OR lastCommentedBy = currentUser()). Note that, where nesting is not defined, the parser nests JQL clauses based on the operator precedence. For example, "A OR B AND C" is parsed as "(A OR B) AND C". See Setting the precedence of operators for more information about precedence in JQL queries.`|
|*anyOf*|[FieldValueClause](#schemafieldvalueclause)|false|none|A clause that asserts the current value of a field. For example, `summary ~ test`.|
|*anyOf*|[FieldWasClause](#schemafieldwasclause)|false|none|A clause that asserts a previous value of a field. For example, `status WAS "Resolved" BY currentUser() BEFORE "2019/02/02"`. See [WAS](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/dgiiLQ#Advancedsearching-operatorsreference-WASWAS) for more information about the WAS operator.|
|*anyOf*|[FieldChangedClause](#schemafieldchangedclause)|false|none|A clause that asserts whether a field was changed. For example, `status CHANGED AFTER startOfMonth(-1M)`.See [CHANGED](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/dgiiLQ#Advancedsearching-operatorsreference-CHANGEDCHANGED) for more information about the CHANGED operator.|

<h2 id="tocS_MappingsByIssueTypeOverride">MappingsByIssueTypeOverride</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamappingsbyissuetypeoverride"></a>
<a id="schema_MappingsByIssueTypeOverride"></a>
<a id="tocSmappingsbyissuetypeoverride"></a>
<a id="tocsmappingsbyissuetypeoverride"></a>

```json
{
  "issueTypeId": "string",
  "statusMappings": [
    {
      "newStatusId": "string",
      "oldStatusId": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

The mappings for migrating issues from old statuses to new statuses when switching from one workflow scheme to another. This field is required if any statuses in the current project's workflows would no longer exist in the target workflow scheme. Each mapping defines how to update issues from an old status to the corresponding new status in the issue’s new workflow.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issueTypeId|string|false|none|none|
|statusMappings|[[WorkflowAssociationStatusMapping](#schemaworkflowassociationstatusmapping)]|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_MappingsByWorkflow">MappingsByWorkflow</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamappingsbyworkflow"></a>
<a id="schema_MappingsByWorkflow"></a>
<a id="tocSmappingsbyworkflow"></a>
<a id="tocsmappingsbyworkflow"></a>

```json
{
  "newWorkflowId": "string",
  "oldWorkflowId": "string",
  "statusMappings": [
    {
      "newStatusId": "string",
      "oldStatusId": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

The status mappings by workflows. Status mappings are required when the new workflow for an issue type doesn't contain all statuses that the old workflow has. Status mappings can be provided by a combination of `statusMappingsByWorkflows` and `statusMappingsByIssueTypeOverride`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|newWorkflowId|string|true|none|The ID of the new workflow.|
|oldWorkflowId|string|true|none|The ID of the old workflow.|
|statusMappings|[[WorkflowAssociationStatusMapping](#schemaworkflowassociationstatusmapping)]|true|none|The list of status mappings.|

<h2 id="tocS_MultipleCustomFieldValuesUpdate">MultipleCustomFieldValuesUpdate</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamultiplecustomfieldvaluesupdate"></a>
<a id="schema_MultipleCustomFieldValuesUpdate"></a>
<a id="tocSmultiplecustomfieldvaluesupdate"></a>
<a id="tocsmultiplecustomfieldvaluesupdate"></a>

```json
{
  "customField": "string",
  "issueIds": [
    0
  ],
  "value": null
}
```

A custom field and its new value with a list of issue to update.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customField|string|true|write-only|The ID or key of the custom field. For example, `customfield_10010`.|
|issueIds|[integer(int64)]|true|write-only|The list of issue IDs.|
|value|object|true|none|The value for the custom field. The value must be compatible with the [custom field type](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/modules/jira-custom-field/#data-types) as follows:<br><br> *  `string` the value must be a string.<br> *  `number` the value must be a number.<br> *  `datetime` the value must be a string that represents a date in the ISO format or the simplified extended ISO format. For example, `"2023-01-18T12:00:00-03:00"` or `"2023-01-18T12:00:00.000Z"`. However, the milliseconds part is ignored.<br> *  `user` the value must be an object that contains the `accountId` field.<br> *  `group` the value must be an object that contains the group `name` or `groupId` field. Because group names can change, we recommend using `groupId`.<br><br>A list of appropriate values must be provided if the field is of the `list` [collection type](https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/manifest-reference/modules/jira-custom-field/#collection-types).|

|password|string|false|none|This property is no longer available. If the user has an Atlassian account, their password is not changed. If the user does not have an Atlassian account, they are sent an email asking them set up an account.|
|products|[string]|true|none|Products the new user has access to. Valid products are: jira-core, jira-servicedesk, jira-product-discovery, jira-software. To create a user without product access, set this field to be an empty array.|
|self|string|false|read-only|The URL of the user.|

<h2 id="tocS_NotificationSchemePayload">NotificationSchemePayload</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanotificationschemepayload"></a>
<a id="schema_NotificationSchemePayload"></a>
<a id="tocSnotificationschemepayload"></a>
<a id="tocsnotificationschemepayload"></a>

```json
"CMP:  \"project\": {\n                 \"pcri\": \"pcri:project:ref:new-project1\",\n                 \"notificationSchemeId\": \"pcri:notificationScheme:id:10000\",\n                 ...\n              }\nTMP: \"notification\": {\n       \"pcri\": \"pcri:notificationScheme:ref:notification1\",\n       \"name\": \"Simplified Notification Scheme\",\n       \"notificationSchemeEvents\": [\n         {\n           \"event\": {\n             \"id\": \"1\"\n           },\n           \"notifications\": [\n             {\n               \"notificationType\": \"CurrentAssignee\"\n             },\n             {\n               \"notificationType\": \"Reporter\"\n             },\n             {\n               \"notificationType\": \"AllWatchers\"\n             }\n           ]\n         },\n         {\n           \"event\": {\n             \"id\": \"2\"\n           },\n           \"notifications\": [\n             {\n               \"notificationType\": \"CurrentAssignee\"\n             },\n             {\n               \"notificationType\": \"Reporter\"\n             },\n             {\n               \"notificationType\": \"AllWatchers\"\n             }\n           ]\n         },...\n       ]\n     }\n"
```

The payload for creating a notification scheme. The user has to supply the ID for the default notification scheme. For CMP this is provided in the project payload and should be left empty, for TMP it's provided using this payload

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|false|none|The description of the notification scheme|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the notification scheme|
|notificationSchemeEvents|[[NotificationSchemeEventPayload](#schemanotificationschemeeventpayload)]|false|none|The events and notifications for the notification scheme|
|onConflict|string|false|none|The strategy to use when there is a conflict with an existing entity|
|pcri|[ProjectCreateResourceIdentifier](#schemaprojectcreateresourceidentifier)|false|none|Every project-created entity has an ID that must be unique within the scope of the project creation. PCRI (Project Create Resource Identifier) is a standard format for creating IDs and references to other project entities. PCRI format is defined as follows: pcri:\[entityType\]:\[type\]:\[entityId\] entityType - the type of an entity, e.g. status, role, workflow type - PCRI type, either `id` - The ID of an entity that already exists in the target site, or `ref` - A unique reference to an entity that is being created entityId - entity identifier, if type is `id` - must be an existing entity ID that exists in the Jira site, if `ref` - must be unique across all entities in the scope of this project template creation|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|onConflict|FAIL|
|onConflict|USE|
|onConflict|NEW|

|position|Last|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|startAt|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The index of the first item returned.|
|total|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The number of items returned.|
|values|[[Dashboard](#schemadashboard)]|false|read-only|The list of items.|

A page of items.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|isLast|boolean|false|read-only|Whether this is the last page.|
|maxResults|integer(int32)|false|read-only|The maximum number of items that could be returned.|
|nextPage|string(uri)|false|read-only|If there is another page of results, the URL of the next page.|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL of the page.|
|startAt|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The index of the first item returned.|
|total|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The number of items returned.|
|values|[[FilterDetails](#schemafilterdetails)]|false|read-only|The list of items.|

Details about a permission granted to a user or group.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|holder|object|false|none|The user or group being granted the permission. It consists of a `type`, a type-dependent `parameter` and a type-dependent `value`. See [Holder object](../api-group-permission-schemes/#holder-object) in *Get all permission schemes* for more information.|
|id|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The ID of the permission granted details.|
|permission|string|false|none|The permission to grant. This permission can be one of the built-in permissions or a custom permission added by an app. See [Built-in permissions](../api-group-permission-schemes/#built-in-permissions) in *Get all permission schemes* for more information about the built-in permissions. See the [project permission](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/modules/project-permission/) and [global permission](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/modules/global-permission/) module documentation for more information about custom permissions.|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL of the permission granted details.|

The payload to create a permission scheme

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|addAddonRole|boolean|false|none|Configuration to generate addon role. Default is false if null. Only applies to GLOBAL-scoped permission scheme|
|description|string|false|none|The description of the permission scheme|
|grants|[[PermissionGrantDTO](#schemapermissiongrantdto)]|false|none|List of permission grants|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the permission scheme|
|onConflict|string|false|none|The strategy to use when there is a conflict with an existing permission scheme. FAIL - Fail execution, this always needs to be unique; USE - Use the existing entity and ignore new entity parameters; NEW - If the entity exist, try and create a new one with a different name|
|pcri|[ProjectCreateResourceIdentifier](#schemaprojectcreateresourceidentifier)|false|none|Every project-created entity has an ID that must be unique within the scope of the project creation. PCRI (Project Create Resource Identifier) is a standard format for creating IDs and references to other project entities. PCRI format is defined as follows: pcri:\[entityType\]:\[type\]:\[entityId\] entityType - the type of an entity, e.g. status, role, workflow type - PCRI type, either `id` - The ID of an entity that already exists in the target site, or `ref` - A unique reference to an entity that is being created entityId - entity identifier, if type is `id` - must be an existing entity ID that exists in the Jira site, if `ref` - must be unique across all entities in the scope of this project template creation|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|onConflict|FAIL|
|onConflict|USE|
|onConflict|NEW|

```json
    "property2": 0
  }
}
```

Mapping of issue priorities for changes in priority schemes.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|in|object|false|write-only|The mapping of priorities for issues being migrated **into** this priority scheme. Key is the old priority ID, value is the new priority ID (must exist in this priority scheme).<br><br>E.g. The current priority scheme has priority ID `10001`. Issues with priority ID `10000` are being migrated into this priority scheme will need mapping to new priorities. The `in` mapping would be `{"10000": 10001}`.|
|out|object|false|write-only|The mapping of priorities for issues being migrated **out of** this priority scheme. Key is the old priority ID (must exist in this priority scheme), value is the new priority ID (must exist in the default priority scheme). Required for updating an existing priority scheme. Not used when creating a new priority scheme.<br><br>E.g. The current priority scheme has priority ID `10001`. Issues with priority ID `10001` are being migrated out of this priority scheme will need mapping to new priorities. The `out` mapping would be `{"10001": 10000}`.|

Details about a project.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|archived|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the project is archived.|
|archivedBy|object|false|read-only|The user who archived the project.|
|archivedDate|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The date when the project was archived.|
|assigneeType|string|false|read-only|The default assignee when creating issues for this project.|
|avatarUrls|object|false|read-only|The URLs of the project's avatars.|
|components|[[ProjectComponent](#schemaprojectcomponent)]|false|read-only|List of the components contained in the project.|
|deleted|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the project is marked as deleted.|
|deletedBy|object|false|read-only|The user who marked the project as deleted.|
|deletedDate|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The date when the project was marked as deleted.|
|description|string|false|read-only|A brief description of the project.|
|email|string|false|none|An email address associated with the project.|
|expand|string|false|read-only|Expand options that include additional project details in the response.|
|favourite|boolean|false|none|Whether the project is selected as a favorite.|
|id|string|false|none|The ID of the project.|
|insight|object|false|read-only|Insights about the project.|
|isPrivate|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the project is private from the user's perspective. This means the user can't see the project or any associated issues.|
|issueTypeHierarchy|object|false|read-only|The issue type hierarchy for the project.|
|issueTypes|[[IssueTypeDetails](#schemaissuetypedetails)]|false|read-only|List of the issue types available in the project.|
|key|string|false|read-only|The key of the project.|
|landingPageInfo|object|false|read-only|The project landing page info.|
|lead|object|false|read-only|The username of the project lead.|
|name|string|false|read-only|The name of the project.|
|permissions|object|false|read-only|User permissions on the project|
|projectCategory|object|false|read-only|The category the project belongs to.|
|projectTypeKey|string|false|read-only|The [project type](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/GwiiLQ#Jiraapplicationsoverview-Productfeaturesandprojecttypes) of the project.|
|properties|object|false|read-only|Map of project properties. Only the properties named in the request's properties query parameter are returned, so this is an empty object when that parameter is omitted.|
|retentionTillDate|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The date when the project is deleted permanently.|
|roles|object|false|read-only|The name and self URL for each role defined in the project. For more information, see [Create project role](#api-rest-api-3-role-post).|
|self|string(uri)|false|read-only|The URL of the project details.|
|simplified|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the project is simplified.|
|style|string|false|read-only|The type of the project.|
|url|string|false|read-only|A link to information about this project, such as project documentation.|
|uuid|string(uuid)|false|read-only|Unique ID for next-gen projects.|
|versions|[[Version](#schemaversion)]|false|read-only|The versions defined in the project. For more information, see [Create version](#api-rest-api-3-version-post).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|assigneeType|PROJECT_LEAD|
|assigneeType|UNASSIGNED|
|projectTypeKey|software|
|projectTypeKey|service_desk|
|projectTypeKey|business|
|projectTypeKey|product_discovery|
|style|classic|
|style|next-gen|
